chapters.title: 第12章
chapters.en:
Rocks began to dance on the ground just then, and the villagers panicked. It was the second time in one night that their world had been shaken.

“Oh, no,” said Anna. “What now?”

But Kristoff knew that this movement was far different from what had happened before.

“Trolls?” he asked in surprise. He rushed to the mountain pass just as a bunch of familiar-looking boulders tumbled through. The boulders rolled toward Elsa and Anna and popped open to reveal mountain trolls. They were thrilled to see Kristoff and Sven and jumped onto the two of them, knocking Kristoff over in their excitement.

“Kristoff!” said Bulda, the troll who had raised Kristoff since he was very young. “We missed you!”

“Grand Pabbie!” Elsa said, recognizing the wise leader of the mountain trolls as he rolled right up to her.

“Well, never a dull moment with you two. I hope you are prepared for what you have done, Elsa. Angry magical spirits are not for the faint of heart,” the elder troll said.

“Why are they still angry?” she asked. They couldn’t possibly still be mad over what had happened when Anna and Elsa’s father was a child—or could they? “What does this have to do with Arendelle?”

“Hmm,” Grand Pabbie mused. “Let me see what I can see.”

Grand Pabbie turned his gaze up to the sky. He waved his hands, stirring the Northern Lights into motion. “The past is not what it seems. A wrong demands to be righted; the truth must be found. Without it…I see no future.”

The words worried Anna. “No future?”

Grand Pabbie lowered his hands and let the sky return to its normal patterns. He focused on Elsa, concern in his eyes. “When one can see no future, all one can do is the next right thing.”

“The next right thing is for me to go to the Enchanted Forest and find that voice,” said Elsa with resolve. “Kristoff, can I borrow your wagon…and Sven?” Elsa asked.

Kristoff raised an eyebrow. “I’m not very comfortable with the idea of that.”

Anna refused to let Elsa go by herself. “You are not going alone,” she insisted.

Elsa shook her head. “Anna, I have my powers to protect me. You don’t.”

“Wait, what, excuse me, pardon?” Anna asked, putting her hands on her hips and staring directly at her sister. “If I recall, your powers have mostly just gotten you into trouble. Protecting you has been my job.”

Grand Pabbie nodded in agreement. “She does have a point.”

Anna smiled at the troll. “Thank you.” Then she turned to her sister. “I’m coming.”

Kristoff chose that moment to enter the conversation.

“Me too,” he added, not wanting to be left out of an adventure. “I’ll drive.”

“I’ll bring the snacks!” Olaf said as the wind twirled him past them, the crystals that clung to him sparkling in the moonlight.

Elsa was reluctant to accept, but as she looked between Anna and Kristoff, she knew her only choice was to agree. She nodded before turning to Grand Pabbie.

“Will you look after our people?” Elsa asked. She was eager to leave and make the kingdom safe again, but was concerned for what the villagers would do until that happened.

“Of course,” Grand Pabbie said.

“Please make sure they stay out of the kingdom until we return,” Anna added.

“Thank you,” Elsa said, trusting the wise troll with the lives of her people the way her parents had trusted him with the life of her sister. “Let’s let them know,” she said to Kristoff, and the two of them rushed to tell everyone the news.

Grand Pabbie motioned for Anna to move close to him. “Anna, I am worried for her. We have always feared Elsa’s powers were too much for this world. Now we must pray they are enough.”

Anna nodded, unable to conceal the worry on her own face. “I won’t let anything happen to her.”

艾莎，我希望你已经做好面对自己所造成这一切的准备。

愤怒的魔法精灵可不是胆小的人能对付的，”年长的巨魔说，“他们为什么还在生气？”她问道。

chapters.title: 第13章
chapters.en:
Early the next morning, as the sunrise painted the fjords of Arendelle in warm colors, Elsa, Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven set out on their journey.

“Hyah!” Kristoff called, holding Sven’s reins. The reindeer trotted forward, pulling the wagon with the rest of the group in it.

Olaf broke the silence, not realizing that everyone was lost in their own thoughts of what might happen during their travels.

“Who’s into trivia?” he asked gleefully. No one answered, so he responded to himself. “I am! Okay!”

Anna caught Elsa’s eye across the snowman’s head. They smiled at each other and settled in for the trip, listening to Olaf spout off his fun facts. He had always been interested in unusual tidbits of information, but ever since he’d learned to read, his interest had grown tremendously.

“Did you know that water has memory?” he asked.

His friends found some of his facts to be interesting, but some were just plain strange.

“Did you know…gorillas burp when they are happy?” Olaf chirped.

As the miles and hours went by, they passed the sparkling waterfalls in the mountains around the fjord as the sun beat down on them from its highest point of the day. Olaf continued with his never-ending list of facts. This time when Elsa caught Anna’s glance, they both slowly shook their heads and rolled their eyes.

When the sun began to set, they finally reached the magnificent ice palace Elsa had built for herself. The sisters stared at it, remembering Elsa’s coronation day three years before.

When Anna had approached her sister and asked for her blessing to marry Hans, she and Elsa had fought. Elsa had found it ridiculous that Anna wanted to marry a man she had just met. And because of that, Elsa’s magical secret, which she had worked so hard to keep hidden, was revealed during their spat, when Anna accidentally pulled off one of Elsa’s gloves and ice shot from her hand.

Anna had felt so lost when Elsa ran off. But she didn’t blame Elsa. If she had been accused of sorcery by the Duke of Weselton, Anna probably would have run away, too. But Anna didn’t care if her sister could freeze things, or even if she could set things on fire. She had just wanted to be with her and for the two of them to be sisters again. Instead, all she could feel was the hurt that had consumed her after calling out to Elsa as her sister ran farther and farther away. Anna couldn’t imagine how lonely and afraid Elsa had been, too.

As Elsa stared at her beautiful ice palace, her thoughts also returned to that day. She remembered how scared she’d been—scared she would hurt Anna and others with her power if she stayed, and scared that her people would think she was a monster once they saw what her powers could do. She had held back tears as Anna called her name. She knew her sister had wanted her to come back. But all Elsa could think about in that moment was running as far away from Arendelle as possible so she could protect Anna, like she’d always tried to do.

Elsa’s confidence had grown when she realized the full extent of what she could do with her magic. It wasn’t until after Anna had sacrificed herself for Elsa, because of the true love she felt for her sister, that Elsa finally embraced the truth. Her magic wasn’t a curse. It wasn’t meant to hurt people. Elsa could do more than build snowmen and make beautiful icy patterns. She had constructed a magnificent ice palace that still stood strong today. Her magic was, and always had been, a gift.

Olaf’s giggle pulled Elsa out of her memories.

“Did you know men are six times more likely to be struck by lightning?” the snowman told whoever was still listening. “Sorry, Kristoff.”

They kept going, over the ridge beyond the ice palace, farther north than they had ever gone before.
chapters.zh:
第二天清晨，日出将阿伦黛尔的峡湾染上温暖的色彩，艾莎、安娜、奥拉夫、克斯托夫和斯文踏上了旅途。“驾！”克斯托夫握着斯文的缰绳喊道。

驯鹿小跑着向前，拉着载着其余伙伴的马车。

奥拉夫打破了沉默——他没意识到大家都沉浸在旅途可能遭遇种种的思绪里。“谁喜欢冷知识？”他兴冲冲地问。

没人回答，于是他自问自答。“我呀！

好呀！”安娜隔着奥拉夫的头顶，和艾莎对上了眼神。

她们相视一笑，安下心来准备赶路，听着奥拉夫滔滔不绝地讲起他那些有趣的小知识。

他向来对稀奇古怪的小知识感兴趣，而自从学会阅读后，这份兴趣更是与日俱增。“你们知道吗，水是有记忆的？”他问。

他的朋友们觉得他讲的一些知识挺有意思，但有些实在古怪得离谱。“你们知道吗……大猩猩开心的时候会打嗝？”奥拉夫叽叽喳喳地说。

随着路程和时光一点点流逝，他们经过峡湾群山间闪闪发亮的小瀑布，头顶的太阳正高悬在一天中最高的位置，炙烤着他们。

奥拉夫还在没完没了地讲着他那串知识。

这回艾莎和安娜目光相遇时，两人都缓缓摇了摇头，翻了个白眼。

太阳开始西沉时，他们终于抵达了艾莎为自己建造的宏伟冰宫。

姐妹俩凝望着它，想起了三年前艾莎加冕的那一天。

当时安娜走近姐姐，请求她祝福自己嫁给汉斯，她和艾莎却吵了一架。

艾莎觉得，安娜想嫁给一个才刚认识的男人，简直荒唐。

也正因如此，艾莎费尽心思隐藏的魔法秘密，在那场争吵中暴露了——安娜不小心扯下了艾莎的一只手套，冰霜便从她手中迸射而出。

艾莎跑掉时，安娜感到无比迷茫。

但她并没有责怪艾莎。

如果换作自己被韦塞尔顿公爵指责施展妖术，安娜大概也会逃走的。

但安娜不在乎姐姐能不能冰冻万物，甚至也不在乎她能不能点燃东西。

她只是想陪在姐姐身边，想让她们俩重新做回姐妹。

相反，她满心都是那样的伤痛——当姐姐越跑越远，她朝艾莎呼喊，那份痛楚将她彻底吞没。

安娜无法想象，艾莎当时又是多么孤独和害怕。

艾莎凝望着自己美丽的冰宫，思绪也同样回到了那一天。

她记得自己当时有多害怕——害怕若留下来，会用魔力伤害安娜和他人；也害怕百姓一旦见识了她的力量，会把她当成怪物。

当安娜呼唤她的名字时，她强忍着泪水。

她知道，妹妹是希望她回来的。

但那一刻，艾莎满脑子只想着尽可能远远地逃离阿伦黛尔，好去保护安娜——就像她一直努力做的那样。

当艾莎意识到自己魔法的全部潜能时，她的自信也增长了。

直到安娜因为对妹妹的真爱而甘愿为艾莎牺牲自己之后，艾莎才终于接受了真相。

她的魔法不是诅咒。

它本不是用来伤害人的。

艾莎能做的，远不止堆雪人和勾勒美丽的冰纹。

她建起了一座宏伟的冰宫，至今依然傲然屹立。

她的魔法，向来、且一直都是一份礼物。

奥拉夫的咯咯笑声把艾莎从回忆里拉了出来。“你们知道吗，男人被闪电击中的概率要高出六倍？”雪人冲着还在听的人说道，“抱歉，克斯托夫。”他们继续向前，越过冰宫之外的山脊，朝着比以往任何时候都更靠北的地方走去。

sentences.en: Early the next morning, as the sunrise painted the fjords of Arendelle in warm colors, Elsa, Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven set out on their journey. “Hyah!” Kristoff called, holding Sven’s reins.
sentences.zh: 第二天清晨，日出将阿伦黛尔的峡湾染上温暖的色彩，艾莎、安娜、奥拉夫、克斯托夫和斯文踏上了旅途。“驾！”克斯托夫握着斯文的缰绳喊道。

sentences.en: The reindeer trotted forward, pulling the wagon with the rest of the group in it.
sentences.zh: 驯鹿小跑着向前，拉着载着其余伙伴的马车。

sentences.en: Olaf broke the silence, not realizing that everyone was lost in their own thoughts of what might happen during their travels. “Who’s into trivia?” he asked gleefully.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫打破了沉默——他没意识到大家都沉浸在旅途可能遭遇种种的思绪里。“谁喜欢冷知识？”他兴冲冲地问。

sentences.en: No one answered, so he responded to himself. “I am!
sentences.zh: 没人回答，于是他自问自答。“我呀！

sentences.en: Okay!” Anna caught Elsa’s eye across the snowman’s head.
sentences.zh: 好呀！”安娜隔着奥拉夫的头顶，和艾莎对上了眼神。

sentences.en: They smiled at each other and settled in for the trip, listening to Olaf spout off his fun facts.
sentences.zh: 她们相视一笑，安下心来准备赶路，听着奥拉夫滔滔不绝地讲起他那些有趣的小知识。

sentences.en: He had always been interested in unusual tidbits of information, but ever since he’d learned to read, his interest had grown tremendously. “Did you know that water has memory?” he asked.
sentences.zh: 他向来对稀奇古怪的小知识感兴趣，而自从学会阅读后，这份兴趣更是与日俱增。“你们知道吗，水是有记忆的？”他问。

sentences.en: His friends found some of his facts to be interesting, but some were just plain strange. “Did you know…gorillas burp when they are happy?” Olaf chirped.
sentences.zh: 他的朋友们觉得他讲的一些知识挺有意思，但有些实在古怪得离谱。“你们知道吗……大猩猩开心的时候会打嗝？”奥拉夫叽叽喳喳地说。

sentences.en: As the miles and hours went by, they passed the sparkling waterfalls in the mountains around the fjord as the sun beat down on them from its highest point of the day.
sentences.zh: 随着路程和时光一点点流逝，他们经过峡湾群山间闪闪发亮的小瀑布，头顶的太阳正高悬在一天中最高的位置，炙烤着他们。

sentences.en: Olaf continued with his never-ending list of facts.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫还在没完没了地讲着他那串知识。

sentences.en: This time when Elsa caught Anna’s glance, they both slowly shook their heads and rolled their eyes.
sentences.zh: 这回艾莎和安娜目光相遇时，两人都缓缓摇了摇头，翻了个白眼。

sentences.en: When the sun began to set, they finally reached the magnificent ice palace Elsa had built for herself.
sentences.zh: 太阳开始西沉时，他们终于抵达了艾莎为自己建造的宏伟冰宫。

sentences.en: The sisters stared at it, remembering Elsa’s coronation day three years before.
sentences.zh: 姐妹俩凝望着它，想起了三年前艾莎加冕的那一天。

sentences.en: When Anna had approached her sister and asked for her blessing to marry Hans, she and Elsa had fought.
sentences.zh: 当时安娜走近姐姐，请求她祝福自己嫁给汉斯，她和艾莎却吵了一架。

sentences.en: Elsa had found it ridiculous that Anna wanted to marry a man she had just met.
sentences.zh: 艾莎觉得，安娜想嫁给一个才刚认识的男人，简直荒唐。

sentences.en: And because of that, Elsa’s magical secret, which she had worked so hard to keep hidden, was revealed during their spat, when Anna accidentally pulled off one of Elsa’s gloves and ice shot from her hand.
sentences.zh: 也正因如此，艾莎费尽心思隐藏的魔法秘密，在那场争吵中暴露了——安娜不小心扯下了艾莎的一只手套，冰霜便从她手中迸射而出。

sentences.en: Anna had felt so lost when Elsa ran off.
sentences.zh: 艾莎跑掉时，安娜感到无比迷茫。

sentences.en: But she didn’t blame Elsa.
sentences.zh: 但她并没有责怪艾莎。

sentences.en: If she had been accused of sorcery by the Duke of Weselton, Anna probably would have run away, too.
sentences.zh: 如果换作自己被韦塞尔顿公爵指责施展妖术，安娜大概也会逃走的。

sentences.en: But Anna didn’t care if her sister could freeze things, or even if she could set things on fire.
sentences.zh: 但安娜不在乎姐姐能不能冰冻万物，甚至也不在乎她能不能点燃东西。

sentences.en: She had just wanted to be with her and for the two of them to be sisters again.
sentences.zh: 她只是想陪在姐姐身边，想让她们俩重新做回姐妹。

sentences.en: Instead, all she could feel was the hurt that had consumed her after calling out to Elsa as her sister ran farther and farther away.
sentences.zh: 相反，她满心都是那样的伤痛——当姐姐越跑越远，她朝艾莎呼喊，那份痛楚将她彻底吞没。

sentences.en: Anna couldn’t imagine how lonely and afraid Elsa had been, too.
sentences.zh: 安娜无法想象，艾莎当时又是多么孤独和害怕。

sentences.en: As Elsa stared at her beautiful ice palace, her thoughts also returned to that day.
sentences.zh: 艾莎凝望着自己美丽的冰宫，思绪也同样回到了那一天。

sentences.en: She remembered how scared she’d been—scared she would hurt Anna and others with her power if she stayed, and scared that her people would think she was a monster once they saw what her powers could do.
sentences.zh: 她记得自己当时有多害怕——害怕若留下来，会用魔力伤害安娜和他人；也害怕百姓一旦见识了她的力量，会把她当成怪物。

sentences.en: She had held back tears as Anna called her name.
sentences.zh: 当安娜呼唤她的名字时，她强忍着泪水。

sentences.en: She knew her sister had wanted her to come back.
sentences.zh: 她知道，妹妹是希望她回来的。

sentences.en: But all Elsa could think about in that moment was running as far away from Arendelle as possible so she could protect Anna, like she’d always tried to do.
sentences.zh: 但那一刻，艾莎满脑子只想着尽可能远远地逃离阿伦黛尔，好去保护安娜——就像她一直努力做的那样。

sentences.en: Elsa’s confidence had grown when she realized the full extent of what she could do with her magic.
sentences.zh: 当艾莎意识到自己魔法的全部潜能时，她的自信也增长了。

sentences.en: It wasn’t until after Anna had sacrificed herself for Elsa, because of the true love she felt for her sister, that Elsa finally embraced the truth.
sentences.zh: 直到安娜因为对妹妹的真爱而甘愿为艾莎牺牲自己之后，艾莎才终于接受了真相。

sentences.en: Her magic wasn’t a curse.
sentences.zh: 她的魔法不是诅咒。

sentences.en: It wasn’t meant to hurt people.
sentences.zh: 它本不是用来伤害人的。

sentences.en: Elsa could do more than build snowmen and make beautiful icy patterns.
sentences.zh: 艾莎能做的，远不止堆雪人和勾勒美丽的冰纹。

sentences.en: She had constructed a magnificent ice palace that still stood strong today.
sentences.zh: 她建起了一座宏伟的冰宫，至今依然傲然屹立。

sentences.en: Her magic was, and always had been, a gift.
sentences.zh: 她的魔法，向来、且一直都是一份礼物。

sentences.en: Olaf’s giggle pulled Elsa out of her memories. “Did you know men are six times more likely to be struck by lightning?” the snowman told whoever was still listening. “Sorry, Kristoff.” They kept going, over the ridge beyond the ice palace, farther north than they had ever gone before.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫的咯咯笑声把艾莎从回忆里拉了出来。“你们知道吗，男人被闪电击中的概率要高出六倍？”雪人冲着还在听的人说道，“抱歉，克斯托夫。”他们继续向前，越过冰宫之外的山脊，朝着比以往任何时候都更靠北的地方走去。

chapters.title: 第14章
chapters.en:
“Did you know we blink four million times a day?” Olaf blurted out. “Did you know wombats poop squares? Did you know donkeys sink but mules don’t?”

Kristoff didn’t mind that Olaf was full of facts, but his head was about to explode from all the talking. So he jumped in when Olaf took a breath. “Did you know sleeping quietly on long journeys prevents insanity?”

Olaf thought about it. “That doesn’t sound true.”

Elsa, Anna, and Sven immediately agreed with Kristoff, nodding vigorously.

“It’s true,” said Anna.

“It’s absolutely true,” said Elsa.

“Gruunnt,” said Sven.

The snowman shrugged. “Well, that was unanimous, but I will look it up when I get home.” He lay back in the hay and watched as Elsa created an ice blanket for him. She placed it over him, making sure he was completely covered. Then she kissed him on his forehead.

“Good night,” she said.

After tucking the blanket under his chin, Olaf finally went to sleep.

Elsa began to yawn when she saw Olaf snuggled in so cozily. It had been a long night for everyone. She pulled her mother’s scarf out of Anna’s bag and wrapped it around her shoulders. Then she nestled down in the hay and drifted to sleep next to her friend.

Anna took the opportunity to climb from the back of the wagon up to the front bench and sit with Kristoff. “They’re both asleep,” she reported. She straightened her clothes, pulled hay from her hair, and checked to make sure her breath smelled fresh. “So, what do you want to do?” She snuggled up against him.

Kristoff grinned. “I can think of something,” he said, tossing the reins to Sven before digging in his pocket. “Sven, keep us steady, will yah?

Sven’s gait changed to a romantic little prance as he grunted his support.

Anna smiled, closing her eyes as she pursed her lips together and leaned in to Kristoff for a kiss.

But Kristoff was so nervous, he missed her cue. “Anna. Ahem.” He cleared his throat and tried again. “Anna, remember our first trip like this, when I said you’d have to be crazy to want to marry a man you just met?”

Anna’s eyes widened and she scooted far enough down the front bench that Marshmallow could have sat between them. “Wait, what?” she asked. “Crazy? You didn’t say I was crazy. You think I’m crazy?”

“No, I did. You were…” He tried to explain, but stopped short at Sven’s warning grunt. Kristoff wanted to save the moment, to bring it back on course. He couldn’t mess this up again. “Not crazy, clearly,” he said dramatically. “Ha, just naive.”

But apparently being naive was even more offensive to Anna. She crossed her arms over her chest, leaned back in the seat, and gave Kristoff a long look. Feeling confused, Kristoff glanced at Sven, who was shaking his head in dismay. Kristoff scrambled for words to dig himself out of the ditch he had tumbled into.

“Not naive. Just new…to love. Like I was. And when you’re new, you’re bound to get it wrong,” he finished with confidence. But that confidence quickly deflated.

“So you’re saying I’m wrong for you?” Anna asked, one eyebrow raised.

“What?” Kristoff asked in alarm. “No. No, no, no.” He took a breath to try to gather his thoughts. “I’m not saying you’re not wrong or crazy. I’m saying that it’s—”

Anna and Kristoff were so intent on their conversation that neither saw Elsa wake and sit straight up, her expression serious as she looked around, searching for something.

“Kristoff, stop,” she said.

He reached for the reins and pulled on them as he asked Sven to bring the wagon to a halt.

“Good idea,” he mumbled, knowing he had botched his chance to ask Anna to marry him, again.

“I hear it. I hear the voice,” Elsa said firmly.

“You do?” Anna asked, her attention now on her sister. “Olaf, wake up.”

Elsa jumped out of the wagon and rushed over to a small rise at the edge of the road. What she saw overwhelmed her with emotion. The others joined her and gasped in awe at what lay before them.
chapters.zh:
“你们知道吗，我们一天要眨四百万人次眼？”奥拉夫脱口而出，“你们知道吗，袋熊拉出来的屎是方形的？

“你们知道吗，驴子会沉下去，骡子却不会？”克斯托夫倒不介意奥拉夫满肚子都是冷知识，但他脑子里快要被这些话炸开了。

于是趁着奥拉夫换气的空当，他赶紧插话：“你们知道吗，长途旅行时安安静静睡觉能防止发疯？”奥拉夫想了想说：“这听起来不像真的。”艾莎、安娜和斯文立刻附和克斯托夫，使劲点头。“是真的，”安娜说。“绝对是真的，”艾莎说。“咕噜——”斯文也叫了一声。

雪人耸了耸肩：“好吧，算是全票通过了，不过等我回到家要查查资料。”他仰面躺进干草里，看着艾莎为他变出一条冰毯子。

她把毯子盖在他身上，确保把他盖得严严实实。

接着她在他额头上亲了一下。“晚安，”她说。

奥拉夫把毯子掖到下巴底下，终于睡着了。

艾莎看到奥拉夫蜷缩得那么舒服，自己也打起了哈欠。

对大家来说，这真是一个漫长的夜晚。

她从安娜的包里取出母亲的围巾，披在自己的肩上。

然后她钻进干草堆，在朋友身旁慢慢进入了梦乡。

安娜趁机从马车后车厢爬到前座长椅上，挨着克斯托夫坐下。“他们俩都睡着了，”她报告说。

她理了理衣服，从头发里揪出干草，还确认了一下自己口气清新。“那么，你想做些什么？”她依偎到他身边。

克斯托夫咧嘴一笑。“我倒能想到一件事，”他说着把缰绳丢给斯文，手伸进兜里掏着。“斯文，帮我们稳住车子，行不？”

斯文哼了一声表示支持，脚步也变成了一副浪漫的小碎步。

安娜微笑着闭上眼睛，嘟起嘴唇，倾身向克斯托夫凑过去要亲吻。

可克斯托夫太紧张了，没接住她的暗示。“安娜。

咳咳。”他清了清嗓子，重新试了一次。“安娜，还记得我们第一次这样的旅行吗？当时我说，想嫁给一个刚认识的男人，你一定是疯了？”安娜瞪大了眼睛，在前座长椅上往远处挪了挪，挪得都能让棉花糖坐到他们中间了。“等等，你说什么？”她问。“疯了？

你没说过我疯了。

你觉得我疯了？”“不，我确实说过。

你是……”他想要解释，却被斯文一声警告般的哼叫打断了。

克斯托夫想把这一刻挽救回来，把气氛拉回正轨。

他不能再搞砸了。“不疯，显然不疯，”他夸张地说，“哈，只是有点天真。”但显然，“天真”这个词更让安娜生气。

她双手抱在胸前，靠回座位上，久久地盯着克斯托夫。

克斯托夫一头雾水，瞥了斯文一眼，只见斯文正沮丧地摇着头。

克斯托夫手忙脚乱地找词儿，想把自己从跌进去的坑里爬出来。“不是天真。

只是对……爱情还陌生。

就像我以前一样。

而一个人刚开始的时候，难免会出错，”他自信地做结。

但这份自信很快泄了气。“所以你是说，我配不上你？”安娜挑起一边眉毛问。“什么？”克斯托夫慌了，“不。

不不不。”他深吸一口气，想理清思路。“我不是说你不对，也不是说你疯了。

我是说，这是——”安娜和克斯托夫太专注于对话，谁也没注意到艾莎醒来，坐得笔直，神情严肃地四下张望，像在找什么。“克斯托夫，停下，”她说。

他伸手抓住缰绳一拉，让斯文把马车停下。“好主意，”他嘟囔着，明知自己又一次错失了向安娜求婚的机会。“我听见了。

我听见那个声音了，”艾莎坚定地说。“真的？”安娜问，注意力这下转到姐姐身上。“奥拉夫，醒醒。”艾莎跳下马车，冲向路边一个小土坡。

眼前的景象让她百感交集。

其他人也跟了过来，望着眼前的景象惊叹地倒吸一口凉气。

sentences.zh: 咳咳。”他清了清嗓子，重新试了一次。“安娜，还记得我们第一次这样的旅行吗？当时我说，想嫁给一个刚认识的男人，你一定是疯了？”安娜瞪大了眼睛，在前座长椅上往远处挪了挪，挪得都能让棉花糖坐到他们中间了。“等等，你说什么？”她问。“疯了？

sentences.en: You didn’t say I was crazy.
sentences.zh: 你没说过我疯了。

sentences.en: You think I’m crazy?” “No, I did.
sentences.zh: 你觉得我疯了？”“不，我确实说过。

sentences.en: You were…” He tried to explain, but stopped short at Sven’s warning grunt.
sentences.zh: 你是……”他想要解释，却被斯文一声警告般的哼叫打断了。

sentences.en: Kristoff wanted to save the moment, to bring it back on course.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫想把这一刻挽救回来，把气氛拉回正轨。

sentences.en: He couldn’t mess this up again. “Not crazy, clearly,” he said dramatically. “Ha, just naive. ” But apparently being naive was even more offensive to Anna.
sentences.zh: 他不能再搞砸了。“不疯，显然不疯，”他夸张地说，“哈，只是有点天真。”但显然，“天真”这个词更让安娜生气。

sentences.en: She crossed her arms over her chest, leaned back in the seat, and gave Kristoff a long look.
sentences.zh: 她双手抱在胸前，靠回座位上，久久地盯着克斯托夫。

sentences.en: Feeling confused, Kristoff glanced at Sven, who was shaking his head in dismay.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫一头雾水，瞥了斯文一眼，只见斯文正沮丧地摇着头。

sentences.en: Kristoff scrambled for words to dig himself out of the ditch he had tumbled into. “Not naive.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫手忙脚乱地找词儿，想把自己从跌进去的坑里爬出来。“不是天真。

sentences.en: Just new…to love.
sentences.zh: 只是对……爱情还陌生。

sentences.en: Like I was.
sentences.zh: 就像我以前一样。

sentences.en: And when you’re new, you’re bound to get it wrong,” he finished with confidence.
sentences.zh: 而一个人刚开始的时候，难免会出错，”他自信地做结。

sentences.en: But that confidence quickly deflated. “So you’re saying I’m wrong for you?” Anna asked, one eyebrow raised. “What?” Kristoff asked in alarm. “No.
sentences.zh: 但这份自信很快泄了气。“所以你是说，我配不上你？”安娜挑起一边眉毛问。“什么？”克斯托夫慌了，“不。

sentences.en: No, no, no.” He took a breath to try to gather his thoughts. “I’m not saying you’re not wrong or crazy.
sentences.zh: 不不不。”他深吸一口气，想理清思路。“我不是说你不对，也不是说你疯了。

sentences.en: I’m saying that it’s—” Anna and Kristoff were so intent on their conversation that neither saw Elsa wake and sit straight up, her expression serious as she looked around, searching for something. “Kristoff, stop,” she said.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是——”安娜和克斯托夫太专注于对话，谁也没注意到艾莎醒来，坐得笔直，神情严肃地四下张望，像在找什么。“克斯托夫，停下，”她说。

sentences.en: He reached for the reins and pulled on them as he asked Sven to bring the wagon to a halt. “Good idea,” he mumbled, knowing he had botched his chance to ask Anna to marry him, again. “I hear it.
sentences.zh: 他伸手抓住缰绳一拉，让斯文把马车停下。“好主意，”他嘟囔着，明知自己又一次错失了向安娜求婚的机会。“我听见了。

sentences.en: I hear the voice,” Elsa said firmly. “You do?” Anna asked, her attention now on her sister. “Olaf, wake up.” Elsa jumped out of the wagon and rushed over to a small rise at the edge of the road.
sentences.zh: 我听见那个声音了，”艾莎坚定地说。“真的？”安娜问，注意力这下转到姐姐身上。“奥拉夫，醒醒。”艾莎跳下马车，冲向路边一个小土坡。

sentences.en: What she saw overwhelmed her with emotion.
sentences.zh: 眼前的景象让她百感交集。

sentences.en: The others joined her and gasped in awe at what lay before them.
sentences.zh: 其他人也跟了过来，望着眼前的景象惊叹地倒吸一口凉气。

chapters.title: 第15章
chapters.en:
The morning light shone on a magical mist that stood like a wall across a wide, flat plain down below them—a wall that barred them from going any farther. Elsa wondered if it was the impenetrable mist that surrounded the Enchanted Forest. Have we finally reached it? she thought. It seemed possible. The mist appeared to enshroud a forest of tall trees—the tops of which they saw poking out of the ceiling of the mist. But everything else in the Enchanted Forest was hidden behind the haze and the rolling particles of colored lights that flashed like lightning bugs as they danced through the mist. Elsa’s heart raced, and she couldn’t resist the pull she felt any longer. She quickly climbed down the side of the cliff, and the others followed.

Elsa ran across the plain, straight toward the Enchanted Forest. Anna did her best to keep up. Then Elsa stopped before she reached the cloudlike mass and stared at it in silence.

Kristoff was not as patient. He walked past the two girls and approached the mist in wonder. He reached out a hand and pressed it against the gray surface. His hand sprang back like it had hit a bouncy ball.

Olaf watched, fascinated. What had happened to Kristoff’s hand gave him an idea. He took a few steps back and charged at the gray cloud as fast as he could. His body bounced off it as if he were hitting a balloon. He giggled as he flew through the air and landed on the ground. All this time, he had thought the journey north would be dangerous. This was fun!

Olaf ran at the mist again. He bounced back again, so he did the only thing he could—he bounced off the mist over and over, laughing hysterically each time.

Anna moved to stand next to Elsa as they stared at the rolling mist. Elsa took a deep breath and grabbed Anna’s hand for strength, and the two of them approached.

For them, the mist sparkled and pulled back, revealing four towering stones with a symbol at the top of each one.

“Air, fire, water, earth,” Elsa said, naming each one and knowing they were the same symbols she had seen on the ice crystals in the sky.

With every step they took, the mist parted further to let them through. Sven trailed after them and called out for Kristoff.

Kristoff saw that the curtain of clouds had parted. He caught Olaf’s attention, and they walked up behind the sisters with Sven.

“Promise me—we’ll do this together,” Anna said to Elsa.

“I promise,” Elsa agreed.

Kristoff grabbed Anna’s hand and put an arm around Sven. Olaf grabbed Elsa’s hand. As they all walked farther inside the mist together, it closed behind them and sealed them in.
chapters.zh:
晨光洒在一片神奇的薄雾上，那雾像一堵墙，横亘在他们下方一片广阔平坦的原野上——一堵挡住他们去路的墙。

艾莎心想，这会不会就是环绕魔法森林、无法穿透的那片迷雾。

我们终于到了吗？她想。

看起来有可能。

迷雾仿佛笼罩着一片高大的树林——他们看见树梢从雾顶探了出来。

但魔法森林里其余的一切，都藏在那片朦胧之后，还有翻滚的彩色光点，像萤火虫般在雾中穿梭飞舞、闪烁不停。

艾莎心跳加速，再也无法抵抗内心那股牵引。

她飞快地顺着崖壁爬下去，其他人紧跟在后。

艾莎跑过原野，直奔魔法森林。

安娜拼尽全力跟上她。

跑到那团云状物跟前，艾莎停下脚步，静静地凝视着它。

克斯托夫可没那么有耐心。

他从两个女孩身边走过，满心惊奇地走近迷雾。

他伸出手，按在灰色的雾面上。

他的手像撞上弹力球一样弹了回来。

奥拉夫看得入了迷。

克斯托夫的手发生的事，给了他一个主意。

他后退几步，然后使出全力朝那团灰云冲了过去。

他的身体像撞上气球一样被弹了回来。

他一边在空中飞，一边咯咯笑着，最后落在地上。

一直以来，他都以为北行之旅会充满危险。

这可真好玩！

奥拉夫又朝迷雾冲了过去。

他又被弹了回来，于是他只能做唯一能做的事——一遍又一遍地从雾上弹开，每次都笑得前仰后合。

安娜走到艾莎身边，两人一起盯着翻滚的迷雾。

艾莎深吸一口气，握住安娜的手给自己打气，姐妹俩一起走上前去。

对他们来说，迷雾闪着光往后退去，露出四块高耸的巨石，每块顶端都有一个符号。“风、火、水、土，”艾莎一边逐一念出，一边认出这正是她在天上冰晶上见过的符号。

他们每往前走一步，迷雾就分得更开，好让他们通过。

斯文跟在他们身后，呼唤着克斯托夫。

克斯托夫看到那道云帘已经分开。

他引起奥拉夫的注意，和斯文一起走到姐妹俩身后。“答应我——我们一起走，”安娜对艾莎说。“我答应你，”艾莎应道。

克斯托夫握住安娜的手，一只胳膊搂住斯文。

奥拉夫抓住艾莎的手。

大家手牵着手一起往迷雾深处走去，迷雾在他们身后合拢，把他们封在了里面。

chapters.title: 第16章
chapters.en:
The mist sparkled. Swirling particles of color danced throughout it. Sven watched, grunting nervously.

“It’s okay,” Kristoff said to calm his friend.

“Did you know that an enchanted forest is a place of transformation?” Olaf asked, his face full of joy. “I have no idea what that means, but I can’t wait to see what it’s going to do to each of us.”

The flashes of color were mesmerizing, until the lights came together and formed ribbons behind the group. The mist moved forward and touched them. But now when it connected with the friends, they didn’t bounce off. Instead, the mist shoved them forward!

The group shouted out in a blur of voices.

“Hey!”

“What the—?”

“No pushing!”

“What is this?”

“Too fast!”

“Tree!” Kristoff grunted as he was pushed straight into a trunk. As he untangled himself, the mist pushed him up to join his group.

They stumbled over rocks and tree roots as they ran, getting turned around in confusion before the mist shoved them completely out of its grasp.

“What was that?” Kristoff asked, thoroughly dazed as he stared at the wall of mist that now seemed as calm as when they had viewed it for the very first time.

Olaf was back to bouncing on it like before. The others banged their fists against it, hoping to find a way out.

“Okay, it let us in, but it clearly doesn’t want to let us out,” Kristoff observed.

“And…we are locked in here. Probably should have seen that coming,” Anna added.

Elsa sighed and let her hands drop to her sides. She decided to accept that going back through the mist wasn’t the way out. When she turned to see where they had been deposited, she realized they were in the middle of the Enchanted Forest.

“This forest is beautiful,” she said in awe as she stepped forward.

The others turned to see what Elsa was talking about. The most amazing, picture-perfect forest stretched before them. They kept moving, captivated by the vibrant reds and yellows of the leaves. Elsa was amazed by the forest canopy that stretched into the mist-covered sky. Sven darted from one tree to the next, scratching his back on the strong trunks.

Anna’s breath caught in her throat when she stepped over a rise and looked down at the dam her father had described to her and Elsa when they were children. It was covered in vines and other shrubbery, but it was tall and vast, and no water leaked through.

“The dam. It still stands,” she said. “It was in Grand Pabbie’s visions. But why?”

Kristoff walked over to her. “Still in good shape…thank goodness.”

“What do you mean?” Anna asked, looking up at him.

“Well, if that dam broke,” Kristoff warned, “it would send a tidal wave so big, it would wash away everything on this fjord.”

Anna couldn’t hide her worry. “Everything? Arendelle’s on this fjord.”

“Nothing’s gonna happen to Arendelle, Anna,” Kristoff assured her. “It’s going to be fine. Come here.” He wrapped an arm around her shoulders. She leaned in close to his touch and was able to relax. Together, they gazed at the beautiful dam.

Kristoff realized how majestic everything was around them. And he had an idea.

“You know, under different circumstances, this would be a pretty romantic place…don’t you think?”

“Different circumstances?” Anna asked, looking puzzled. “You mean like with someone else?”

“What? No, no—” Kristoff said, fishing a hand into his back pocket for the ring he had already tried to give her twice. But now seemed a better time than ever. He found it, pulled it out of his pocket, and put it behind his back. “I’m saying…” He cleared his throat to make sure the words came out right. “Just in case we don’t make it out of here—”

Anna pulled away from him. “Wait, what? You don’t think we’re going to make it out of here?”

“No. No!” he said. “I mean, we will make it out here. Well, technically, the odds are kinda complicated. But my point is, in case we die—”

“You think we’re going to die?” Anna asked, her voice getting higher.

“No!” Kristoff insisted. “No, no, no, we will die at some point, but not at any recent time will we die—”

Anna realized Elsa wasn’t with them. If they were in danger, they all needed to stay together. And Anna had made an oath to Grand Pabbie to protect her sister.

“Where’s Elsa?” she asked. “I swore I wouldn’t leave her side. Elsa?” Anna ran off to search for her.

“—but way far in the future, we will die!” Kristoff sighed. Why couldn’t he ever get it right? He’d blown it yet again. Then, as best friends do, Sven came to his side. The reindeer nudged him.

Kristoff looked at him. “Sven, don’t patronize me.” Kristoff felt bad enough already.

Elsa wandered among the tall trees, enjoying the beauty around her. She took in a deep, peaceful breath and closed her eyes, trying to forget her cares. But there was something…something she couldn’t put her finger on, and it made the hairs on the back of her neck stand up. Her eyes shot open, and she spun quickly when she sensed something rushing toward her.

She was surprised to see it was Anna.

“Elsa!” her sister said. “There you are. You okay?”

“I’m fine,” Elsa replied, unsettled by what she had just felt.

Anna was relieved. She took a moment to look around. “Okay. Good. Where’s Olaf?”
chapters.zh:
迷雾闪闪发光。

漩涡般的彩色光点在雾中四处起舞。

斯文看着，紧张地哼哼。“没事，”克斯托夫安抚朋友道。“你们知道吗，魔法森林是会改变人的地方？”奥拉夫满脸欢喜地问。“我完全不懂这是什么意思，但我等不及想看看它会对我们每个人都有什么影响。”那些彩色闪光令人着迷，直到所有光点汇聚起来，在队伍身后化作一条条光带。

迷雾向前涌动，触到了他们。

可这一次，雾碰到伙伴们时，他们没有被弹开。

相反，迷雾把他们往前推！

众人乱糟糟地叫成一片。“嘿！”“搞什么——？”“别推！”“这是什么东西？”“太快了！”“树！”克斯托夫被直接推进了一棵树干，发出一声闷哼。

他刚从树干上挣脱开，迷雾又推着他去和家人会合。

他们奔跑时踉踉跄跄地绊过石头和树根，晕头转向地转了好几圈，直到迷雾把他们彻底推出了掌控。“那是什么？”克斯托夫呆呆地问，眼睛盯着那堵迷雾墙——此刻它又平静得像他们初见时一样。

奥拉夫又像之前那样在雾上弹来弹去。

其他人用拳头捶打着雾墙，希望能找到出路。“好吧，它放我们进来，但显然不想放我们出去，”克斯托夫说，“而且……我们被锁在里面了。

“早该想到的，”安娜补了一句。

艾莎叹了口气，双手垂在身侧。

她决定接受这个事实：从迷雾穿回去不是出路。

她转过身，想看看自己被送到了哪里，这才发现他们正站在魔法森林中央。“这片森林真美，”她一边敬畏地说，一边迈步向前。

其他人也转头去看艾莎说的是什么。

一片美得不可思议、如同画卷般完美的森林在他们眼前展开。

他们继续前行，被叶片上鲜亮的红与黄深深吸引。

艾莎惊叹于那片伸向迷雾笼罩天空的林冠。

斯文从一棵树窜到另一棵，在粗壮的树干上蹭着背。

安娜翻过一道土坡，低头看见那座水坝——父亲小时候曾对她和艾莎描述过它——顿时屏住了呼吸。

水坝上爬满了藤蔓和其他灌木，但它依然高大巍峨，没有一丝漏水。“水坝。

它还立着，”她说，“这也是皮比大仙预见过的景象。

可为什么呢？”克斯托夫走到她身边。“状况还不错……谢天谢地。”“你什么意思？”安娜抬头问他。“唔，要是那水坝塌了，”克斯托夫提醒道，“就会掀起巨大的海啸，把这条峡湾里的一切都冲走。”安娜掩饰不住担忧。“一切？

阿伦黛尔就在这条峡湾上。”“阿伦黛尔不会有事的，安娜，”克斯托夫向她保证，“会没事的。

过来。”他用一只胳膊搂住她的肩膀。

她靠上他的肩膀，终于放松下来。

两人一起凝望着那座美丽的水坝。

克斯托夫意识到，周围的万物是何等壮丽。

他冒出了一个念头。“你说，要是在别的情境下，这儿该是个挺浪漫的地方……你不觉得吗？”“别的情境？”安娜不解地问，“你是说，跟别人一起？”“什么？

不不——”克斯托夫说着，把手伸进后兜，掏出那枚他已经试过两次想送给她的戒指。

可现在似乎比以往任何时候都更合适。

他找到了，从兜里掏出来，藏到背后。“我是说……”他清了清嗓子，确保话说得妥帖。“就怕我们走不出这里——”安娜从他身边退开。“等等，你说什么？

你觉得我们走不出这里了？”“不。

不！”他说，“我是说，我们能走出这里。

唔，严格来说，概率这事儿有点复杂。

但我想说的是，万一我们死了——”“你认为我们会死？”安娜的声音拔高了。“不会！”克斯托夫坚持道，“不不不，我们迟早会死，但绝不会在最近死——”安娜这时发现艾莎不在他们身边。

若真有危险，大家必须待在一起。

而且安娜曾向皮比大仙发誓要保护姐姐。“艾莎呢？”她问，“我发过誓不会离开她身边的。

艾莎？”安娜跑开去找她了。“——但那是很久很久以后的事，我们总会死的！”克斯托夫叹了口气。

他怎么老是把话说岔？

他又一次搞砸了。

然后，作为最好的朋友，斯文来到他身边。

驯鹿用鼻子拱了拱他。

克斯托夫看着他。“斯文，别安慰我了。”克斯托夫已经够难受了。

艾莎在高大的树木间漫步，享受着周围的美好。

她深深、平静地吸了一口气，闭上眼睛，想把烦忧都忘掉。

可有什么……某种她说不清的东西，让她后颈的汗毛都竖了起来。

她猛地睁开眼，感觉到有什么东西朝自己冲来，迅速转过身。

她惊讶地发现那是安娜。“艾莎！”姐姐喊道，“原来你在这儿。

你还好吗？”“我没事，”艾莎回答，心里还因刚才的感觉而隐隐不安。

安娜松了口气。

她环顾四周，定了定神。“好吧。

好。

奥拉夫呢？”

chapters.title: 第17章
chapters.en:
Olaf was happy to explore the forest. He didn’t even know he was lost. He marched along, thinking his friends were right behind him.

“Anyone else feel like we’re being watched. Anyone? No one?” Olaf turned around and saw only the forest. “I’m alone.”

He peered deeper into the woods, trying to confirm that no one was with him.

“Anna? Elsa? Sven? Samantha?” He laughed. “I don’t even know a Samantha.”

He continued laughing until a gust of wind blew at his backside.

“Whoa,” he said in surprise. He spun around again, searching for the culprit. Seeing nothing, the snowman simply shrugged.

The trees above him crackled, and a pile of leaves crashed on his head. Olaf pushed the leaves off and picked one out of his mouth.

“That’s normal,” he said.

A rock flew out of the bushes as if from nowhere, and when Olaf turned to continue on his journey, he tripped over it and landed on his face.

A hot gush of water pushed him back up to his feet.

This is getting weird, he thought.

Tree limbs shimmied above his head, rattling the leaves as something large scampered through them. Olaf turned quickly to look behind him.

“What was that?” he asked.

A large hole gaped in the ground before him, and he quickly stopped before he fell in. He cautiously looked into what seemed to be a bottomless pit.

“Samantha?” he called, his voice echoing as it faded into the nothingness.

No response. Olaf backed away nervously.

The snowman was confident that although there was no explanation at the moment, there would be one day. He just needed to be a bit older and wiser. Then, when he thought back about everything strange that was happening to him now, he would realize it had all been completely normal.

A sizzling sound caught his attention, and he turned his head just in time to see a smoking blaze burn through the moss and race toward him. He didn’t know what it was, but he knew it couldn’t be good. He dove out of the way.

Olaf kept moving and soon reached a dark part of the forest, overgrown with vines and twisted branches all around him. He convinced himself that the fear he felt would seem childish in a couple of years. Creepy, unblinking white eyes peered out of the bushes everywhere he looked. He tried not to think about anything but using his manners.

“Excuse me,” he said, backing out of the small grove of trees.

Olaf scurried away and found himself in a small clearing by a brook. He knew he’d make it somewhere safe! He had been willing to face his fears, and look what had happened! Olaf believed that by looking down at his reflection in the water, he would feel even better. What he saw was a distorted, rippling version of himself, but Olaf remained secure. Even with the creepy face and eyes staring back at him, nothing could shake his courage—until that image was replaced by a big scary horse’s face!

“AAAAAAHHHHHH!” Olaf screamed in terror. Then a nearby bush burst into flames.

Olaf continued screaming until he ran out of breath, not even noticing that the fire in the bush went out the moment he stopped screaming.

Everything went back to normal, and he reminded himself that in a few years, he would find explanations for all these strange things. Olaf wasn’t even worried when he saw trees deeper in the forest bending to the ground as if they were pushed by a heavy wind.

“This is fine,” he said confidently.

But it wasn’t. The heavy wind found him and swept him up into the roaring storm—one piece at a time.

奥拉夫兴高采烈地在森林里探索。

他甚至没意识到自己迷路了。

他大步往前走，以为朋友们就紧跟在身后。“还有谁觉得……我们被盯上了。

有人吗？

没人？”奥拉夫转过身，只看见森林。“就我一个。”他往树林深处张望，想确认确实没人和他在一起。“安娜？

艾莎？

斯文？

萨曼莎？”他笑起来，“我根本不认识什么萨曼莎。”他笑着笑着，一阵风忽然吹到他屁股上。“哇哦，”他惊讶地说。

他又转了一圈，想找出那个捣蛋鬼。

什么也没看见，雪人只是耸了耸肩。

头顶的树发出噼啪声，一堆叶子哗啦砸在他头上。

奥拉夫把叶子拨开，从嘴里揪出一片。“这很正常，”他说。

一块石头像凭空冒出来似的从灌木丛里飞出，奥拉夫转身要继续走时，被它绊了一跤，脸朝下摔在地上。

一股热水喷涌而出，把他顶得重新站了起来。

这越来越诡异了，他想。

头顶的树枝轻轻颤动，叶子沙沙作响——有什么大个儿的东西在枝叶间匆匆跑过。

奥拉夫迅速转身看身后。“那是什么？”他问。

他面前地上张着一个大洞，他赶紧停下，没摔进去。

他小心地朝那个仿佛无底的深坑里望去。“萨曼莎？”他喊道，声音回荡着，渐渐消失在虚无中。

没有回应。

奥拉夫紧张地往后退。

雪人相信，虽然此刻无法解释，但总有一天会真相大白。

他只需要再长大一点、再懂事一点。

到那时，回想起现在发生在自己身上的一切怪事，他就会明白，那其实都再正常不过。

一阵滋滋声引起了他的注意，他及时转过头，正好看见一团冒着烟的火苗烧穿苔藓，朝他冲来。

他不知道那是什么，但他知道准没好事。

他猛地往旁边一扑躲开。

奥拉夫继续走，很快来到森林中一处阴暗的地方，四周爬满藤蔓，枝条扭曲纠缠。

他劝自己，现在感到的恐惧，过几年再看会显得很幼稚。

无论他往哪儿看，灌木丛里都瞪着一双双诡异、一眨不眨的白眼睛。

他努力什么也不去想，只管讲礼貌。“借过，”他说着，从小树丛里退了出来。

奥拉夫慌忙跑开，发现自己来到一条小溪旁的小空地。

他知道自己一定能到达安全的地方！

他本来已经鼓起勇气面对恐惧了，结果看看发生了什么！

奥拉夫相信，低头看看水中自己的倒影，心情会好一些。

他看到的是扭曲、荡漾的自己，但奥拉夫依旧安心。

哪怕那张诡异的脸和那双眼睛正回瞪着他，也没什么能动摇他的勇气——直到那影像被一张巨大恐怖的马脸取代！“啊啊啊啊啊啊！”奥拉夫惊恐地尖叫。

接着，旁边一丛灌木猛地燃起火焰。

奥拉夫一直尖叫到没气为止，甚至没注意到，他一停下尖叫，灌木里的火就灭了。

一切恢复了正常，他提醒自己，再过几年，这些怪事都能解释得通。

奥拉夫看见森林深处的大树像被一阵猛风推着弯向地面，竟也不慌。“这没关系，”他自信地说。

可事实并非如此。

那阵猛风找到了他，把他卷进了咆哮的风暴——一次卷走他一块身体零件。

sentences.en: Olaf was happy to explore the forest.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫兴高采烈地在森林里探索。

sentences.en: He didn’t even know he was lost.
sentences.zh: 他甚至没意识到自己迷路了。

sentences.en: He marched along, thinking his friends were right behind him. “Anyone else feel like we’re being watched.
sentences.zh: 他大步往前走，以为朋友们就紧跟在身后。“还有谁觉得……我们被盯上了。

sentences.en: Anyone?
sentences.zh: 有人吗？

sentences.en: No one?” Olaf turned around and saw only the forest. “I’m alone.” He peered deeper into the woods, trying to confirm that no one was with him. “Anna?
sentences.zh: 没人？”奥拉夫转过身，只看见森林。“就我一个。”他往树林深处张望，想确认确实没人和他在一起。“安娜？

sentences.en: Elsa?
sentences.zh: 艾莎？

sentences.en: Sven?
sentences.zh: 斯文？

sentences.en: Samantha?” He laughed. “I don’t even know a Samantha.” He continued laughing until a gust of wind blew at his backside. “Whoa,” he said in surprise.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎？”他笑起来，“我根本不认识什么萨曼莎。”他笑着笑着，一阵风忽然吹到他屁股上。“哇哦，”他惊讶地说。

sentences.en: He spun around again, searching for the culprit.
sentences.zh: 他又转了一圈，想找出那个捣蛋鬼。

sentences.en: Seeing nothing, the snowman simply shrugged.
sentences.zh: 什么也没看见，雪人只是耸了耸肩。

sentences.en: The trees above him crackled, and a pile of leaves crashed on his head.
sentences.zh: 头顶的树发出噼啪声，一堆叶子哗啦砸在他头上。

sentences.en: Olaf pushed the leaves off and picked one out of his mouth. “That’s normal,” he said.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫把叶子拨开，从嘴里揪出一片。“这很正常，”他说。

sentences.en: A rock flew out of the bushes as if from nowhere, and when Olaf turned to continue on his journey, he tripped over it and landed on his face.
sentences.zh: 一块石头像凭空冒出来似的从灌木丛里飞出，奥拉夫转身要继续走时，被它绊了一跤，脸朝下摔在地上。

sentences.en: A hot gush of water pushed him back up to his feet.
sentences.zh: 一股热水喷涌而出，把他顶得重新站了起来。

sentences.en: This is getting weird, he thought.
sentences.zh: 这越来越诡异了，他想。

sentences.en: Tree limbs shimmied above his head, rattling the leaves as something large scampered through them.
sentences.zh: 头顶的树枝轻轻颤动，叶子沙沙作响——有什么大个儿的东西在枝叶间匆匆跑过。

sentences.en: Olaf turned quickly to look behind him. “What was that?” he asked.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫迅速转身看身后。“那是什么？”他问。

sentences.en: A large hole gaped in the ground before him, and he quickly stopped before he fell in.
sentences.zh: 他面前地上张着一个大洞，他赶紧停下，没摔进去。

sentences.en: He cautiously looked into what seemed to be a bottomless pit. “Samantha?” he called, his voice echoing as it faded into the nothingness.
sentences.zh: 他小心地朝那个仿佛无底的深坑里望去。“萨曼莎？”他喊道，声音回荡着，渐渐消失在虚无中。

sentences.en: No response.
sentences.zh: 没有回应。

sentences.en: Olaf backed away nervously.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫紧张地往后退。

sentences.en: The snowman was confident that although there was no explanation at the moment, there would be one day.
sentences.zh: 雪人相信，虽然此刻无法解释，但总有一天会真相大白。

sentences.en: He just needed to be a bit older and wiser.
sentences.zh: 他只需要再长大一点、再懂事一点。

sentences.en: Then, when he thought back about everything strange that was happening to him now, he would realize it had all been completely normal.
sentences.zh: 到那时，回想起现在发生在自己身上的一切怪事，他就会明白，那其实都再正常不过。

sentences.en: A sizzling sound caught his attention, and he turned his head just in time to see a smoking blaze burn through the moss and race toward him.
sentences.zh: 一阵滋滋声引起了他的注意，他及时转过头，正好看见一团冒着烟的火苗烧穿苔藓，朝他冲来。

sentences.en: He didn’t know what it was, but he knew it couldn’t be good.
sentences.zh: 他不知道那是什么，但他知道准没好事。

sentences.en: He dove out of the way.
sentences.zh: 他猛地往旁边一扑躲开。

sentences.en: Olaf kept moving and soon reached a dark part of the forest, overgrown with vines and twisted branches all around him.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫继续走，很快来到森林中一处阴暗的地方，四周爬满藤蔓，枝条扭曲纠缠。

sentences.en: He convinced himself that the fear he felt would seem childish in a couple of years.
sentences.zh: 他劝自己，现在感到的恐惧，过几年再看会显得很幼稚。

sentences.en: Creepy, unblinking white eyes peered out of the bushes everywhere he looked.
sentences.zh: 无论他往哪儿看，灌木丛里都瞪着一双双诡异、一眨不眨的白眼睛。

sentences.en: He tried not to think about anything but using his manners. “Excuse me,” he said, backing out of the small grove of trees.
sentences.zh: 他努力什么也不去想，只管讲礼貌。“借过，”他说着，从小树丛里退了出来。

sentences.en: Olaf scurried away and found himself in a small clearing by a brook.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫慌忙跑开，发现自己来到一条小溪旁的小空地。

sentences.en: He knew he’d make it somewhere safe!
sentences.zh: 他知道自己一定能到达安全的地方！

sentences.en: He had been willing to face his fears, and look what had happened!
sentences.zh: 他本来已经鼓起勇气面对恐惧了，结果看看发生了什么！

sentences.en: Olaf believed that by looking down at his reflection in the water, he would feel even better.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫相信，低头看看水中自己的倒影，心情会好一些。

sentences.en: What he saw was a distorted, rippling version of himself, but Olaf remained secure.
sentences.zh: 他看到的是扭曲、荡漾的自己，但奥拉夫依旧安心。

sentences.en: Even with the creepy face and eyes staring back at him, nothing could shake his courage—until that image was replaced by a big scary horse’s face! “AAAAAAHHHHHH!” Olaf screamed in terror.
sentences.zh: 哪怕那张诡异的脸和那双眼睛正回瞪着他，也没什么能动摇他的勇气——直到那影像被一张巨大恐怖的马脸取代！“啊啊啊啊啊啊！”奥拉夫惊恐地尖叫。

sentences.en: Then a nearby bush burst into flames.
sentences.zh: 接着，旁边一丛灌木猛地燃起火焰。

sentences.en: Olaf continued screaming until he ran out of breath, not even noticing that the fire in the bush went out the moment he stopped screaming.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫一直尖叫到没气为止，甚至没注意到，他一停下尖叫，灌木里的火就灭了。

sentences.en: Everything went back to normal, and he reminded himself that in a few years, he would find explanations for all these strange things.
sentences.zh: 一切恢复了正常，他提醒自己，再过几年，这些怪事都能解释得通。

sentences.en: Olaf wasn’t even worried when he saw trees deeper in the forest bending to the ground as if they were pushed by a heavy wind. “This is fine,” he said confidently.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫看见森林深处的大树像被一阵猛风推着弯向地面，竟也不慌。“这没关系，”他自信地说。

sentences.en: But it wasn’t.

sentences.en: The heavy wind found him and swept him up into the roaring storm—one piece at a time.
sentences.zh: 那阵猛风找到了他，把他卷进了咆哮的风暴——一次卷走他一块身体零件。

chapters.title: 第18章
chapters.en:
Elsa, Anna, Kristoff, and Sven were able to track Olaf down when they heard him scream. They rushed toward the whirlwind, shouting for their friend.

But the wild winds wanted more than the icy man. Everyone else was swept up into the vortex with him. The gusts whipped their bodies around in circles, arms grabbing and legs kicking as they tried to find something stable to hold on to. Anna and Elsa reached for each other as Olaf’s body parts swung around them—first his midsection, then his head. “Hey, guys!” Olaf said, and then his feet passed, too. “Meet the Wind Spirit.”

“Coming through,” Kristoff said as he swept past Elsa.

Anna’s skirt blew over her head and her hands were pulled from Elsa’s grasp. Anna spun wildly out of control.

“I think I’m going to be sick!” she said.

“I’d hold your hair back, but I can’t find my arms!” Olaf shouted as he sailed past her again.

Kristoff and Sven slammed into each other. They all soared higher into the vortex, flailing and flapping, grumbling and groaning. Their bodies moved forward and back, up and down. Everyone looked like they were doing a ridiculous dance.

But it wasn’t just the friends who were caught in the whirlwind—the debris that had been on the forest floor was everywhere. One large tree branch soared through the vortex, headed straight for Anna. Elsa threw out her hands and hit the branch with an icy blast right before it hit her sister. The queen’s magic knocked the branch free of the wind’s grasp. After that, things seemed to change. The vortex centered itself on Elsa’s hands.

“Hey, stop!” she said, just before it pushed the others, including all of Olaf’s parts.

Kristoff landed on a mound of star moss, which cushioned his fall. Olaf’s body parts fell back together in one piece on the end of log. But there was a problem. They were in the wrong order.

Sven dropped out of the sky on the other end of the log, and when he did, Olaf’s parts flew back up into the air. When they came down this time, everything was exactly where it was supposed to be!

Anna fell with a splash into the brook Olaf had discovered earlier. But before she could get her bearings, a small ripple that turned into a wave rushed toward her. Anna was so frantic to get back to her sister that she didn’t even notice. She jumped to her feet and moved to the bank of the brook. When she emerged on the shoreline, she began to run.

“Elsa!” she called out, never noticing watchful eyes staring at her from the crest of the small wave. “Let her go!” Anna demanded of the Wind Spirit.

Anna arrived near the vortex as Kristoff climbed out of the star moss, trying to pull off the green bits of shrubbery that clung to him.

“Anna, be careful!” he called. They tried to get close to the vortex, but it wouldn’t let them in—it threw them back.

“That’s my sister!” Anna shouted.

Elsa could see her friends through the rushing winds, and she knew they were doing their best to help her. She also knew she had only one option left as the vortex swirled around her, refusing to let her out. Elsa moved her hands away from each other, as far as she could, and made a steady stream of snow to mix with the wind.

The vortex thickened with the snow’s weight, which slowed the spin Elsa was in. She was sure she heard human voices, the sounds of animals, and echoes of the forest around her as the spinning continued to slow.

“Prince Agnarr!” she heard a man yell.

She closed her eyes and curled up as the slushy, ribbony whiteness overtook her. Without warning, Elsa threw open her arms, releasing all her magic, flooding the vortex with her power.

“For Arendelle,” a deep voice intoned as a blast of snow filled the air with white.
chapters.zh:
艾莎、安娜、克斯托夫和斯文听到奥拉夫的尖叫，循声找到了他。

他们冲向那股旋风，呼喊着朋友的名字。

可狂野的风要的远不止那个冰雪人。

其他人也和他一起被卷进了漩涡。

一阵阵疾风把他们的身体甩着打转，大家手抓脚蹬，想抓住什么稳当的东西。

安娜和艾莎伸手想抓住彼此，奥拉夫的身体零件在他们周围飞旋——先是他中段，接着是脑袋。“嘿，各位！”奥拉夫说，随后他的脚也飞了过去。“来认识一下风灵。”“借过，”克斯托夫掠过艾莎身边时说。

安娜的裙子被吹到头上，双手也从艾莎手里挣脱了。

安娜失控地疯狂旋转。“我快吐了！”她说。“我很想帮你把头发拢起来，可我找不到自己的胳膊了！”奥拉夫又一次从她身边飞过时喊道。

克斯托夫和斯文撞在了一起。

他们在漩涡里越升越高，乱挥乱扑，嘟嘟囔囔，唉声叹气。

他们的身体前前后后、上上下下地翻飞。

每个人都像在跳一支滑稽的舞。

可被困在旋风里的不止朋友们——森林地面上的一切残枝败叶也到处翻飞。

一根粗大的树枝从漩涡中掠过，直冲安娜而去。

艾莎伸出双手，在树枝撞到妹妹前一刻用冰霜一击将它击退。

女王的魔法让树枝脱离了风的掌控。

之后，情形似乎变了。

漩涡把中心对准了艾莎的双手。“嘿，停下！”她说，就在它把其他人——包括奥拉夫所有零件——推开之前。

克斯托夫落在一堆星状苔藓上，苔藓缓冲了他的坠落。

奥拉夫的身体零件在一段木头的一端重新拼成了一整块。

可出了个问题。

它们拼的顺序不对。

斯文从天上落在木头的另一端，他一落地，奥拉夫的零件又被弹回了空中。

这一次落下时，所有零件都回到了该在的位置！

安娜扑通一声掉进了奥拉夫早先发现的那条小溪。

可她还没站稳，一圈小涟漪就化成一道波浪朝她涌来。

安娜一心只想回到姐姐身边，连这都没注意到。

她跳起来，朝溪岸挪去。

她一上岸就拔腿奔跑。“艾莎！”她喊着，全然没发现浪尖上有双警惕的眼睛正盯着她。“放了她！”安娜对风灵喝道。

安娜赶到漩涡附近时，克斯托夫正从星状苔藓里爬出来，想扯掉粘在身上的绿色碎枝叶。“安娜，小心！”他喊道。

他们想靠近漩涡，可它不让他们进——反而把他们弹开。“那是我姐姐！”安娜喊道。

艾莎透过疾风看见了朋友们，知道他们正尽全力帮自己。

她也知道，漩涡围着她打转，不肯放她出去，自己只剩一个选择了。

艾莎把双手尽量向两边分开，让一股稳定的雪花之流与风交融。

雪花加重了漩涡，也减慢了艾莎旋转的速度。

旋转越来越慢，她确信自己听见了人声、野兽声，还有森林的回响。“安格瑞王子！”她听见一个男人喊道。

她闭上眼睛蜷起身子，那黏糊糊、如缎带般的白茫茫将她吞没。

艾莎毫无预兆地张开双臂，释放出全部魔力，让力量灌满整个漩涡。“为了阿伦黛尔，”一个低沉的声音庄严地说道，一阵雪暴把空气染成白茫茫一片。

sentences.zh: 安娜一心只想回到姐姐身边，连这都没注意到。

sentences.en: She jumped to her feet and moved to the bank of the brook.
sentences.zh: 她跳起来，朝溪岸挪去。

sentences.en: When she emerged on the shoreline, she began to run. “Elsa!” she called out, never noticing watchful eyes staring at her from the crest of the small wave. “Let her go!” Anna demanded of the Wind Spirit.
sentences.zh: 她一上岸就拔腿奔跑。“艾莎！”她喊着，全然没发现浪尖上有双警惕的眼睛正盯着她。“放了她！”安娜对风灵喝道。

sentences.en: Anna arrived near the vortex as Kristoff climbed out of the star moss, trying to pull off the green bits of shrubbery that clung to him. “Anna, be careful!” he called.
sentences.zh: 安娜赶到漩涡附近时，克斯托夫正从星状苔藓里爬出来，想扯掉粘在身上的绿色碎枝叶。“安娜，小心！”他喊道。

sentences.en: They tried to get close to the vortex, but it wouldn’t let them in—it threw them back. “That’s my sister!” Anna shouted.
sentences.zh: 他们想靠近漩涡，可它不让他们进——反而把他们弹开。“那是我姐姐！”安娜喊道。

sentences.en: Elsa could see her friends through the rushing winds, and she knew they were doing their best to help her.
sentences.zh: 艾莎透过疾风看见了朋友们，知道他们正尽全力帮自己。

sentences.en: She also knew she had only one option left as the vortex swirled around her, refusing to let her out.
sentences.zh: 她也知道，漩涡围着她打转，不肯放她出去，自己只剩一个选择了。

sentences.en: Elsa moved her hands away from each other, as far as she could, and made a steady stream of snow to mix with the wind.
sentences.zh: 艾莎把双手尽量向两边分开，让一股稳定的雪花之流与风交融。

sentences.en: The vortex thickened with the snow’s weight, which slowed the spin Elsa was in.
sentences.zh: 雪花加重了漩涡，也减慢了艾莎旋转的速度。

sentences.en: She was sure she heard human voices, the sounds of animals, and echoes of the forest around her as the spinning continued to slow. “Prince Agnarr!” she heard a man yell.
sentences.zh: 旋转越来越慢，她确信自己听见了人声、野兽声，还有森林的回响。“安格瑞王子！”她听见一个男人喊道。

sentences.en: She closed her eyes and curled up as the slushy, ribbony whiteness overtook her.
sentences.zh: 她闭上眼睛蜷起身子，那黏糊糊、如缎带般的白茫茫将她吞没。

sentences.en: Without warning, Elsa threw open her arms, releasing all her magic, flooding the vortex with her power. “For Arendelle,” a deep voice intoned as a blast of snow filled the air with white.
sentences.zh: 艾莎毫无预兆地张开双臂，释放出全部魔力，让力量灌满整个漩涡。“为了阿伦黛尔，”一个低沉的声音庄严地说道，一阵雪暴把空气染成白茫茫一片。

chapters.title: 第19章
chapters.en:
The vortex had disappeared and peace was restored to the Enchanted Forest. As the snow slowly fell from the air, Anna looked around frantically for her sister. Then she saw Elsa standing in what looked to be a garden, surrounded by beautiful sculptures made from ice. The queen looked from one sculpture to the next, stunned. Anna went to her side, taking Elsa’s hand.

“Are you okay?” she asked.

Elsa squeezed her hand. “I’m fine,” she said.

“What are these?” Kristoff asked when he arrived. Awestruck, he circled the ice sculptures with the rest of the group, looking closely at the detail, the delicacy. As an ice harvester, he was a big fan of anything made of ice.

“They look like moments in time,” Elsa said softly.

Elsa’s words reminded Anna of something she had heard earlier. Anna turned to the snowman. “What’s that thing you say, Olaf?”

“Oh!” he replied. “My theory about advancing technology as both our savior and our doom?”

“No, not the…not that one,” Anna said. “The one about—”

“The one about cucumbers?” Olaf asked. He had read so many books and had learned so much, there were hundreds of things he had talked about to anyone who would listen.

“No, the thing about water,” Anna said, narrowing it down.

“Oh, yeah,” Olaf said. “Water has memory. The water that makes up you and me has passed through at least four or five people or animals before us.”

Sven’s head jerked up at Olaf’s statement. His eyes were wide, his muzzle twisted in what appeared to be disgust. He glanced at the ice sculpture he had been licking and spit on the ground.

“It remembers everything,” Olaf finished.

The wind rustled the leaves, coming from nowhere and sweeping around Olaf. “Oh, the wind’s back,” he said. “I think I’ll name you…Gale.”

Everyone braced themselves as the wind moved around Anna and then slipped up the leg of Kristoff’s pants.

“Ooh, ah,” Kristoff called, dancing around a bit, hoping it would leave him alone. “Whoa, get out of there.”

The Wind Spirit twirled in Anna’s hair and made her clothing flutter as if it was examining her. “Oh, aren’t you curious….”

Then it moved on to Elsa and swept her up in its grip. “Oh!” she gasped. But she quickly realized the Wind Spirit was no longer being aggressive.

The group immediately stood around her, ready to protect her.

“I’m okay. I’m okay,” she told them.

Gale held Elsa aloft for only a few moments before setting her gently on her feet. Elsa smiled. The Wind Spirit’s energy had lifted her mood and made her feel ready to take on any obstacle that came her way.

“Did you want me to make these?” Elsa asked. The wind ruffled her skirts while she looked at the nearest ice sculpture.

But Gale didn’t answer. The Wind Spirit swirled around the sisters, then swept down through a small opening in the trees. Aloft in its breeze were leaves of red and orange hues, making it easy for the group to follow where it led. Anna passed though the opening with the others. Gale had brought them to an ice sculpture that was set apart from the rest.

The sculpture depicted a couple swept up in a windstorm—a young girl helping a young boy.

Anna and Elsa approached the sculpture in disbelief. They moved around it, looking closely from every angle.

“Father?” Anna asked softly, recognizing the elements of the sculpture’s face. “That’s Father.”
chapters.zh:
漩涡消散了，魔法森林重归宁静。

雪花缓缓飘落，安娜焦急地四下寻找姐姐。

接着她看见艾莎站在一处像是花园的地方，周围环绕着美丽的冰雕。

女王一座接一座地看着冰雕，惊呆了。

安娜走到她身边，握住艾莎的手。“你没事吧？”她问。

艾莎握紧她的手。“我没事，”她说。“这些是什么？”克斯托夫赶到时问。

他满心敬畏，和众人一起绕着冰雕打转，仔细端详其中的细节与精巧。

作为一个采冰人，他格外偏爱一切冰做的事物。“它们像是一个个凝固的瞬间，”艾莎轻声说。

艾莎的话让安娜想起早先听过的一句话。

安娜转向雪人。“你常说那句什么来着，奥拉夫？”“哦！”他答道，“是说科技进步既是我们的救星也是我们的末日那个理论吗？”“不，不是那个……不是那个，”安娜说，“是那个关于——”“关于黄瓜的那个？”奥拉夫问。

他读过太多书、懂得太多，跟谁都能滔滔不绝说上几百样事。“不，是关于水的那句，”安娜把范围缩小。“哦，对，”奥拉夫说，“水是有记忆的。

构成你我的水，在我们之前至少已经流过四五个人或动物。”斯文听到这话猛地抬起头。

他瞪圆了眼睛，嘴脸皱成一团，一副嫌恶的表情。

他瞥了一眼自己刚才在舔的冰雕，朝地上啐了一口。“它什么都记得，”奥拉夫把话说完。

风沙沙地吹动树叶，不知从哪儿冒出来，绕着奥拉夫打转。“哦，风又回来了，”他说，“我想给你起个名字……就叫盖尔吧。”风绕着安娜转了一圈，又顺着陆克斯托夫的裤腿钻了进去，大家都绷紧了神经。“哎哟，啊，”克斯托夫叫着，扭动几下身子，希望它别缠着自己。“哇，快出来。”风灵在安娜头发里打转，吹得她衣衫飘动，像是在打量她。“哦，你不好奇吗……”接着它又挪到艾莎身边，一把将她卷了起来。“哦！”她倒吸一口气。

但她很快意识到，风灵不再有攻击性了。

大家立刻围到她身边，准备保护她。“我没事。

我没事，”她告诉大家。

盖尔只把艾莎托在半空片刻，便轻轻把她放回地上。

艾莎笑了。

风灵的力量让她心情大好，觉得自己能应对任何挡在前面的障碍。“这些是你希望我雕出来的吗？”艾莎问。

风轻轻撩起她的裙摆，她正望着最近的一座冰雕。

但盖尔没有回答。

风灵在姐妹俩身边打着旋，然后顺着树木间一个小缺口俯冲下去。

它的微风托着红红黄黄的树叶，让大家很容易跟上前去。

安娜和其他人一起穿过那个缺口。

盖尔把他们带到了一座与众不同的冰雕前。

雕像刻画的是一对被风暴卷起的人——一个少女正扶着一个少年。

安娜和艾莎难以置信地走近那座雕像。

她们围着雕像转，从每个角度细细端详。“父亲？”安娜轻声问，认出了雕像脸上的某些特征，“那是父亲。”
