chapters.title: 第20章
chapters.en:
Elsa leaned closer to the young boy and nodded. It was definitely her father. She turned her focus to the girl holding him. There was something special about her, too.

“This girl,” she said.

“She’s saving him…,” Olaf said.

“She’s Northuldra,” Kristoff added, recognizing that she wasn’t dressed in typical Arendellian clothing.

Suddenly, a whirring sound swished from the trees closest to them. Olaf squealed and hid behind Anna. He reached into her satchel and pulled Iduna’s scarf out far enough that he could wrap it over his head and shoulders, as if it could conceal him from whatever was coming their way.

“What is that?” Anna asked.

“Olaf, get behind me,” Elsa ordered.

Loud bangs joined the whirring, creating a rhythmic beat. The noise filled the air, escalating in volume and tempo.

The bushes in front of them, next to the sculpture, rustled. Anna had had enough. Since they’d entered the Enchanted Forest, their experience had been anything but enchanting. Stepping forward, she reached toward another ice sculpture and broke off a sword.

“What are you going to do with that?” Kristoff asked as the whirring intensified.

“I have no idea,” Anna said. But then she made a decision. Holding the ice sword in front of her, she marched toward the bushes that had since stopped moving.

With one swing, Anna cut the offensive bush down the middle. It was time to reveal whatever danger lurked within! Then she saw a group of people crouched low to the ground. Behind them stood a group of reindeer. Are they Northuldra? Anna thought as she stared at their unfamiliar clothes.

THUMP!

Anna spun at the loud sound. More Northuldra dropped from the trees. Each person was swinging a round object on a string, which she saw was making the whirring noise.

“Lower your weapon,” a young woman commanded. She was one of the Northuldra who’d dropped from the trees. With a raised staff, she moved toward Anna and her friends. The other Northuldra moved behind her.

Swords slammed against shields. Five newcomers appeared, looking different from the Northuldra, their swords at the ready.

“And YOU lower yours,” the soldier in charge commanded the Northuldra. He stood strong in a uniform that showed the wear and tear of many years. But it was still clearly an Arendellian uniform. He looked familiar to Anna.

“Arendellian soldiers?” Anna asked her friends, wondering if it was possible. She had always assumed that when the mist had closed around the forest, the only people who’d been trapped within had been their enemies, the Northuldra.

An older woman seemed to come from nowhere just then. She stood at the soldier’s side, holding a staff. The soldier closed his eyes briefly, then opened them again and stared straight ahead.

“Threatening my people again, Lieutenant?” the woman said.

He regarded her like an old neighbor he had been squabbling with for years.

“Invading my dance space again, Yelana?” he responded.

The two continued to bicker like old enemies, or friends—it was hard to tell which.

“Why does that soldier look so familiar?” Anna wondered aloud. She stared at the Arendellian soldier in charge and stepped forward with the ice sword still in her hand.

A soldier noticed Anna moving toward them and shouted, “Look out, Lieutenant!”

The lieutenant spun his shield, trying to knock Yelana’s staff away from his side. But Yelana countered his move.

“Get the sword!” he ordered his soldiers.

They charged Elsa, Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven. The Northuldra were close behind.

Elsa blasted her power at the ground to create a slick, glassy coating around her group. The soldiers and the Northuldra slipped and slid until they all fell onto their backs and rear ends.

The lieutenant crashed next to Yelana. “That was magic,” he said in shock. “Did you see that?”

“Of course I saw it,” she replied. She’d hidden her surprise.

Elsa and her friends stared at the two groups, now sprawled on the ground.

Anna leaned into her sister. “You chose a nice, cold greeting,” she said.

“They’ve been trapped in here this whole time?” Kristoff whispered in disbelief.

“What do we do now?” Elsa whispered back.
chapters.zh:
艾莎朝那少年凑近一些，点了点头。

那确实是她的父亲。

她把注意力转向扶着他的那个女孩。

这个女孩也不一般。“这个女孩，”她说，“她在救他……”奥拉夫说。“她是北地人，”克斯托夫补充道，认出她的衣着不是阿伦黛尔常见款式。

忽然，一阵呼啸声从离他们最近的树丛里响起。

奥拉夫尖叫一声，躲到安娜身后。

他伸手探进安娜的挎包，把伊杜娜的围巾扯出来，足够盖住头和肩膀，好像这样就能把自己藏在来犯之物面前。“那是什么？”安娜问。“奥拉夫，躲我身后，”艾莎命令道。

响亮的撞击声加入呼啸，形成有节奏的鼓点。

喧闹声充斥空气，音量和节奏都越来越强。

他们前方、雕像旁的灌木丛沙沙作响。

安娜受够了。

自从进了魔法森林，他们的遭遇可一点都不“魔法”——一点都不美妙。

她上前一步，朝另一座冰雕伸手，掰下一把冰剑。“你拿那个要干什么？”呼啸声越来越急，克斯托夫问。“我也不知道，”安娜说。

但她随即下了决心。

她把冰剑横在身前，朝那丛已经不动了的灌木走去。

安娜一剑挥下，把那丛讨厌的灌木从中间劈开。

是时候让藏在里面的危险现形了！

接着她看见一群人正低低地蹲在地上。

他们身后站着一群驯鹿。

他们是北地人吗？

安娜盯着他们陌生的衣着，心中暗想。

咚！

安娜被这巨响惊得转过身。

更多北地人从树上跃下。

每个人都在甩动系在绳上的圆形物件，她看清了，那呼啸声正是它发出的。“放下武器，”一个年轻女子命令道。

她是从树上跃下的北地人之一。

她高举着手杖，朝安娜和朋友们逼近。

其他北地人跟在她身后。

刀剑撞上盾牌，哐当作响。

五个新面孔出现了，模样与北地人不同，剑已出鞘。“你，也放下你的，”带头的士兵对北地人下令。

他身姿笔挺，穿着一件显出多年风霜的制服。

但那显然是一身阿伦黛尔制服。

安娜觉得他面熟。“阿伦黛尔的士兵？”安娜问朋友们，心里怀疑这是否可能。

她一直以为，迷雾合拢时被困在森林里的，只有他们的敌人——北地人。

就在这时，一位年长的妇人仿佛凭空出现。

她站在士兵身旁，手执一根手杖。

士兵短暂地闭了下眼，又睁开直视前方。“又来威胁我的人了，中尉？”妇人说。

他看她的眼神，像在打量一个吵了多年的老邻居。“又闯进我的舞场了，耶拉娜？”他回敬道。

两人继续斗嘴，像老对头，又像老朋友——分不清到底是哪种。“那个士兵怎么这么眼熟？”安娜大声纳闷。

她盯着那个带头的阿伦黛尔士兵，手里仍握着冰剑走上前。

一名士兵注意到安娜逼近，喊道：“小心，中尉！”中尉抡起盾牌，想挡开耶拉娜戳向他身侧的手杖。

但耶拉娜化解了他的动作。“夺下那把剑！”他命令手下的士兵。

他们朝艾莎、安娜、奥拉夫、克斯托夫和斯文冲来。

北地人紧随其后。

艾莎将魔力击向地面，在同伴四周凝出一层光滑如镜的冰面。

士兵和北地人脚下一滑再滑，最后全都仰面朝天、屁股着地摔了下去。

中尉摔在耶拉娜身旁。“那是魔法，”他震惊地说，“你看见了吗？”“我当然看见了，”她答道。

她把惊讶藏了起来。

艾莎和朋友们盯着地上那两群人——此刻都四脚朝天躺着。

安娜靠向姐姐。“你选了个挺冷——挺凉快的见面礼，”她说。“他们一直被困在这里？”克斯托夫难以置信地低语。“我们现在怎么办？”艾莎低声回问。

sentences.en: Elsa leaned closer to the young boy and nodded.
sentences.zh: 艾莎朝那少年凑近一些，点了点头。

sentences.en: It was definitely her father.
sentences.zh: 那确实是她的父亲。

sentences.en: She turned her focus to the girl holding him.
sentences.zh: 她把注意力转向扶着他的那个女孩。

sentences.en: There was something special about her, too. “This girl,” she said. “She’s saving him…,” Olaf said. “She’s Northuldra,” Kristoff added, recognizing that she wasn’t dressed in typical Arendellian clothing.
sentences.zh: 这个女孩也不一般。“这个女孩，”她说，“她在救他……”奥拉夫说。“她是北地人，”克斯托夫补充道，认出她的衣着不是阿伦黛尔常见款式。

sentences.en: Suddenly, a whirring sound swished from the trees closest to them.
sentences.zh: 忽然，一阵呼啸声从离他们最近的树丛里响起。

sentences.en: Olaf squealed and hid behind Anna.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫尖叫一声，躲到安娜身后。

sentences.en: He reached into her satchel and pulled Iduna’s scarf out far enough that he could wrap it over his head and shoulders, as if it could conceal him from whatever was coming their way. “What is that?” Anna asked. “Olaf, get behind me,” Elsa ordered.
sentences.zh: 他伸手探进安娜的挎包，把伊杜娜的围巾扯出来，足够盖住头和肩膀，好像这样就能把自己藏在来犯之物面前。“那是什么？”安娜问。“奥拉夫，躲我身后，”艾莎命令道。

sentences.en: Loud bangs joined the whirring, creating a rhythmic beat.
sentences.zh: 响亮的撞击声加入呼啸，形成有节奏的鼓点。

sentences.en: The noise filled the air, escalating in volume and tempo.
sentences.zh: 喧闹声充斥空气，音量和节奏都越来越强。

sentences.en: The bushes in front of them, next to the sculpture, rustled.
sentences.zh: 他们前方、雕像旁的灌木丛沙沙作响。

sentences.en: Anna had had enough.
sentences.zh: 安娜受够了。

sentences.en: Since they’d entered the Enchanted Forest, their experience had been anything but enchanting.
sentences.zh: 自从进了魔法森林，他们的遭遇可一点都不“魔法”——一点都不美妙。

sentences.en: Stepping forward, she reached toward another ice sculpture and broke off a sword. “What are you going to do with that?” Kristoff asked as the whirring intensified. “I have no idea,” Anna said.
sentences.zh: 她上前一步，朝另一座冰雕伸手，掰下一把冰剑。“你拿那个要干什么？”呼啸声越来越急，克斯托夫问。“我也不知道，”安娜说。

sentences.en: But then she made a decision.
sentences.zh: 但她随即下了决心。

sentences.en: Holding the ice sword in front of her, she marched toward the bushes that had since stopped moving.
sentences.zh: 她把冰剑横在身前，朝那丛已经不动了的灌木走去。

sentences.en: With one swing, Anna cut the offensive bush down the middle.
sentences.zh: 安娜一剑挥下，把那丛讨厌的灌木从中间劈开。

sentences.en: It was time to reveal whatever danger lurked within!
sentences.zh: 是时候让藏在里面的危险现形了！

sentences.en: Then she saw a group of people crouched low to the ground.
sentences.zh: 接着她看见一群人正低低地蹲在地上。

sentences.en: Behind them stood a group of reindeer.
sentences.zh: 他们身后站着一群驯鹿。

sentences.en: Are they Northuldra?
sentences.zh: 他们是北地人吗？

sentences.en: Anna thought as she stared at their unfamiliar clothes.
sentences.zh: 安娜盯着他们陌生的衣着，心中暗想。

sentences.en: THUMP!
sentences.zh: 咚！

sentences.en: Anna spun at the loud sound.
sentences.zh: 安娜被这巨响惊得转过身。

sentences.en: More Northuldra dropped from the trees.
sentences.zh: 更多北地人从树上跃下。

sentences.en: Each person was swinging a round object on a string, which she saw was making the whirring noise. “Lower your weapon,” a young woman commanded.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在甩动系在绳上的圆形物件，她看清了，那呼啸声正是它发出的。“放下武器，”一个年轻女子命令道。

sentences.en: She was one of the Northuldra who’d dropped from the trees.
sentences.zh: 她是从树上跃下的北地人之一。

sentences.en: With a raised staff, she moved toward Anna and her friends.
sentences.zh: 她高举着手杖，朝安娜和朋友们逼近。

sentences.en: The other Northuldra moved behind her.
sentences.zh: 其他北地人跟在她身后。

sentences.en: Swords slammed against shields.
sentences.zh: 刀剑撞上盾牌，哐当作响。

sentences.en: Five newcomers appeared, looking different from the Northuldra, their swords at the ready. “And YOU lower yours,” the soldier in charge commanded the Northuldra.
sentences.zh: 五个新面孔出现了，模样与北地人不同，剑已出鞘。“你，也放下你的，”带头的士兵对北地人下令。

sentences.en: He stood strong in a uniform that showed the wear and tear of many years.
sentences.zh: 他身姿笔挺，穿着一件显出多年风霜的制服。

sentences.en: But it was still clearly an Arendellian uniform.
sentences.zh: 但那显然是一身阿伦黛尔制服。

sentences.en: He looked familiar to Anna. “Arendellian soldiers?” Anna asked her friends, wondering if it was possible.
sentences.zh: 安娜觉得他面熟。“阿伦黛尔的士兵？”安娜问朋友们，心里怀疑这是否可能。

sentences.en: She had always assumed that when the mist had closed around the forest, the only people who’d been trapped within had been their enemies, the Northuldra.
sentences.zh: 她一直以为，迷雾合拢时被困在森林里的，只有他们的敌人——北地人。

sentences.en: An older woman seemed to come from nowhere just then.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，一位年长的妇人仿佛凭空出现。

sentences.en: She stood at the soldier’s side, holding a staff.
sentences.zh: 她站在士兵身旁，手执一根手杖。

sentences.en: The soldier closed his eyes briefly, then opened them again and stared straight ahead. “Threatening my people again, Lieutenant?” the woman said.
sentences.zh: 士兵短暂地闭了下眼，又睁开直视前方。“又来威胁我的人了，中尉？”妇人说。

sentences.en: He regarded her like an old neighbor he had been squabbling with for years. “Invading my dance space again, Yelana?” he responded.
sentences.zh: 他看她的眼神，像在打量一个吵了多年的老邻居。“又闯进我的舞场了，耶拉娜？”他回敬道。

sentences.en: The two continued to bicker like old enemies, or friends—it was hard to tell which. “Why does that soldier look so familiar?” Anna wondered aloud.
sentences.zh: 两人继续斗嘴，像老对头，又像老朋友——分不清到底是哪种。“那个士兵怎么这么眼熟？”安娜大声纳闷。

sentences.en: She stared at the Arendellian soldier in charge and stepped forward with the ice sword still in her hand.
sentences.zh: 她盯着那个带头的阿伦黛尔士兵，手里仍握着冰剑走上前。

sentences.en: A soldier noticed Anna moving toward them and shouted, “Look out, Lieutenant!” The lieutenant spun his shield, trying to knock Yelana’s staff away from his side.
sentences.zh: 一名士兵注意到安娜逼近，喊道：“小心，中尉！”中尉抡起盾牌，想挡开耶拉娜戳向他身侧的手杖。

sentences.en: But Yelana countered his move. “Get the sword!” he ordered his soldiers.
sentences.zh: 但耶拉娜化解了他的动作。“夺下那把剑！”他命令手下的士兵。

sentences.en: They charged Elsa, Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven.
sentences.zh: 他们朝艾莎、安娜、奥拉夫、克斯托夫和斯文冲来。

sentences.en: The Northuldra were close behind.
sentences.zh: 北地人紧随其后。

sentences.en: Elsa blasted her power at the ground to create a slick, glassy coating around her group.
sentences.zh: 艾莎将魔力击向地面，在同伴四周凝出一层光滑如镜的冰面。

sentences.en: The soldiers and the Northuldra slipped and slid until they all fell onto their backs and rear ends.
sentences.zh: 士兵和北地人脚下一滑再滑，最后全都仰面朝天、屁股着地摔了下去。

sentences.en: The lieutenant crashed next to Yelana. “That was magic,” he said in shock. “Did you see that?” “Of course I saw it,” she replied.
sentences.zh: 中尉摔在耶拉娜身旁。“那是魔法，”他震惊地说，“你看见了吗？”“我当然看见了，”她答道。

sentences.en: She’d hidden her surprise.
sentences.zh: 她把惊讶藏了起来。

sentences.en: Elsa and her friends stared at the two groups, now sprawled on the ground.
sentences.zh: 艾莎和朋友们盯着地上那两群人——此刻都四脚朝天躺着。

sentences.en: Anna leaned into her sister. “You chose a nice, cold greeting,” she said. “They’ve been trapped in here this whole time?” Kristoff whispered in disbelief. “What do we do now?” Elsa whispered back.
sentences.zh: 安娜靠向姐姐。“你选了个挺冷——挺凉快的见面礼，”她说。“他们一直被困在这里？”克斯托夫难以置信地低语。“我们现在怎么办？”艾莎低声回问。

chapters.title: 第21章
chapters.en:
The history between the two groups in the forest was complicated. They’d met at the celebration for the dam completion. And that was the day they’d become enemies.

But Mattias had met Yelana long before then, during the negotiations on the cliff between the Northuldra ruler and King Runeard. He didn’t need to be reminded how they were stuck in the forest. And Mattias woke every night in a cold sweat, remembering the day more than thirty-four years ago when his whole life had changed.

Boulders had fallen from the sky with perfect aim. Fire had chased the soldiers and the Northuldra like a pack of hungry wolves. Many men and women were injured, and others were lost. Mattias had been in battles before, but never one without an enemy to fight. That wasn’t what bothered him the most, though. He had failed to protect the one person he’d thought of as his son: Prince Agnarr.

Mattias and his soldiers had searched the forest for days for Agnarr. Even now, he didn’t want to accept that the prince had been lost forever the day the forest fell. Mattias still held out hope that somehow, Agnarr had escaped.

Mattias and Yelana had called a truce in the early years so they could work together. They had to find a way to get through the mist that had trapped them in the forest. They knew it would be better to partner in some ways, rather than to be stuck together as enemies. They didn’t always get along, but there were times when they respected each other.

The soldiers had been forced to become experts at using their swords to hunt. They created bows and arrows from sticks and rope. They gathered berries, acorns, and nettles to supplement their diet. They didn’t share food with the Northuldra. And the Northuldra didn’t share their food with them.

Mattias had volunteered when the soldiers constructed a catapult to fire something at the mist that first week. They didn’t know whether it was safe on the other side, but Mattias had been willing to give it a try. He remembered the exhilaration he’d felt when his soldiers had chopped the twisted ropes that held the catapult down. He’d laughed as he soared through the air.

But his laughter changed to dread when he bounced off the mist, as if he’d hit an invisible wall. His body flew back and crashed in a heap on the ground. The fall left him with a heavily sprained arm that never worked properly again. Just thinking about it made Mattias rub his shoulder.

The soldiers tested the catapult repeatedly over the next few months. A hammock was created to catch them when they bounced off the invisible wall. The volunteers were launched into different areas each time, but the results were always the same.

“Hey, Yelana,” Mattias had called out one day.

“Yeah?” she answered.

“Four months, two weeks, and three days,” he said with a wink.

“What’s that?” she asked, confused.

“It’s how long we’ve been here,” he confirmed.

She shook her head. “Don’t remind me.”

Yelana and the Northuldra had later come up with the idea of tunneling underneath the mist. Mattias had thought it was a great plan. The Northuldra had provided them all with shovels made of wood and bone, and both sides had dug day and night for months. For years. But just like the invisible wall above the mist, there was one below the mist. Their shovels bounced off it every time.

“Hey, Mattias,” Yelana had crowed after some time had passed.

“Yes, ma’am?” he asked.

“Three years, seven months, one week, and two days.”

He chuckled. “Don’t remind me.”

A soldier had once tried to chop his way through the mist with an ax. The ax had bounced back and flown out of his hand. Mattias had moved out of the way just as it sailed past his head.

The two groups had refused to give up. Again, the soldiers and Northuldra had worked together as areas of the mist were zoned for testing with axes. Only one person at a time had been allowed in each area, and every inch of the mist was tested for a weak spot. This had taken many years and caused many injuries. No signs of weakness in the mist were ever found.

“Hey, Yelana!” Mattias had hollered at one point after receiving another ax scrape.

“What?” she asked in an annoyed voice.

“Seventeen years, eight months, three weeks, and five days.”

She laughed and walked away.

The Northuldra were experts at climbing trees and mountains. Yelana had led them to the highest points to see how far up the invisible wall extended, but it didn’t matter how high they went, even up to the clouds. Whenever they reached their hands out, their hands would always bounce back.

“Hey, Mattias,” Yelana had growled after even more time had passed.

“I know, I know,” he said with his hands up. “Twenty-four years, ten months, two weeks, and one day.”

Yelana stared back at Mattias and wondered how he could be so naive. He had been there when King Runeard had arrived and promised her people friendship and cooperation. Together, they were supposed to have built a new world of greatness.

She’d seen through the lies. She’d seen the way King Runeard had looked at her people, as if he was better than them. When the children had danced and played with the magic of wind and fire, he had shaken his head and frowned. She could sense his hatred. But their leader had wanted to see the best in their new allies. He’d blindly agreed to their terms and let them in.

Yelana didn’t understand why Mattias believed that nature had rewarded Elsa with magic. She felt sorry for him. Maybe he didn’t know any better and really believed he’d served a great king.

Yelana had never fully trusted him or any of the soldiers, but she had been willing to work with them so she could keep them close. She’d instructed her people to stay away from the soldiers during any other times—they’d interacted only when sharing tools and ideas to escape the mist. She alone had dealt with Mattias directly.

As the years passed, Mattias truly seemed to accept her people and want to help. But Yelana had always remembered how she had thought King Runeard had seemed like a good man, too. And with him she’d made a mistake—one she would never make again.
chapters.zh:
森林里这两群人之间的恩怨，说来话长。

他们是在水坝竣工的庆祝会上相识的。

而那一天，他们成了仇敌。

但马蒂亚斯早在那之前就见过耶拉娜——当时北地人的首领和鲁尼德国王在悬崖上谈判。

他无需别人提醒他们是怎么被困在森林里的。

马蒂亚斯每夜都冷汗涔涔地惊醒，想起三十多年前那个改变他一生的一天。

巨石从天而降，落点分毫不差。

火像一群饿狼，紧追着士兵和北地人。

许多男女受了伤，还有一些人永远失散了。

马蒂亚斯打过仗，却从没打过这样一场没有敌人的仗。

不过，最让他耿耿于怀的并不是这个。

他没能保护好那个他视如己出的人：安格瑞王子。

马蒂亚斯和手下在森林里找了安格瑞好几天。

直到现在，他仍不愿接受：森林崩落的那天，王子就已经永远迷失了。

马蒂亚斯仍抱着一丝希望——或许安格瑞总算逃了出去。

早些年，马蒂亚斯和耶拉娜曾达成休战，以便一同想办法。

他们得找到办法穿过那片把他们困在森林里的迷雾。

他们知道，与其作为仇敌困在一起，不如在某些方面联手。

他们不总和睦，但也有彼此敬重的时候。

士兵们被迫练成了用剑打猎的高手。

他们用树枝和绳索做成了弓箭。

他们采集浆果、橡果和荨麻来补充口粮。

他们不与北地人分享食物。

北地人也不把自己的食物分给他们。

第一周，士兵们造了台投石机，想往迷雾里发射点什么，马蒂亚斯主动报了名。

他们不知道雾的另一边是否安全，但马蒂亚斯愿意试一试。

他还记得，当手下砍断固定投石机的扭曲绳索时，他心里那股兴奋劲儿。

他腾空飞起时，还笑着。

可当他像撞上隐形墙一样被迷雾弹回时，笑声变成了恐惧。

他的身体飞回去，重重摔成一团。

这一摔，他的胳膊严重扭伤，从此再也没好利索。

光是想想，马蒂亚斯就揉起了肩膀。

接下来的几个月，士兵们反复试验那台投石机。

他们还做了个吊床，好在被隐形墙弹回时接住人。

每次志愿者都被发射到不同区域，结果却总是一模一样。“嘿，耶拉娜，”有一天马蒂亚斯喊道。“嗯？”她答。“四个月，两星期，又三天，”他眨眨眼说。“那是什么？”她不解地问。“是我们被困在这儿的时间，”他确认道。

她摇摇头。“别提醒我。”后来，耶拉娜和北地人想出了从迷雾底下打隧道的法子。

马蒂亚斯觉得这主意不错。

北地人给大家发了木头和骨头做的铲子，两边一连几个月日夜开挖。

一连好几年。

可就像迷雾上方有堵隐形墙，下方也有一道。

他们的铲子每次都被弹回来。“嘿，马蒂亚斯，”过了一阵子，耶拉娜得意地喊。“在，长官？”他问。“三年，七个月，一星期，又两天。”他轻笑。“别提醒我。”曾有士兵想用斧头劈开迷雾。

斧头弹了回来，脱手飞出。

斧头擦着他头顶飞过时，马蒂亚斯刚好闪开。

两群人都不肯放弃。

他们又合作起来，把迷雾划分成块，逐块用斧头测试。

每块区域每次只允许一人进入，迷雾的每一寸都被试过，看有没有薄弱处。

这花了许多年，也造成了许多伤。

迷雾上始终没找到任何薄弱的迹象。“嘿，耶拉娜！”马蒂亚斯又一次被斧头刮伤后，有回大叫。“干嘛？”她不耐烦地问。“十七年，八个月，三星期，又五天。”她笑着走开了。

北地人最擅长爬树攀山。

耶拉娜带他们爬到最高处，看那堵隐形墙往上延伸多高——可无论爬多高，哪怕爬到云端，都没用。

只要伸手去探，手总会弹回来。“嘿，马蒂亚斯，”又过了更久，耶拉娜低吼道。“知道知道，”他举起双手说，“二十四年，十个月，两星期，又一天。”耶拉娜盯着马蒂亚斯，心里纳闷他怎么还能这么天真。

鲁尼德国王到来、向她的族人许下友谊与合作诺言时，他就在场。

他们本该携手建起一个伟大的新世界。

她早就看穿了那些谎言。

她见过鲁尼德国王看她族人的眼神，仿佛他高人一等。

当孩子们借着风与火的魔法起舞嬉戏时，他摇头皱眉。

她能感觉到他的憎恨。

可他们的首领却愿意相信新盟友善良的一面。

他盲目地答应了对方的条件，把他们放了进来。

耶拉娜不明白，马蒂亚斯为何相信是自然把魔法赏赐给了艾莎。

她替他感到悲哀。

也许他只是不懂，真心以为自己侍奉过一位伟大的国王。

耶拉娜从没完全信任过他或任何士兵，但她愿意与他们合作，只为把他们留在眼皮底下。

她叮嘱族人在其他时候远离士兵——只有交换工具、商讨逃出迷雾的计策时，双方才打交代。

只有她一个人直接跟马蒂亚斯打交道。

年复一年，马蒂亚斯似乎真的接纳了她的族人，想要帮忙。

可耶拉娜始终记得，自己也曾以为鲁尼德国王是个好人。

而在他身上，她犯过一次错——一个她绝不会再犯的错。

sentences.en: The history between the two groups in the forest was complicated.
sentences.zh: 森林里这两群人之间的恩怨，说来话长。

sentences.en: They’d met at the celebration for the dam completion.
sentences.zh: 他们是在水坝竣工的庆祝会上相识的。

sentences.en: And that was the day they’d become enemies.
sentences.zh: 而那一天，他们成了仇敌。

sentences.en: But Mattias had met Yelana long before then, during the negotiations on the cliff between the Northuldra ruler and King Runeard.
sentences.zh: 但马蒂亚斯早在那之前就见过耶拉娜——当时北地人的首领和鲁尼德国王在悬崖上谈判。

sentences.en: He didn’t need to be reminded how they were stuck in the forest.
sentences.zh: 他无需别人提醒他们是怎么被困在森林里的。

sentences.en: And Mattias woke every night in a cold sweat, remembering the day more than thirty-four years ago when his whole life had changed.
sentences.zh: 马蒂亚斯每夜都冷汗涔涔地惊醒，想起三十多年前那个改变他一生的一天。

sentences.en: Boulders had fallen from the sky with perfect aim.
sentences.zh: 巨石从天而降，落点分毫不差。

sentences.en: Fire had chased the soldiers and the Northuldra like a pack of hungry wolves.
sentences.zh: 火像一群饿狼，紧追着士兵和北地人。

sentences.en: Many men and women were injured, and others were lost.
sentences.zh: 许多男女受了伤，还有一些人永远失散了。

sentences.en: Mattias had been in battles before, but never one without an enemy to fight.
sentences.zh: 马蒂亚斯打过仗，却从没打过这样一场没有敌人的仗。

sentences.en: That wasn’t what bothered him the most, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，最让他耿耿于怀的并不是这个。

sentences.en: He had failed to protect the one person he’d thought of as his son: Prince Agnarr.
sentences.zh: 他没能保护好那个他视如己出的人：安格瑞王子。

sentences.en: Mattias and his soldiers had searched the forest for days for Agnarr.
sentences.zh: 马蒂亚斯和手下在森林里找了安格瑞好几天。

sentences.en: Even now, he didn’t want to accept that the prince had been lost forever the day the forest fell.
sentences.zh: 直到现在，他仍不愿接受：森林崩落的那天，王子就已经永远迷失了。

sentences.en: Mattias still held out hope that somehow, Agnarr had escaped.
sentences.zh: 马蒂亚斯仍抱着一丝希望——或许安格瑞总算逃了出去。

sentences.en: Mattias and Yelana had called a truce in the early years so they could work together.
sentences.zh: 早些年，马蒂亚斯和耶拉娜曾达成休战，以便一同想办法。

sentences.en: They had to find a way to get through the mist that had trapped them in the forest.
sentences.zh: 他们得找到办法穿过那片把他们困在森林里的迷雾。

sentences.en: They knew it would be better to partner in some ways, rather than to be stuck together as enemies.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，与其作为仇敌困在一起，不如在某些方面联手。

sentences.en: They didn’t always get along, but there were times when they respected each other.
sentences.zh: 他们不总和睦，但也有彼此敬重的时候。

sentences.en: The soldiers had been forced to become experts at using their swords to hunt.
sentences.zh: 士兵们被迫练成了用剑打猎的高手。

sentences.en: They created bows and arrows from sticks and rope.
sentences.zh: 他们用树枝和绳索做成了弓箭。

sentences.en: They gathered berries, acorns, and nettles to supplement their diet.
sentences.zh: 他们采集浆果、橡果和荨麻来补充口粮。

sentences.en: They didn’t share food with the Northuldra.
sentences.zh: 他们不与北地人分享食物。

sentences.en: And the Northuldra didn’t share their food with them.
sentences.zh: 北地人也不把自己的食物分给他们。

sentences.en: Mattias had volunteered when the soldiers constructed a catapult to fire something at the mist that first week.
sentences.zh: 第一周，士兵们造了台投石机，想往迷雾里发射点什么，马蒂亚斯主动报了名。

sentences.en: They didn’t know whether it was safe on the other side, but Mattias had been willing to give it a try.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道雾的另一边是否安全，但马蒂亚斯愿意试一试。

sentences.en: He remembered the exhilaration he’d felt when his soldiers had chopped the twisted ropes that held the catapult down.
sentences.zh: 他还记得，当手下砍断固定投石机的扭曲绳索时，他心里那股兴奋劲儿。

sentences.en: He’d laughed as he soared through the air.
sentences.zh: 他腾空飞起时，还笑着。

sentences.en: But his laughter changed to dread when he bounced off the mist, as if he’d hit an invisible wall.
sentences.zh: 可当他像撞上隐形墙一样被迷雾弹回时，笑声变成了恐惧。

sentences.en: His body flew back and crashed in a heap on the ground.
sentences.zh: 他的身体飞回去，重重摔成一团。

sentences.en: The fall left him with a heavily sprained arm that never worked properly again.
sentences.zh: 这一摔，他的胳膊严重扭伤，从此再也没好利索。

sentences.en: Just thinking about it made Mattias rub his shoulder.
sentences.zh: 光是想想，马蒂亚斯就揉起了肩膀。

sentences.en: The soldiers tested the catapult repeatedly over the next few months.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几个月，士兵们反复试验那台投石机。

sentences.en: A hammock was created to catch them when they bounced off the invisible wall.
sentences.zh: 他们还做了个吊床，好在被隐形墙弹回时接住人。

sentences.en: The volunteers were launched into different areas each time, but the results were always the same. “Hey, Yelana,” Mattias had called out one day. “Yeah?” she answered. “Four months, two weeks, and three days,” he said with a wink. “What’s that?” she asked, confused. “It’s how long we’ve been here,” he confirmed.
sentences.zh: 每次志愿者都被发射到不同区域，结果却总是一模一样。“嘿，耶拉娜，”有一天马蒂亚斯喊道。“嗯？”她答。“四个月，两星期，又三天，”他眨眨眼说。“那是什么？”她不解地问。“是我们被困在这儿的时间，”他确认道。

sentences.en: She shook her head. “Don’t remind me.” Yelana and the Northuldra had later come up with the idea of tunneling underneath the mist.
sentences.zh: 她摇摇头。“别提醒我。”后来，耶拉娜和北地人想出了从迷雾底下打隧道的法子。

sentences.en: Mattias had thought it was a great plan.
sentences.zh: 马蒂亚斯觉得这主意不错。

sentences.en: The Northuldra had provided them all with shovels made of wood and bone, and both sides had dug day and night for months.
sentences.zh: 北地人给大家发了木头和骨头做的铲子，两边一连几个月日夜开挖。

sentences.en: For years.
sentences.zh: 一连好几年。

sentences.en: But just like the invisible wall above the mist, there was one below the mist.
sentences.zh: 可就像迷雾上方有堵隐形墙，下方也有一道。

sentences.en: Their shovels bounced off it every time. “Hey, Mattias,” Yelana had crowed after some time had passed. “Yes, ma’am?” he asked. “Three years, seven months, one week, and two days.” He chuckled. “Don’t remind me.” A soldier had once tried to chop his way through the mist with an ax.
sentences.zh: 他们的铲子每次都被弹回来。“嘿，马蒂亚斯，”过了一阵子，耶拉娜得意地喊。“在，长官？”他问。“三年，七个月，一星期，又两天。”他轻笑。“别提醒我。”曾有士兵想用斧头劈开迷雾。

sentences.en: The ax had bounced back and flown out of his hand.
sentences.zh: 斧头弹了回来，脱手飞出。

sentences.en: Mattias had moved out of the way just as it sailed past his head.
sentences.zh: 斧头擦着他头顶飞过时，马蒂亚斯刚好闪开。

sentences.en: The two groups had refused to give up.
sentences.zh: 两群人都不肯放弃。

sentences.en: Again, the soldiers and Northuldra had worked together as areas of the mist were zoned for testing with axes.
sentences.zh: 他们又合作起来，把迷雾划分成块，逐块用斧头测试。

sentences.en: Only one person at a time had been allowed in each area, and every inch of the mist was tested for a weak spot.
sentences.zh: 每块区域每次只允许一人进入，迷雾的每一寸都被试过，看有没有薄弱处。

sentences.en: This had taken many years and caused many injuries.
sentences.zh: 这花了许多年，也造成了许多伤。

sentences.en: No signs of weakness in the mist were ever found. “Hey, Yelana!” Mattias had hollered at one point after receiving another ax scrape. “What?” she asked in an annoyed voice. “Seventeen years, eight months, three weeks, and five days.” She laughed and walked away.
sentences.zh: 迷雾上始终没找到任何薄弱的迹象。“嘿，耶拉娜！”马蒂亚斯又一次被斧头刮伤后，有回大叫。“干嘛？”她不耐烦地问。“十七年，八个月，三星期，又五天。”她笑着走开了。

sentences.en: The Northuldra were experts at climbing trees and mountains.
sentences.zh: 北地人最擅长爬树攀山。

sentences.en: Yelana had led them to the highest points to see how far up the invisible wall extended, but it didn’t matter how high they went, even up to the clouds.
sentences.zh: 耶拉娜带他们爬到最高处，看那堵隐形墙往上延伸多高——可无论爬多高，哪怕爬到云端，都没用。

sentences.en: Whenever they reached their hands out, their hands would always bounce back. “Hey, Mattias,” Yelana had growled after even more time had passed. “I know, I know,” he said with his hands up. “Twenty-four years, ten months, two weeks, and one day.” Yelana stared back at Mattias and wondered how he could be so naive.
sentences.zh: 只要伸手去探，手总会弹回来。“嘿，马蒂亚斯，”又过了更久，耶拉娜低吼道。“知道知道，”他举起双手说，“二十四年，十个月，两星期，又一天。”耶拉娜盯着马蒂亚斯，心里纳闷他怎么还能这么天真。

sentences.en: He had been there when King Runeard had arrived and promised her people friendship and cooperation.
sentences.zh: 鲁尼德国王到来、向她的族人许下友谊与合作诺言时，他就在场。

sentences.en: Together, they were supposed to have built a new world of greatness.
sentences.zh: 他们本该携手建起一个伟大的新世界。

sentences.en: She’d seen through the lies.
sentences.zh: 她早就看穿了那些谎言。

sentences.en: She’d seen the way King Runeard had looked at her people, as if he was better than them.
sentences.zh: 她见过鲁尼德国王看她族人的眼神，仿佛他高人一等。

sentences.en: When the children had danced and played with the magic of wind and fire, he had shaken his head and frowned.
sentences.zh: 当孩子们借着风与火的魔法起舞嬉戏时，他摇头皱眉。

sentences.en: She could sense his hatred.
sentences.zh: 她能感觉到他的憎恨。

sentences.en: But their leader had wanted to see the best in their new allies.
sentences.zh: 可他们的首领却愿意相信新盟友善良的一面。

sentences.en: He’d blindly agreed to their terms and let them in.
sentences.zh: 他盲目地答应了对方的条件，把他们放了进来。

sentences.en: Yelana didn’t understand why Mattias believed that nature had rewarded Elsa with magic.
sentences.zh: 耶拉娜不明白，马蒂亚斯为何相信是自然把魔法赏赐给了艾莎。

sentences.en: She felt sorry for him.
sentences.zh: 她替他感到悲哀。

sentences.en: Maybe he didn’t know any better and really believed he’d served a great king.
sentences.zh: 也许他只是不懂，真心以为自己侍奉过一位伟大的国王。

sentences.en: Yelana had never fully trusted him or any of the soldiers, but she had been willing to work with them so she could keep them close.
sentences.zh: 耶拉娜从没完全信任过他或任何士兵，但她愿意与他们合作，只为把他们留在眼皮底下。

sentences.en: She’d instructed her people to stay away from the soldiers during any other times—they’d interacted only when sharing tools and ideas to escape the mist.
sentences.zh: 她叮嘱族人在其他时候远离士兵——只有交换工具、商讨逃出迷雾的计策时，双方才打交代。

sentences.en: She alone had dealt with Mattias directly.
sentences.zh: 只有她一个人直接跟马蒂亚斯打交道。

sentences.en: As the years passed, Mattias truly seemed to accept her people and want to help.
sentences.zh: 年复一年，马蒂亚斯似乎真的接纳了她的族人，想要帮忙。

sentences.en: But Yelana had always remembered how she had thought King Runeard had seemed like a good man, too.
sentences.zh: 可耶拉娜始终记得，自己也曾以为鲁尼德国王是个好人。

sentences.en: And with him she’d made a mistake—one she would never make again.
sentences.zh: 而在他身上，她犯过一次错——一个她绝不会再犯的错。

chapters.title: 第22章
chapters.en:
“I got this,” Olaf said confidently as he moved out from behind Elsa and waddled forward. “Hi, I’m Olaf.”

The Northuldra and Arendellians alike screamed, shouted, and slipped as they attempted to get away from the walking, talking snowman.

Olaf looked down at himself, and then back up at the frightened people. “Oh, sorry,” he said. “Yeah, I just find clothes restricting. But you’re wondering who we are and why we’re here.”

As if he were on a stage, performing a one-snowman show under a spotlight, Olaf started his dramatization.

“It began with two sisters. One born with magical powers. One born powerless.”

The Northuldra and the Arendellian soldiers stared.

“Anna, no! Too high! BLAST!” Olaf fell to the ground, then quickly got back to his feet and channeled Elsa. “NO! Mama, Papa, HELP!”

Mattias looked on as the snowman continued to act out key moments in the sisters’ lives.

“SLAM! Doors shutting everywhere! Sisters torn apart!”

Olaf walked around, taking on the gait and mannerisms of each person he was portraying.

“Well, at least they have their parents,” Olaf said in a soft voice. Then his voice changed and became completely void of emotion: “Their parents are dead.”

Next, he dramatized Elsa’s little sister.

“Hi, I’m Anna. I’ll marry a man I just met.”

Anna wanted to melt into the ground. Although no one there knew who she was, it felt as if they had all been clued in on her biggest, most horrifying secret. She mentally prodded Olaf to move on to another subject.

“Elsa’s gonna blow!” Olaf shouted. “Snow! Snow! AAHHH! Run!”

Olaf began to hum a wildly off-tune melody that seemed as if it should have been majestic.

“Magic pulses through my snowflakes,” he said, and then pulled in a deep breath of air before shouting, “I live!” He held his twig arms over his head.

He took a stroll, gesturing like Elsa did when she made magical creations.

“Ice palace for one, ice palace for one. Get out, Anna! Pew, pew!”

Olaf spun around and staggered in what Anna felt was a completely fabricated performance.

“My heart!” he gasped.

Mattias’s eyes widened. “Oh my goodness….”

“Only an act of true love can save you,” Olaf continued, his voice deepening as he did what he thought was a spot-on impersonation of Grand Pabbie.

Kristoff clapped, but after a look from Anna, he let his hands drop to his sides.

“Here’s a true-love’s kiss. You’re not worth it. Guess what? I’m the bad guy!” Olaf exclaimed, as Hans.

“What?” Mattias shouted.

“Then Anna freezes to death…forever.”

Mattias wiped at the tears that sprang to his eyes. “Oh, Anna.”

“Then she unfreezes!” Olaf shouted. The snowman took a big breath and finished his story. “Oh, and then Elsa woke up the magical spirits, and we were forced out of our kingdom. Now our only hope is to find the truth about the past, but we don’t have a clue how to do that. Except Elsa’s hearing voices. So we got that going for us. Any questions?”

The Northuldra and the Arendellians had long since stopped trying to flee. They sat where they had fallen, transfixed both by the tale and the living snowman. No one knew how to react…to either.

“I think they got it,” Olaf whispered loudly to Anna and Elsa.

With one motion of her hands, Elsa wiped away the ice on the ground. The lieutenant took his time getting to his feet. And when he did, he offered his hand to Yelana. The Northuldra woman frowned at him but accepted his help nonetheless. As soon as she stood, they parted, as if the assistance had never happened.

“Are you really Queen of Arendelle?” Mattias asked as they approached the sisters.

“I am,” Elsa said.

“Why would nature reward a person of Arendelle with magic?” Yelana asked, her expression showing her confusion.

“Perhaps to make up for the actions of your people,” Mattias responded as he turned to face her.

Yelana’s eyes hardened. “My people are innocent. We would never attack first.”

Anna and Elsa watched the decades-old enemies rehash an argument they seemed to have had many times before. But it still bothered Anna that she couldn’t recall where she knew Mattias from. She framed the lieutenant’s face with her fingers, making a square. She closed one eye and looked through the square at him, changing the angle and size of the square as well as her position.

“May the truth be found,” he said. Then he caught sight of Anna. “Hi. I’m sorry. What’s happening?”

Anna didn’t answer, too intent on her task.

“This is different,” he said.

“To the left,” Anna instructed. “Right.”

“Okay…this?” he asked, trying to follow her directions. “This side?”

“No, left,” she corrected him.

“Sure?” Mattias moved again. “Ugh.”

“Now look like you have just a little bit of indigestion,” she said.

Mattias made one last move.

“That’s it!” Anna shouted in excitement, causing a few people nearby to jump at her sudden burst of energy. “Lieutenant Mattias! Library, second portrait on the right! You were our father’s official guard.”

Mattias’s eyes narrowed as what Anna was saying sank into his head. Then he looked right at her, and at Elsa, who had walked up behind her sister. He suddenly realized who the two of them were. “Agnarr…he was lost at sea?”

“Yes,” Anna said, sadness creeping into her voice, as it always did when she thought about the loss of her parents. “Our parents’ ship went down in the Southern Sea six years ago.”

The four Arendellian soldiers and Mattias bowed their heads out of respect to their fallen king and queen. When Mattias looked up, he regarded the sisters with compassion.

“I see him,” he said, looking back and forth between the two of them. “I see him in your faces.”

Anna was flattered to hear his words. She looked at her sister, gauging her excitement before meeting Mattias’s gaze. She was thrilled to know she reminded someone of her father.

“Really?” said Anna. “He’d have been so happy to know you’re okay.”

“Soldiers,” Mattias commanded with a signal.

The soldiers and shield maiden fell into a formation behind Elsa. They had recognized her as their queen, and with their formal military stance, they offered their support. But the atmosphere of the camp shifted dramatically when the Arendellians moved into formation. The Northuldra whispered and paced nervously, even though Mattias smiled at Yelana. Elsa felt the discomfort as well as saw it.

“Please,” said Elsa, her tone soothing as she tried to calm them all. “Someone called me here. If I can just find them, I believe they have answers that may help free this forest.” Elsa smiled, hoping her words would raise everyone’s spirits. “Trust me, I just want to help.”

But the Northuldra had trusted before, and it had been to their detriment.

“We only trust nature,” said Yelana. “When nature speaks—”

Yelana was interrupted by a fireball shooting up behind Elsa, catching the leaves of a tree on fire.

Yelana waited a beat, then finished. “We listen.”
chapters.zh:
“交给我，”奥拉夫自信地说着，从艾莎身后挪出来，一摇一摆走上前。“嗨，我是奥拉夫。”北地人和阿伦黛尔人齐声尖叫、惊呼，拼命想躲开这个会走会说的雪人，脚下直打滑。

奥拉夫低头看看自己，又抬头看看那些受惊的人。“哦，抱歉，”他说，“是啊，我只是觉得衣服太束缚了。

但你们一定想知道我们是谁、来这儿干什么。”奥拉夫仿佛站在舞台上、聚光灯下演独角戏，开始了他的表演。“故事从两姐妹开始。

一个生来就有魔法。

一个生来毫无魔力。”北地人和阿伦黛尔士兵愣愣地看。“安娜，不！

太高了！

爆裂！”奥拉夫扑倒在地，又迅速爬起，模仿起艾莎。“不！

爸爸妈妈，救命！”雪人继续演绎姐妹俩人生中的关键片段，马蒂亚斯在一旁看着。“砰！

到处是关上的门！

姐妹被拆散！”奥拉夫走来走去，学着他扮演的每个人的步态和神态。“唔，至少她们还有父母，”奥拉夫轻声说。

sentences.en: If I can just find them, I believe they have answers that may help free this forest.” Elsa smiled, hoping her words would raise everyone’s spirits. “Trust me, I just want to help.” But the Northuldra had trusted before, and it had been to their detriment. “We only trust nature,” said Yelana. “When nature speaks—” Yelana was interrupted by a fireball shooting up behind Elsa, catching the leaves of a tree on fire.
sentences.zh: 只要我找到他们，相信他们有答案，能帮这片森林获得自由。”艾莎微笑着，希望这话能鼓舞大家。“相信我，我只想帮忙。”可北地人曾经信过别人，结果吃了大亏。“我们只信自然，”耶拉娜说，“当自然开口——”耶拉娜的话被艾莎身后窜起的一颗火球打断，火苗点着了树叶。

chapters.title: 第23章
chapters.en:
Suddenly, a bright flash of fire whipped out from behind a nearby tree in a blur, then vanished as quickly as it had appeared. Everyone stood on guard, looking around, trying to see where it had gone.

BOOM!

The tree it had come from behind lit up, blazing with flames.

“FIRE SPIRIT!” Yelana shouted.

Olaf backed away. While he didn’t know what a Fire Spirit was, and even though he was now made of permafrost, he was still aware that it wasn’t a good idea to be too close to fire. But this fire looked different from any he had ever seen. The flames weren’t purely red and orange—Olaf saw hints of purple, too. And the flames were as terrifying as they were fascinating.

“This will all make sense when I am older,” Olaf said to himself.

“Get back, everyone!” Yelana ordered, wanting nothing more than to keep her people safe.

All around, the Northuldra grabbed their children and their essentials, trying to keep away from the fire as much as they could.

“Head for the river!” Mattias yelled.

The Fire Spirit began to move, leaving a trail of the magical fire in its wake. There appeared to be no logic to its direction. Arendellians and the Northuldra ran around in confusion, having no idea which way the fire trail would go. Elsa raced after them, wanting to help any way she could.

The trail sparked and popped in the dry brush, and stray flames began new paths of their own. Flames sped up a shrub, then a tree. They appeared in the grasses. They consumed and the fire grew, taking on a life of its own.

The heat and the crackling flames added to the confusion. The Northuldra reindeer pawed the ground nervously. One of them panicked and ran off. The rest of them followed, their hooves thundering as they galloped past.

“No, no, no! The reindeer!” a Northuldra man named Ryder shouted as their movement caught his attention. “That’s a dead end!”

Kristoff turned and saw that the reindeer had bolted out of the area, and he knew there wasn’t any time to waste. “Come on, Sven. We’ll get them!” With a quick leap, he hopped on Sven and they raced after the runaway reindeer, even as fire threatened to close their path.

But Elsa saw what was happening. She spun around and blasted her ice, widening the opening through the fire in front of them. Kristoff and Sven leaped through it.

Anna, who had been helping the Northuldra gather up their things and get to the river, turned to find that Elsa wasn’t directly behind her. Instead, her sister was in the heart of the fire, her face intent as she used her power to battle the flames.

“Elsa! Get out of there!” Anna shouted.

Anna struggled against the waves of people running for their lives as she headed closer to the flames instead of away from them. She was determined to get back to her sister.

“Elsa!” she called again.

The heat of the raging fire got stronger the closer she got to her sister, and the smoke flooded her lungs with every breath she took. But she continued. Anna refused to leave Elsa.

Kristoff and Sven caught up with the terrified reindeer. They pranced and grunted nervously in a small area where the exits were blocked by fallen trees and fire. Their unease, and the closeness of the flames, bothered Sven as well. Kristoff patted his neck to reassure him. “Come on, buddy,” Kristoff coaxed.

There was something about the interaction between Sven and Kristoff that calmed the other reindeer—at least enough that the duo was able to lead them safely away from the flames that were starting to sprout up at the dead end. They raced back at full speed.

Kristoff felt an urgency to make sure his friends were safe. “We can do this. Hiya!”

One by one, the reindeer jumped through the flaming bushes until they were safely in the clearing. Kristoff and Sven had done it! Ryder and a few of the other Northuldra rushed forward to care for the reindeer. Ryder looked at Kristoff gratefully. Kristoff smiled.

Now it was time to find Anna. Kristoff looked around the flames and smoke, searching everywhere for a glimpse of her. When he finally found her, what he saw terrified him.

“Anna!” Kristoff yelled, frightened for her life.

Flames surrounded Anna and were closing in. Only one person could help Kristoff save her: Elsa. She had been so busy trying to control the fire that she hadn’t seen the danger her sister was in. When she finally saw the threat to Anna, she changed her tactics. ­Nothing can happen to her! Elsa thought, spinning around and throwing out her magic. She created a hole in the flames just large enough for Kristoff and Sven to get through and reach Anna.

It was getting harder and harder for Anna to breathe as she lay on the forest floor, wondering how to get to Elsa. She didn’t hear the sounds of hooves and Kristoff’s voice. She didn’t even know they were there until Kristoff grabbed her, swung her up onto Sven, and the three of them exited the same way that Sven and Kristoff had come in.

“Get her out of here!” Elsa shouted. She had been filled with fear, knowing all she could do was watch as Kristoff went after Anna. Now that her sister was safe, she wanted her to run.

“No, Elsa!” Anna cried, her voice hoarse from the smoke. They couldn’t just leave her sister behind! But Kristoff didn’t stop, and neither did Sven. The fire had been too close to Anna, and they wouldn’t let anything happen to her.

Elsa ran toward the flames. She hadn’t even heard Anna call after her. It was up to HER to put out the fire, and she would do whatever she could to stop it.

The inferno tore through the Northuldra camp, relentless and unforgiving. Elsa fought to control as much of the damage as possible. And then she saw it…the fireball that had started everything. It danced, it darted, it circled, and she followed it. She had been blasting the flames it had left behind, and they hadn’t gone out, at least not all the way. She hadn’t been able to make a dent in the blaze. It was time for a new plan.
chapters.zh:
忽然，一道明亮的火光从附近一棵树后疾掠而出，一闪即逝，快得和出现时一样。

人人严阵以待，四下张望，想看清它去了哪里。

轰！

它身后那棵树瞬间燃起熊熊火焰。“火灵！”耶拉娜喊道。

奥拉夫连连后退。

虽然他不知道火灵是什么，尽管如今他由永冻冰做成，他仍清楚离火太近绝不是好事。

可这火看上去和以往见过的都不一样。

火焰不单是红与橙——奥拉夫还看出了紫色。

而这火焰既恐怖又迷人。“等我长大就都明白了，”奥拉夫对自己说。“大家都退后！”耶拉娜下令，她只想着保族人平安。

四周的北地人抱起孩子和要紧物事，尽量远离火焰。“往河边跑！”马蒂亚斯大喊。

火灵动了起来，身后拖出一道魔法之火。

它行进的方向似乎毫无章法。

阿伦黛尔人和北地人慌乱地四处奔逃，根本不知道火线会往哪儿烧。

艾莎追在他们后面跑，想尽己所能帮忙。

火线在干枯的灌木丛中噼啪迸溅，零星的火苗又自己开辟出新路。

火苗窜上一丛灌木，又窜上一棵树。

草丛里也冒出了火。

火越烧越旺，仿佛有了自己的生命。

热浪和噼啪作响的火焰更添混乱。

北地人的驯鹿不安地刨着地面。

其中一头受惊跑开了。

其余的跟着跑，蹄声如雷，奔腾而过。“不不不！

那些驯鹿！”一个叫莱德的北地男子见状大喊，“那是死路！”克斯托夫转头看见驯鹿已冲出那片地方，知道一刻也不能耽误。“快，斯文。

我们去拦住它们！”他纵身一跃跳上斯文，朝逃跑的驯鹿追去，哪怕火焰正要封住去路。

可艾莎看出了端倪。

她转身喷出冰霜，把前方火焰间的缺口拓宽。

克斯托夫和斯文一跃穿过。

安娜一直在帮北地人收拾东西、往河边撤，这时转身发现艾莎不在自己正后方。

相反，姐姐正身处火心，神情专注地用魔力对抗烈焰。“艾莎！

快出来！”安娜喊。

安娜逆着四散逃命的人潮，不往外却往火边挤去。

她打定主意要回到姐姐身边。“艾莎！”她又喊了一声。

离姐姐越近，烈火的热浪越猛，每吸一口气，烟都灌满她的肺。

可她脚步不停。

安娜不肯丢下艾莎。

克斯托夫和斯文追上了受惊的驯鹿。

在出口被倒木和火焰堵死的一小块空地上，它们不安地腾跃、哼叫。

它们的不安，加上近在咫尺的火焰，也让斯文烦躁。

克斯托夫拍拍他的脖子安抚他。“来吧，老伙计，”克斯托夫哄道。

斯文和克斯托夫之间的互动，不知怎的让其他驯鹿也平静下来——至少足以让这俩人带着它们安全避开死路上窜起的火苗。

他们全速往回冲。

克斯托夫心急如焚，只想确保朋友们平安。“我们能做到。

驾！”驯鹿一头接一头跳过燃烧的灌木，直到全部安全落到空地上。

克斯托夫和斯文成功了！

莱德和另外几个北地人冲上前照料驯鹿。

莱德感激地看着克斯托夫。

克斯托夫笑了。

现在该去找安娜了。

克斯托夫在火焰与浓烟中四下张望，拼命寻找她的身影。

当他终于找到她时，眼前的景象令他胆寒。“安娜！”克斯托夫为她的安危惊恐大喊。

火焰围着安娜，正不断收紧。

能帮克斯托夫救她的，只有一个人：艾莎。

她一直忙着控制火势，没看见妹妹身陷险境。

等她终于看到安娜的危情，立刻改变策略。她绝不能有事！

艾莎想，转身释放出魔力。

她在火焰中开出一个刚好够克斯托夫和斯文穿过、够到安娜的洞。

安娜躺在林地上，呼吸越来越困难，一心想着怎么到艾莎身边。

她没听见蹄声，也没听见克斯托夫的声音。

直到克斯托夫一把抓住她、把她甩上斯文，三人顺着斯文和克斯托夫进来的路撤出，她才知道他们在。“把她带出去！”艾莎喊。

她满心恐惧，知道自己只能眼睁睁看着克斯托夫去救安娜。

既然妹妹安全了，她想让她快跑。“不，艾莎！”安娜哭喊，声音被烟呛得沙哑。

她们不能就这么把姐姐丢下！

可克斯托夫没停，斯文也没停。

火离安娜太近了，他们绝不让她出半点差池。

艾莎朝火焰跑去。

她甚至没听见安娜在身后喊她。

灭火只能靠她自己，她会不惜一切把它扑灭。

那场烈火席卷北地人的营地，毫不留情。

艾莎奋力把破坏控制到最小。

接着她看见了它……那颗引发一切的火球。

它蹦跳、疾窜、打转，她就一路跟着。

她一直在喷射它留下的火苗，可火没灭，至少没全灭。

她根本没能伤那大火分毫。

是时候换套新法子了。

sentences.zh: 等她终于看到安娜的危情，立刻改变策略。她绝不能有事！

sentences.en: Elsa thought, spinning around and throwing out her magic.
sentences.zh: 艾莎想，转身释放出魔力。

sentences.en: She created a hole in the flames just large enough for Kristoff and Sven to get through and reach Anna.
sentences.zh: 她在火焰中开出一个刚好够克斯托夫和斯文穿过、够到安娜的洞。

sentences.en: It was getting harder and harder for Anna to breathe as she lay on the forest floor, wondering how to get to Elsa.
sentences.zh: 安娜躺在林地上，呼吸越来越困难，一心想着怎么到艾莎身边。

sentences.en: She didn’t hear the sounds of hooves and Kristoff’s voice.
sentences.zh: 她没听见蹄声，也没听见克斯托夫的声音。

sentences.en: She didn’t even know they were there until Kristoff grabbed her, swung her up onto Sven, and the three of them exited the same way that Sven and Kristoff had come in. “Get her out of here!” Elsa shouted.
sentences.zh: 直到克斯托夫一把抓住她、把她甩上斯文，三人顺着斯文和克斯托夫进来的路撤出，她才知道他们在。“把她带出去！”艾莎喊。

sentences.en: She had been filled with fear, knowing all she could do was watch as Kristoff went after Anna.
sentences.zh: 她满心恐惧，知道自己只能眼睁睁看着克斯托夫去救安娜。

sentences.en: Now that her sister was safe, she wanted her to run. “No, Elsa!” Anna cried, her voice hoarse from the smoke.
sentences.zh: 既然妹妹安全了，她想让她快跑。“不，艾莎！”安娜哭喊，声音被烟呛得沙哑。

sentences.en: They couldn’t just leave her sister behind!
sentences.zh: 她们不能就这么把姐姐丢下！

sentences.en: But Kristoff didn’t stop, and neither did Sven.
sentences.zh: 可克斯托夫没停，斯文也没停。

sentences.en: The fire had been too close to Anna, and they wouldn’t let anything happen to her.
sentences.zh: 火离安娜太近了，他们绝不让她出半点差池。

sentences.en: Elsa ran toward the flames.
sentences.zh: 艾莎朝火焰跑去。

sentences.en: She hadn’t even heard Anna call after her.
sentences.zh: 她甚至没听见安娜在身后喊她。

sentences.en: It was up to HER to put out the fire, and she would do whatever she could to stop it.
sentences.zh: 灭火只能靠她自己，她会不惜一切把它扑灭。

sentences.en: The inferno tore through the Northuldra camp, relentless and unforgiving.
sentences.zh: 那场烈火席卷北地人的营地，毫不留情。

sentences.en: Elsa fought to control as much of the damage as possible.
sentences.zh: 艾莎奋力把破坏控制到最小。

sentences.en: And then she saw it…the fireball that had started everything.
sentences.zh: 接着她看见了它……那颗引发一切的火球。

sentences.en: It danced, it darted, it circled, and she followed it.
sentences.zh: 它蹦跳、疾窜、打转，她就一路跟着。

sentences.en: She had been blasting the flames it had left behind, and they hadn’t gone out, at least not all the way.
sentences.zh: 她一直在喷射它留下的火苗，可火没灭，至少没全灭。

sentences.en: She hadn’t been able to make a dent in the blaze.
sentences.zh: 她根本没能伤那大火分毫。

sentences.en: It was time for a new plan.
sentences.zh: 是时候换套新法子了。

chapters.title: 第24章
chapters.en:
Elsa threw the full force of her powers on the fireball’s blazing trail. She chased it until it was contained beneath a rocky overhang, where the flames seemed to lessen.

Curious, Elsa bent down and studied what was left of the fire. Two tiny, terrified eyes stared up at her. This is the Fire Spirit? she asked herself. The powerful, fearsome Fire Spirit? It looked just like a little salamander. But if anyone knew that appearances could be deceiving, it was Elsa.

The salamander whimpered, and a blast of fire shot from its mouth, aimed directly at a tree behind Elsa. But she was quick, and she froze the fire in midair, creating a spectacular display that hung there for the briefest of moments and was gone. The salamander looked from their joint creation and back to her. With one webbed foot raised, it took a hesitant step toward Elsa, moving ever so slowly, like a frightened puppy.

Elsa was deeply touched. She wondered if the creature had been hurt in the past, or misunderstood. Those were feelings she could easily relate to. She crouched down closer to the rock and leaned in, then stretched a hand out to the Fire Spirit.

The salamander slowly came forward and climbed onto her hand. It appeared to be relieved by the touch of Elsa’s cold skin, making itself comfortable as it settled in, sizzling on her palm.

“Oh!” Elsa yelped in surprise. “Ow, ow.” She winced from the salamander’s heat, but the most important thing was for the creature to feel safe.

A thought came to her. She created snowflakes on the tips of her fingers and let them drift down to the Fire Spirit. The salamander looked at them curiously before darting out its tongue and catching them. As the Fire Spirit ate them, the flames on its back eased and the fire in the trees around them lessened. It playfully shot out a tiny burst of fire to pop another snowflake, then snuggled in the crevices of Elsa’s hand. The fire went out in the other areas of the forest.

Footsteps crept up behind Elsa. She sighed. The moments she had just shared with the Fire Spirit had been so…magical.

“They’re all looking at us, aren’t they?” she whispered to her new friend.

She turned her head and glanced over her shoulder. A crowd stood about five feet away, looking and whispering. More people were approaching, many of them with their eyes wide in amazement.

“Got any advice?” Elsa whispered to the Fire Spirit, who stared at her unblinkingly. “No? Nothing?” The Fire Spirit licked its eye. “Hmm, should I know what that means?”

Then the mysterious voice broke through, haunting and eerie, pushing to the front of everything that was happening. It became the only thing Elsa could focus on. And she noticed that for the first time, someone else was focused on it, too.

The Fire Spirit looked around, searching for the source of the voice. And then just as quickly as it had begun, it stopped. Elsa turned to her friend. “You hear it, too?” she asked. “Somebody’s calling us. Who is it? What do we do?” The salamander hopped out of her hand and ran up a rock, its head angled to look at something far in the distance. Then the Fire Spirit turned back to her.

“Okay, keep going north,” Elsa interpreted. The salamander glowed bright for a moment, then disappeared over the top of the rock.

“Elsa!”

She turned at the sound of her sister’s voice, and the smile that crossed her face when Anna appeared was brilliant. Elsa moved toward her and wrapped her arms around her little sister, relieved that she was okay.

“Oh, thank goodness,” Anna said, hugging Elsa back just as tightly.

“Anna,” Elsa reprimanded. Now that she knew her sister was safe, she was angry that Anna had been foolish to not get to a safe part of the forest with the others. She pulled away and frowned. “What were you doing? You could have been killed. You can’t just follow me into fire.”

“You don’t want me to follow you into fire,” Anna argued, “then don’t run into fire! You’re not being careful, Elsa.”

Elsa took a deep breath and actually heard the words Anna said. That helped her calm down. Anna always had her best interests in mind, and she would have done the same thing. “I’m sorry. Are you okay?”

“I’ve been better,” Anna responded.

Kristoff and Olaf remained silent as they came up behind the girls with Sven. It was not the time or place for them to interrupt. But they had never seen the girls fight before, and their concern was evident on their faces.

“Hmm, I know what you need.” Elsa reached for the satchel that Anna carried and tugged on the corner of their mother’s scarf dangling from the side. She pulled it out of the bag and wrapped it around her sister’s shoulders.

The Northuldra around them gasped, turning to one another and whispering. Yelana moved through the crowd, approaching Elsa and Anna before raising a hand as a signal for everyone to calm down. Anna and Elsa turned to them, wondering why everyone was staring.

“Where did you get that scarf?” Yelana asked.

A young Northuldra man and woman moved closer. They seemed curious to hear the answer to Yelana’s question. Anna stared at the young woman until it hit her…she was the one who had challenged them initially, with her staff. They nodded to each other in greeting.

“I’m Honeymaren,” she said. “And that is my brother, Ryder.”

Ryder stepped forward—with a smile, but also with curiosity all over his face. “That’s a Northuldra scarf,” he said.
chapters.zh:
艾莎把全身魔力倾泻在火球燃烧的轨迹上。

她一路追，直到把它逼到一处岩石悬檐下，那里的火势似乎弱了些。

艾莎好奇地弯下腰，端详火剩下来的东西。

一双小小的、惊恐的眼睛抬头望着她。

这就是火灵？她暗自问。

那个强大、可怕的火灵？

它看上去就像只小蝾螈。

但若说有谁懂得“人不可貌相”，那便是艾莎。

小蝾螈呜咽一声，喷出一道火，直冲艾莎身后一棵树。

但她手疾眼快，把那道火冻在半空，凝成一场转瞬即逝的奇景。

小蝾螈看看他们共同的“作品”，又看看她。

它抬起一只带蹼的脚，朝艾莎迟疑地迈了一步，慢得像个受惊的小狗。

艾莎深受触动。

她猜想，这小家伙是不是曾经受过伤，或被误解。

这些感受，她太能共鸣了。

她蹲得更低，凑近岩石，然后向火灵伸出一只手。

小蝾螈慢慢上前，爬上她的手。

碰上艾莎冰凉的皮肤，它似乎松了口气，舒舒服服地安顿下来，在掌心嘶嘶作响。“哦！”艾莎惊讶地叫。“嗷，嗷。”被蝾螈烫到，她龇牙咧嘴，可眼下最重要的是让小家伙感到安全。

她冒出一个念头。

她在指尖凝出雪花，让它们飘落到火灵身上。

小蝾螈好奇地看着，随后吐出舌头把雪花卷住。

火灵吃着雪花，背上的火焰渐弱，四周树上的火也小了。

它顽皮地喷出一小簇火，炸开另一片雪花，然后蜷进艾莎手心的纹路里。

森林其他地方的大火也灭了。

艾莎身后响起了轻轻的脚步声。

她叹了口气。

方才与火灵共度的片刻，如此……神奇。“他们都在看我们，对吧？”她对新朋友耳语。

她转过头，从肩上看了一眼。

大约五步开外站着一群人，正望着、窃窃私语。

更多人正走过来，许多人瞪大了惊奇的眼。“有啥建议没？”艾莎对火灵耳语，火灵一眨不眨地盯着她。“没有？

啥也没有？”火灵舔了舔眼睛。“嗯，这动作是什么意思我该懂吗？”这时，那神秘的声音穿透而来，诡谲而幽远，盖过了周遭一切。

它成了艾莎唯一能专注的东西。

她注意到，这是头一回，还有别人也在专注着它。

火灵四下张望，寻找那声音的来源。

然后，它停了——停得和开始时一样突然。

艾莎转向朋友。“你也听见了？”她问，“有人在召唤我们。

会是谁？

我们该怎么办？”小蝾螈从她手上跳下，跑上岩石，歪着头望向远方某处。

接着火灵转回身对着她。“好吧，继续往北走，”艾莎会意道。

小蝾螈亮了一下，便从岩顶消失了。“艾莎！”她循声转头，安娜出现时，她脸上绽放出灿烂的笑容。

艾莎迎上去，双臂搂住小妹，为她平安而宽慰。“哦，谢天谢地，”安娜说，同样紧紧回抱。“安娜，”艾莎嗔怪道。

既然知道妹妹平安，她便恼火安娜竟傻得没和别人一起撤到森林安全处。

她退开一步，皱起眉。“你刚才在干什么？

你差点就没命了。

你不能就这么跟着我进火里。”“你不想我跟着你进火里，”安娜反驳，“那你就别往火里冲！

你太不小心了，艾莎。”艾莎深吸一口气，真的听进了安娜的话。

这话让她平静下来。

安娜总是为她着想，换作她也会一样。“对不起。

你还好吗？”“比现在好不到哪去，”安娜答。

克斯托夫和奥拉夫默默跟在女孩们身后，带着斯文走来。

此刻此景，不是他们插话的时机。

可他们从没见女孩们吵过架，脸上写满担忧。“嗯，我知道你需要什么。”艾莎伸手去够安娜背的挎包，拽出垂在侧边的母亲围巾一角。

她把围巾从包里抽出来，披在妹妹肩上。

周围的北地人倒吸一口气，转头彼此低语。

耶拉娜穿过人群，走近艾莎和安娜，然后举起一只手示意大家安静。

安娜和艾莎转向他们，纳闷大家为何都盯着看。“那条围巾你从哪儿来的？”耶拉娜问。

一男一女两个年轻的北地人凑近了些。

他们似乎很想听耶拉娜这个问题的答案。

安娜盯着那年轻女子，忽然想起来了……最初用杖拦住他们的，就是她。

两人点头致意。“我是霍妮玛伦，”她说，“那是我哥哥，莱德。”莱德上前一步——面带微笑，脸上却也写满好奇。“那是北地人的围巾，”他说。

sentences.zh: 你太不小心了，艾莎。”艾莎深吸一口气，真的听进了安娜的话。

sentences.en: That helped her calm down.

sentences.en: Anna always had her best interests in mind, and she would have done the same thing. “I’m sorry.

sentences.en: But they had never seen the girls fight before, and their concern was evident on their faces. “Hmm, I know what you need.” Elsa reached for the satchel that Anna carried and tugged on the corner of their mother’s scarf dangling from the side.

sentences.en: She pulled it out of the bag and wrapped it around her sister’s shoulders.
sentences.zh: 她把围巾从包里抽出来，披在妹妹肩上。

sentences.zh: 周围的北地人倒吸一口气，转头彼此低语。

sentences.zh: 耶拉娜穿过人群，走近艾莎和安娜，然后举起一只手示意大家安静。

sentences.zh: 安娜和艾莎转向他们，纳闷大家为何都盯着看。“那条围巾你从哪儿来的？”耶拉娜问。

sentences.zh: 一男一女两个年轻的北地人凑近了些。

sentences.en: They seemed curious to hear the answer to Yelana’s question.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎很想听耶拉娜这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: Anna stared at the young woman until it hit her…she was the one who had challenged them initially, with her staff.
sentences.zh: 安娜盯着那年轻女子，忽然想起来了……最初用杖拦住他们的，就是她。

sentences.en: They nodded to each other in greeting. “I’m Honeymaren,” she said. “And that is my brother, Ryder.” Ryder stepped forward—with a smile, but also with curiosity all over his face. “That’s a Northuldra scarf,” he said.
sentences.zh: 两人点头致意。“我是霍妮玛伦，”她说，“那是我哥哥，莱德。”莱德上前一步——面带微笑，脸上却也写满好奇。“那是北地人的围巾，”他说。

chapters.title: 第25章
chapters.en:
“What?” Anna asked in surprise.

“Scarves like these,” Honeymaren said, gesturing to the scarf that Anna wore, “were given to a child at birth. This is from one of our oldest families.”

Anna and Elsa stared at one another, both feeling overwhelmed. “It was our mother’s,” Anna said.

Elsa had an idea coming to her. She grabbed her sister’s hand and pulled her through the brush. The others followed, wondering where they were going. The sisters rushed up to the ice sculpture of the young Northuldra girl holding their father as a boy.

“Elsa…,” Anna said as she touched the icy face of the girl and the scarf she wore.

Elsa examined the sculpture more closely. “I see it. That’s Mother.”

They turned to each other, a realization hitting them. “Mother saved father’s life that day,” Anna said, announcing the truth for the very first time.

After a moment, Elsa turned to Yelana, and the rest of the people gathered around them. “Our mother was Northuldra.”

The silence was widespread as everyone tried to understand what they had just heard.

“What?” Mattias asked softly.

“I knew she was Northuldra,” Ryder said to no one in particular. “I could just feel it. I have…I have a way.”

And then the wind stirred through the trees, creating a harmony of nature as it wound through the leaves and branches. The ice sculptures twinkled and glistened with a magical glow, drawing everyone’s attention to them. Even Olaf began to glow as the owls and animals of the night called out to the forest in song.

Olaf sang along. “Oooohhh…”

Yelana was speechless. An elder Northuldra put a hand on the shoulder of another Northuldra. That person then reached for the person in front of him and placed his hand on her shoulder. The others followed, all of them connecting with each other one by one. They began to sing a song of their people that filled the forest with a deep sense of belonging and hope.

The Arendellian soldiers stood on the outer edges, on guard. Olaf put one hand on Kristoff and the other on Sven. He wasn’t exactly sure what the Northuldra were doing, but he wanted to make sure they were a part of it, too. He even sang along, though he didn’t know what the words were. He was happy that the danger of the Fire Spirit was gone.

Ryder and Honeymaren were near the front of their group. They each put a hand on Yelana’s shoulder. Yelana looked at Anna and Elsa. She reached for their hands and held them in her own.

“We are called Northuldra. We are the people of the sun,” she said, accepting that these people were part of her family. Anna and Elsa nodded, filled with emotion.

Mattias stepped forward, seeing the feelings on their faces. He stopped and waited.

“I promise you,” Elsa said to Yelana, “I will free this forest and restore Arendelle.” She turned to Mattias to acknowledge him as well.

Anna was surprised by Elsa’s promise. It was a vow for her sister to keep, not the two of them. Something in her stomach twisted.

“That’s a pretty big promise, Elsa,” she said, trying to keep the hurt to herself.

The rumble of voices started low at first, Arendellian mixing with Northuldra, then got louder as the hope of the mist falling spread through the crowd.

“We’re getting out of here!” Ryder shouted, and people all around him laughed gleefully. “What! I’m excited about it!” He turned to Krisotff. “It’s just…some of us were born in here. We’ve never even seen an open sky.”

“Hey, I get it,” Kristoff said, patting his new friend on the shoulder.

“Thanks,” Ryder said. “Thank you for saving the reindeer.”

“You bet,” said Kristoff.

“I heard the voice again,” Elsa said, smiling at Yelana. “We need to go north.”

“But the Earth Giants now roam the north at night,” Honeymaren warned.

“They sleep by day,” Yelana advised. “You can leave in the morning.”

“什么？”安娜惊讶地问。“像这样的围巾，”霍妮玛伦指了指安娜身上的围巾，“是孩子一出生就收到的。

这条出自我们最古老的家族之一。”安娜和艾莎对视，都心潮起伏。“这是我们母亲的，”安娜说。

艾莎心里冒出一个念头。

她抓住妹妹的手，拉着她穿过灌木。

其他人跟在后面，不知她们要去哪儿。

姐妹俩冲到那座冰雕前——正是扶着少年父亲的北地少女。“艾莎……”安娜摸着少女冰冷的脸和她戴的围巾，开口道。

艾莎更仔细地打量冰雕。“我看到了。

那是母亲。”两人面面相觑，恍然大悟。“那天是母亲救了父亲的命，”安娜说，第一次道出这个真相。

片刻后，艾莎转向耶拉娜和围拢过来的众人。“我们的母亲是北地人。”全场陷入沉默，人人都在消化刚听到的话。“什么？”马蒂亚斯轻声问。“我早知道她是北地人，”莱德也不知在对谁说，“我就是感觉得到。

我……我有这种感应。”接着，风穿过树林，在枝叶间缠绕，奏出自然的和鸣。

冰雕闪烁着魔法般的光辉，把大家的目光都吸了过去。

连奥拉夫也泛起光来，夜里的猫头鹰和野兽以歌声回应森林。

奥拉夫跟着唱。“哦——哦——”耶拉娜说不出话来。

一位年长的北地人把手搭在另一个北地人肩上。

那人又伸手搭在前面那人的肩上。

其他人纷纷效仿，一个接一个地彼此相连。

他们唱起本族人的歌，让森林充满深沉的归属感与希望。

阿伦黛尔的士兵守在外围，保持警戒。

奥拉夫一只手搭在克斯托夫身上，另一只搭在斯文身上。

他不太确定北地人在做什么，但想确保自己这边也没被落下。

他甚至跟着唱，尽管根本不知道词儿。

他高兴火灵的威胁总算过去了。

莱德和霍妮玛伦站在队伍的靠前位置。

他们各自把一只手搭在耶拉娜肩上。

耶拉娜看向安娜和艾莎。

她伸手握住她们的手。“我们叫北地人。

我们是太阳的子民，”她说，承认这些人也是她的族人。

安娜和艾莎含泪点头。

马蒂亚斯上前，看出了她们脸上的神情。

他停下脚步等着。“我向您保证，”艾莎对耶拉娜说，“我会让这片森林重获自由，也会重建阿伦黛尔。”她又转向马蒂亚斯，也向他表明心迹。

安娜对艾莎的承诺感到意外。

这本该是姐姐一人的誓言，不是她们两人的。

她心里一阵纠结。“这可是个不小的承诺，艾莎，”她说，把受伤的感觉藏了起来。

低低的议论声先起，阿伦黛尔话混着北地话，随后越来越高——迷雾将散的希望传遍人群。“我们要出去了！”莱德大喊，周围的人开心地笑起来。“什么！

我兴奋还来不及呢！”他转向克斯托夫，“只是……我们当中有的人生在里头。

我们连开阔的天空都没见过。”“嘿，我懂，”克斯托夫拍拍新朋友肩膀说。“谢了，”莱德说，“谢谢你救了驯鹿。”“没问题，”克斯托夫说。“我又听见那声音了，”艾莎对耶拉娜微笑着说，“我们得往北走。”“可大地巨人如今夜里在北面游荡，”霍妮玛伦提醒。“它们白天睡觉，”耶拉娜建议，“你们早上再出发。”

chapters.title: 第26章
chapters.en:
As everyone returned to the Northuldra camp, they were relieved to see that the damage from the Fire Spirit was not what they had imagined. Many hands tidied up in an atmosphere of celebration and thanks, relief and joy. The Northuldra and the Arendellians gathered to take a moment to recognize how important life is and how grateful they should be for each day. As music filled the air, everyone enjoyed warm drinks and bowls of steaming stew.

Near where the cooking was taking place, some of the Northuldra toddlers gathered around Olaf. At first they just looked at him curiously. He was quite different from anyone they’d ever seen before. Then one bold little girl moved forward and poked his body. She seemed surprised that he was cold to the touch.

Olaf was thrilled to spend time with the little ones. And as they got more comfortable being around him, they drifted closer and began pulling at his arms, legs, and even at his nose. Olaf talked to them the whole time.

“Hey, let me ask you,” he began, “how do you guys cope with the ever-increasing complexity of thought that comes with maturity—”

Olaf was interrupted when one of the kids grabbed his carrot nose and stuffed it up his own nose. All the kids giggled.

“Brilliant!” Olaf said. “It is so refreshing to get to talk to the youth of today. Our future is in bright hands.”

But the children didn’t respond with words. Some of them began to chew on him. Others took his feet off and placed them on top of his head. That made them laugh, too. Then a girl took a foot from his head and began to bite on it.

“No, no, no, don’t chew that,” he warned. “You don’t know what I’ve stepped in.”

Kristoff and Ryder were in a different part of the camp, near makeshift tables made from old barrels. Kristoff fumbled in his pocket and pulled out the ring he planned to give to Anna. He showed it to Ryder.

“The mountain trolls mined it out of the core of the Black Mountains,” Kristoff said.

Ryder was shocked. “You know mountain trolls?”

“I was raised by mountain trolls,” Kristoff announced proudly.

“Oh, I’ve got to get out of this forest,” Ryder said. It wasn’t a bad life, but he had never been out of the forest because of the mist and had always wondered what he was missing on the other side of it.

“I can’t seem to get her attention,” Kristoff complained, “or even say the right thing.”

“Well, you’re in luck; I know absolutely nothing about women, but I do know that we have the most amazing way of proposing,” Ryder said. “It’ll definitely get her attention. If we start now, you’ll be ready by dawn.”

“Really?” Kristoff asked in amazement.

Ryder grabbed his new friend’s arm and pulled him. “Let’s just say it involves a lot of reindeer.”

Kristoff’s eyes widened and he broke into a grin. “Ooohhh.”

They sneaked past Anna and Mattias, who stood at the edge of the encampment eating stew. Mattias was alert, always watching, always scanning. He never seemed to let down his guard.

“He was about your height,” Anna said to the lieutenant. She was happy to stand with him and eat stew while he kept watch. She respected him because she would never have been born if he hadn’t saved her father all those years before. And she was grateful that Mattias had taken such good care of her father when he was a young men. It was hard for Anna to believe that he’d been stuck in the Enchanted Forest for longer than she had been alive.

“That tall, huh,” Mattias asked, thinking back to the boy he used to know. There were moments when it was hard for him to reconcile his own memories of Agnarr with the information Anna and Elsa shared with him.

“You meant a lot to him. Whenever we’d get butter biscuits from Blodgets’ Bakery, he’d say, ‘Mattias could never get enough of these.’ ”

“It’s the butter…,” Mattias said. He had given up hope long before of ever getting back to the things he loved. But now with Anna and Elsa there in the forest…the hope had returned. “Hey, back at home—Halima still over at Hudson’s Hearth?”

“She is,” Anna said.

Mattias couldn’t believe it. So many years had passed! “Really? She married?” He asked. Anna shook her head no. “Oh, wow. Why doesn’t that make me feel better?”

“What else do you miss?” Anna asked.

“My father,” he answered without hesitation. “He passed long before all this. He was a great man. Built us a good life in Arendelle, but taught me to never take the good for granted. He’d say, ‘Be prepared—just when you think you’ve found your way, life will throw you onto a new path.’ ”

“What do you do when it does?” Anna asked.

“Don’t give up,” he said. “Take it one step at a time, and…”

“Just do the next right thing?” Anna added, remembering what Grand Pabbie had told her.

“Yeah,” Matthias said with a smile. “You got it.” Then he saw the concern on Anna’s face as she watched Elsa walk past with Honeymaren.

大家回到北地人的营地，松了口气——火灵造成的破坏并不像想象中那么严重。

许多双手在庆祝、感恩、宽慰与喜悦的气氛中收拾打扫。

北地人和阿伦黛尔人聚在一起，静心体味生命的可贵，感念每一天。

乐声洋溢，人人喝着热饮，吃着热气腾腾的炖菜。

在煮食的附近，几个北地小孩围住了奥拉夫。

起初他们只是好奇地打量他。

他和他们见过的任何人都不一样。

接着一个胆大的小女孩走上前，戳了戳他的身子。

摸到他冰凉的身子，她似乎很意外。

奥拉夫能和小朋友们待在一起，开心极了。

他们跟他越来越熟，凑得更近，开始扯他的胳膊、腿，甚至鼻子。

奥拉夫一直跟他们说话。“嘿，问你们个事，”他开口，“你们是怎么应对随着年龄增长、思想越来越复杂这档子事的——”一个小孩一把抓过他的胡萝卜鼻子，塞进自己鼻孔里，打断了他。

孩子们咯咯笑。“妙啊！”奥拉夫说，“能跟如今的年轻人聊聊天，真让人耳目一新。

我们的未来交到一双双灵巧的小手里了。”可孩子们没用话回应。

有几个开始啃他。

别的把他的脚拆下来，顶在脑袋上。

这把他们也逗笑了。

接着一个女孩从他头上取下一只脚开始咬。“不不不，别啃那个，”他警告，“你不知道我都踩过什么。”克斯托夫和莱德在营地另一头，靠近用旧木桶搭的临时桌子。

克斯托夫在兜里摸索，掏出那枚打算送给安娜的戒指。

他给莱德看。“这戒指是山地地精从黑山脉的矿芯里挖出来的，”克斯托夫说。

莱德大吃一惊。“你认识山地地精？”“我是被山地地精养大的，”克斯托夫骄傲地宣布。“哦，我非得走出这片森林不可了，”莱德说。

这日子不算差，可因为迷雾，他从没出过森林，总好奇外面错过了什么。“我好像总引不起她注意，”克斯托夫抱怨，“连句对的话都说不好。”“那你走运了；我对女人一窍不通，但我知道我们有最绝的求婚方式，”莱德说，“绝对能让她注意你。

现在开始练，天亮前你准能准备好。”“真的？”克斯托夫惊讶地问。

莱德一把抓住新朋友的胳膊拽他走。“这么说吧，少不了好多驯鹿。”克斯托夫瞪大眼，咧嘴一笑。“哦——”他们悄悄从安娜和马蒂亚斯身边溜过，那两人正站在营地边喝炖菜。

马蒂亚斯保持警觉，眼观六路。

他似乎从不懈怠。“他大概到你这么高，”安娜对中尉说。

她乐意陪他站着，趁他放哨时吃口炖菜。

安娜难以相信，他被困魔法森林的时间比她整个生命还长。“那么高啊，”马蒂亚斯回想当年那个少年，问道。

每次我们从布洛杰特面包房买黄油饼干，他都说：‘马蒂亚斯吃这些永远吃不腻。’”“是因为黄油……”马蒂亚斯说。

他早就放弃希望，以为再也回不到心爱的一切身边。

可如今安娜和艾莎就在森林里……希望又回来了。“嘿，老家那边——哈丽玛还在哈德逊壁炉馆吗？”“在的，”安娜说。

马蒂亚斯不敢相信。

这么多年过去了！“真的？

她结婚了？”他问。

安娜摇头说没有。“哦，天。

怎么这反而没让我好受点？”“你还想念什么？”安娜问。“我父亲，”他不假思索，“他早在这一切之前就过世了。

他是个了不起的人。

他在阿伦黛尔给了我们好日子，却教我永远别把好运当成理所当然。

chapters.title: 第27章
chapters.en:
Honeymaren and Elsa walked over to the logs around a campfire and sat down. A baby reindeer ran up, nuzzling and rubbing its head on them. Elsa stroked the little reindeer’s back as she thought about everything that had happened since they’d entered the forest.

“I want to show you something. May I?” Honeymaren asked. Elsa nodded. Honeymaren reached for one end of the beautiful burgundy scarf that had belonged to Elsa’s mother and gestured to the snowflakes on it. She identified the symbols on the points of one snowflake. “You know air, fire, water, earth.”

“Yes,” Elsa said.

“But look.” Honeymaren touched a diamond in the center of the snowflake, a symbol Elsa had never noticed before. “There’s a fifth spirit.” Honeymaren smiled at the surprised expression on Elsa’s face. “Said to be a bridge between us and the magic of nature.”

Elsa was shocked. “A fifth spirit?”

“Some say they heard it call out the day the forest fell,” Honeymaren said. She had Elsa’s full attention.

“My father heard it,” said Elsa. “Do you think that’s who’s calling me?” Elsa asked.

“Maybe.” Honeymaren smiled. “Alas, only Ahtohallan knows.”

Elsa smiled back, recalling that her mother had said the same thing to Anna and herself when they were children. “Ahtohallan—” She drew the scarf tightly around her shoulders, remembering the words to the lullaby her mother had soothed them with. She half sang and half spoke the words aloud.

Honeymaren smiled again, recognizing the song and singing along with Elsa.

“Why do lullabies always have to have some terrible warning in them?” Honeymaren asked once they had finished.

“I wonder that all the time,” Elsa said.

Suddenly, the ground shook from a distant boom like thunder. But no lightning followed to electrify the sky.

“Earth Giants,” Honeymaren said.
chapters.zh:
霍妮玛伦和艾莎走到篝火边的木头旁坐下。

一只小驯鹿跑过来，用脑袋蹭她们。

艾莎抚摸小驯鹿的背，回想他们进森林后发生的一切。“我想给你看样东西。

可以吗？”霍妮玛伦问。

艾莎点点头。

霍妮玛伦伸手拈起艾莎母亲那条酒红色美丽围巾的一端，指向上面的雪花图案。

她指出一片雪花尖角上的符号。“你知道的，风、火、水、土。”“嗯，”艾莎说。“可你看。”霍妮玛伦点了点雪花中心的一颗菱形，那是个艾莎从没注意过的符号。“还有第五种精灵。”霍妮玛伦看着艾莎惊讶的表情笑了。“据说它是我们与自然魔法之间的桥梁。”艾莎震惊了。“第五种精灵？”“有人说，森林崩落那天听见它呼喊过，”霍妮玛伦说。

这下她彻底抓住了艾莎的注意力。“我父亲听见了，”艾莎说，“你觉得在召唤我的，就是它吗？”艾莎问。“也许吧。”霍妮玛伦微笑，“唉，只有阿托哈兰知道。”艾莎回以微笑，想起小时候母亲也曾对她们姐妹说过同样的话。“阿托哈兰——”她把围巾紧紧裹在肩上，想起母亲哼来哄她们入睡的摇篮曲歌词。

她半唱半念，把词儿轻声吐出。

霍妮玛伦又笑了，认出这首歌，跟着艾莎一起唱。“为什么摇篮曲里总得带点可怕的警告？”唱完后霍妮玛伦问。“我也一直在想这事，”艾莎说。

忽然，远处一声闷雷般的巨响震得大地发颤。

却没有闪电划破天空。“大地巨人，”霍妮玛伦说。

sentences.zh: 她指出一片雪花尖角上的符号。“你知道的，风、火、水、土。”“嗯，”艾莎说。“可你看。”霍妮玛伦点了点雪花中心的一颗菱形，那是个艾莎从没注意过的符号。“还有第五种精灵。”霍妮玛伦看着艾莎惊讶的表情笑了。“据说它是我们与自然魔法之间的桥梁。”艾莎震惊了。“第五种精灵？”“有人说，森林崩落那天听见它呼喊过，”霍妮玛伦说。

sentences.en: She had Elsa’s full attention. “My father heard it,” said Elsa. “Do you think that’s who’s calling me?” Elsa asked. “Maybe.” Honeymaren smiled. “Alas, only Ahtohallan knows.” Elsa smiled back, recalling that her mother had said the same thing to Anna and herself when they were children. “Ahtohallan—” She drew the scarf tightly around her shoulders, remembering the words to the lullaby her mother had soothed them with.
sentences.zh: 这下她彻底抓住了艾莎的注意力。“我父亲听见了，”艾莎说，“你觉得在召唤我的，就是它吗？”艾莎问。“也许吧。”霍妮玛伦微笑，“唉，只有阿托哈兰知道。”艾莎回以微笑，想起小时候母亲也曾对她们姐妹说过同样的话。“阿托哈兰——”她把围巾紧紧裹在肩上，想起母亲哼来哄她们入睡的摇篮曲歌词。

sentences.en: She half sang and half spoke the words aloud.
sentences.zh: 她半唱半念，把词儿轻声吐出。

sentences.en: Honeymaren smiled again, recognizing the song and singing along with Elsa. “Why do lullabies always have to have some terrible warning in them?” Honeymaren asked once they had finished. “I wonder that all the time,” Elsa said.
sentences.zh: 霍妮玛伦又笑了，认出这首歌，跟着艾莎一起唱。“为什么摇篮曲里总得带点可怕的警告？”唱完后霍妮玛伦问。“我也一直在想这事，”艾莎说。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the ground shook from a distant boom like thunder.
sentences.zh: 忽然，远处一声闷雷般的巨响震得大地发颤。

sentences.en: But no lightning followed to electrify the sky. “Earth Giants,” Honeymaren said.
sentences.zh: 却没有闪电划破天空。“大地巨人，”霍妮玛伦说。

chapters.title: 第28章
chapters.en:
Everyone panicked and scattered in different directions. They doused the cooking fires and grabbed the children. They searched for places to hide from the looming threat.

“What are they doing down here?” Yelana whispered sharply to Elsa.

The ground shook again, as if feet the weight of mountains stomped on it. The giants were close; tree limbs wavered from their heavy breathing. A huge nose parted the limbs and sniffed loudly, searching for a specific scent.

“Hide,” Honeymaren instructed.

Olaf quickly ducked behind a rock, trying to make himself as small as possible. And then he noticed the Fire Spirit. He waved his hands at the salamander, trying to shoo it away. His gestures had the opposite effect: the Fire Spirit ignited!

He gasped in horror. “No, no, shhh,” he said, trying to soothe it. Taking a deep breath, he blew on the crackling flames, but the flames expanded, engulfing the Fire Spirit. “They’re coming. They’re coming!”

He tried blowing on the flames again, yet they continued to spread. Olaf reached for the Fire Spirit. “Ooh. Ooh. Hot. Hot,” he said as he tossed the creature back and forth between his hands. Finally, he put the salamander back down on the rock and looked at it pleadingly. “Unlight that fire,” he begged.

Without warning, the Fire Spirit jumped onto Olaf’s head, turning around three times before lying down on the cold permafrost with a smile. At first Olaf winced in pain. Then he gave a sigh of relief—the fire on the salamander had gone out.

BOOM, BOOM, BOOM.

Everyone in the Earth Giants’ path held their breath and prayed they would just go away. Elsa, intrigued, peeked out from behind the tree. The nose of the one closest to her turned slowly toward her, as if it had caught her scent. A shadow crossed over her as the whole Earth Giant emerged. Before ducking behind the tree, she looked up at its face, intrigued by its sheer size and the velocity with which it moved toward her. Then, without warning, it turned in a different direction and continued walking.

Elsa peeked out from behind the tree again. Realizing the Earth Giant was moving away from their camp, she stepped out and started after it. Anna jumped into her path, her face full of questions.

“Tell me you were not about to follow them,” she whispered.

“What if I can settle them like I did the wind and fire?” Elsa asked.

“Or what if they can crush you before you even get the chance? Remember, the goal is to find the voice, find the truth, and get us home,” Anna reminded her sister.

Olaf ran up just as the Earth Giants faded into the distance. The Fire Spirit was still relaxing comfortably on his head.

“Hey, guys—that was close! But, bright side: the Fire Spirit and I are fast friends. We’re going with the name Bruni. Either that or Sally. Aren’t we, Bruni…or Sally?”

Elsa smiled and Bruni jumped onto her arm and sat on her shoulder. “Good. Watch your twigs, though, Olaf.” She turned to Anna. “The giants sensed me. They may come back here. I don’t want to put anyone at risk again. And you’re right, Anna; we’ve got to find the voice. We’re going now.”

Anna hesitated. “Okay. We’re going. Let me just—”

But Elsa didn’t wait another second for her sister to finish. She went through the camp, with Olaf at her heels, determined to continue her journey north.

Anna looked around the camp. “Where are Kristoff and Sven?” she asked in a panic.

“Oh, yeah. I think they took off with that Ryder guy and a bunch of reindeer,” Olaf said.

“They left?” Anna asked, confused. “Just…just left? Without saying anything?” What could be so important that Kristoff would leave me behind?

Olaf shrugged. “Who knows the ways of men?” He turned and followed Elsa.

Anna glanced back at her sister, getting farther away with each second. Anna didn’t want to leave without Kristoff. But she’d promised to keep Elsa safe.

She raced off and caught up with Olaf. Elsa was ahead of them, pushing through the forest with determination, always aware of the potential dangers all around. Anna did her best to hold her head up and not cry. And when Olaf reached his hand up to her, she gladly took it.
chapters.zh:
人人慌了神，朝不同方向散开。

他们扑灭炊火，抱起孩子。

他们寻找藏身之处，躲避逼近的威胁。“它们到下面来干什么？”耶拉娜急切地低声问艾莎。

地面又震了一下，仿佛有山一般重的脚踩在上面。

巨人很近了；树枝随着它们沉重的呼吸摇曳。

一只巨大的鼻子拨开枝叶，大声嗅着，搜寻某种特定的气味。“藏起来，”霍妮玛伦吩咐。

奥拉夫迅速蹲到岩石后，尽量把自己缩成一团。

这时他注意到了火灵。

他朝小蝾螈挥手，想把它赶走。

他的动作适得其反：火灵点燃了！

他惊恐地倒吸凉气。“不不，嘘——”他说着想安抚它。

他深吸一口气，朝噼啪作响的火苗吹气，火却蔓延开，把火灵整个吞没。“它们来了。

它们来了！”他又朝火吹，可火仍在扩散。

奥拉夫伸手去够火灵。“嗷。

嗷。

烫。

烫，”他一边说，一边把小家伙两手来回倒。

终于，他把小蝾螈放回岩石上，恳求地望着它。“把火熄掉，”他央求。

火灵毫无预兆地跳上奥拉夫的脑袋，转了三圈，然后笑眯眯地趴在冰凉的永冻冰上。

起初奥拉夫疼得龇牙。

接着他松了口气——蝾螈身上的火灭了。

轰，轰，轰。

大地巨人途经之处的每个人，都屏住呼吸，祈祷它们快快离开。

艾莎好奇，从树后探出头。

离她最近那只的鼻子缓缓转向她，仿佛嗅到了她的气味。

整只大地巨人现身，阴影笼罩了她。

躲回树后之前，她抬头望向它的脸，被它庞大的体型和朝自己冲来的速度吸引住了。

接着，它毫无预兆地转向别处，继续前行。

艾莎又从树后探出头。

她发现大地巨人正远离营地，便走出去，跟了上去。

安娜跳出来挡住她，脸上写满疑问。“告诉我你不是要跟上去，”她低声说。“要是我能像驯服风与火那样安抚它们呢？”艾莎问，“可要是它们没等你靠近就把你碾碎呢？

记住，我们的目标是找到声音、找到真相，然后回家，”安娜提醒姐姐。

大地巨人渐渐远去时，奥拉夫跑了过来。

火灵还舒舒服服趴在他头上。“嘿，各位——好险！

不过好的一面是：火灵和我也成铁哥们了。

我们决定叫它布鲁尼。

不然就叫萨莉。

你说是不是，布鲁尼……还是萨莉？”艾莎笑了，布鲁尼跳上她的胳膊，坐在她肩上。“好。

不过当心你的树枝，奥拉夫。”她转向安娜，“那些巨人感应到了我。

它们可能会回来。

我不想再让任何人冒险。

而且你说得对，安娜；我们得找到那个声音。

我们现在就走。”安娜犹豫了。“好吧。

我们走。

让我先——”可艾莎没等妹妹说完。

她穿过营地，奥拉夫紧随其后，决心继续北行。

安娜环顾营地。“克斯托夫和斯文呢？”她慌了，“哦，对。

我想他们是跟那个莱德，还有一群驯鹿一起走了，”奥拉夫说。“他们走了？”安娜不解，“就……就这么走了？

什么都没说？”什么事这么要紧，克斯托夫竟把我丢下？

奥拉夫耸耸肩。“谁搞得懂男人的心思？”他转身去追艾莎。

安娜回头望姐姐，姐姐正一秒比一秒远。

安娜不想没等克斯托夫就走。

可她答应过要护艾莎周全。

她拔腿追赶，赶上了奥拉夫。

艾莎走在前面，坚定地穿过森林，始终留意着四周潜在的危险。

安娜努力昂起头，不让自己哭。

奥拉夫伸手够她时，她欣然握住。
