chapters.title: 第29章
chapters.en:
Kristoff was excited for the day ahead as he stood in a beautiful cove full of wildflowers, watching the sun rise. Stray sunbeams fell on his hair, highlighting the white lichen sprinkled there. He had even put some on Sven, for good luck.

“Okay,” he said. “Everybody ready?”

Among the trees, reindeer surrounded Kristoff in a spiral formation.

Ryder was there, too and knew how to have fun with them. “Ready,” he said in the voice of one of the reindeer.

He changed his voice again. “Um, I could use a rehearsal.”

In another voice, Ryder said, “I love love.”

Kristoff was shocked. “Wait. You talk for them, too?”

Ryder, not ashamed, said, “I do.”

“It’s like you can actually hear what they’re thinking.” Kristoff beamed. The reindeer looked at each other as if they thought the two men were crazy.

“Yeah,” Ryder agreed.

“And then you just say it,” they said simultaneously.

Kristoff was happy to have a friend who thought like him.

They stopped when the sound of footsteps broke the quiet of the morning.

“Okay,” Ryder said in his real voice. “Here she comes.”

Kristoff and Ryder launched into motion. They hit triggers that made flowers fly and butterflies soar in a colorful dance through the air. Kristoff hopped onto a boulder in the middle of a big circle of them. He poked one rock with his toe and it nudged the others to fall in a dazzling domino effect around him.

“Princess Anna of Arendelle, my feisty, fearless, ginger-sweet love, will you marry—” he began.

He froze when Yelana walked into the clearing. She looked around as if she had no idea what to say. “This is so sudden…,” she said. “Um. The princess left with the queen.”

That didn’t make any sense to Kristoff. Why would Anna and Elsa leave? And more important, why would they leave without him?

“What?” asked Kristoff. “Wait, what? What?”

Yelana shrugged. The situation was getting really awkward, and she was ready to leave. She was just a messenger.

“I wouldn’t try to follow,” she said. “They’re long gone.”

Kristoff couldn’t move. “Long gone?”

“Yeah,” she confirmed. “So—we’re heading west, to the lichen meadows. You can come with us if you want.” She turned and walked out of the cove.

Kristoff was shocked. He couldn’t think. He was too embarrassed to meet Ryder’s eyes, knowing that Ryder knew Anna had left the Northuldra camp without even telling him. They had put so much work into this proposal because he was sure that he and Anna were meant to be together forever.

“Hey…,” Ryder said, feeling bad for his new friend. “I’m really sorry that—”

“No, I’m fine,” Kristoff interrupted, lying.

“Yeah. Yup. Okay. I better go pack,” Ryder said. “You coming with?”

“I’ll just, uh— Yeah, I’ll meet you there,” Kristoff promised.

“Okay. You know where you’re going? Right?” Ryder asked.

“Yeah,” he confirmed. “Yeah. I know the woods.”

Ryder nodded and headed for the camp.

Kristoff’s whole body felt numb. He sat on the boulder he’d been standing on and put his head in his hands. Sven nudged him to offer support and to make sure his best friend was okay.

How could she leave me behind? Should I even follow her? Are we growing apart? Kristoff thought. He felt lost without her.

克斯托夫站在一片开满野花的美丽小海湾里，望着朝阳升起，对即将到来的一天满怀期待。

零碎的阳光洒在他的头发上，照出里面点缀着的白色地衣。

他甚至还往斯文身上也撒了些，图个好彩头。"好了，"他说，"大家都准备好了吗？"树林间，驯鹿们以螺旋队形把克斯托夫团团围住。

莱德也在那儿，他可懂得怎么跟它们玩。"准备好了。"他学着驯鹿的嗓音说道。

他换了个声音又说："呃，我得先彩排一下。"接着莱德用另一种声音说："我爱爱情。"克斯托夫惊呆了。"等等——

你连它们的话也替它们说？"莱德毫不害臊地说："没错。""就好像你真的能听见它们在想什么似的。"克斯托夫笑开了花。

驯鹿们你看我我看你，仿佛觉得这两个人疯了。"是啊，"莱德表示同意。"然后你直接替它们说出来就行了。"两人异口同声地说。

克斯托夫很高兴能有个和他想法一样的朋友。

当脚步声打破了清晨的宁静，他们停了下来。"好了，"莱德用自己本来的声音说，"她来了。"克斯托夫和莱德立刻动了起来。

他们触动了机关，让花朵飞起、蝴蝶腾空，在空气中跳起一场五彩斑斓的舞蹈。

克斯托夫跳到那一圈机关正中央的一块大石头上。

他用脚趾轻轻一碰其中一块石头，它便推倒旁边的石头，以令人眼花缭乱的多米诺效应在他四周接连倒下。"阿伦黛尔的安娜公主，我那泼辣、无畏、像生姜般甜美的爱人，你愿意嫁——"他开了口。

当叶拉娜走进空地时，他僵住了。

她环顾四周，仿佛不知该说什么好。"这也太突然了……"她说，"嗯。

王后和公主一起走了。"这话克斯托夫完全听不懂。

安娜和艾莎为什么要走？

更重要的是，她们为什么连他都不告而别？"什么？"克斯托夫问，"等等，你说什么？

什么？"叶拉娜耸了耸肩。

气氛变得实在尴尬，她已经准备离开了。

她只是个传话的。"我劝你别去追，"她说，"她们早就走远了。"克斯托夫呆立不动。"走远了？""对，"她确认道，"所以——我们要往西去地衣草甸。

你愿意的话可以跟我们一起走。"她转过身走出了小海湾。

克斯托夫惊呆了。

他想不出任何头绪。

他羞得不敢去对上莱德的眼神，因为他知道莱德清楚安娜连招呼都没跟他打一声就离开了北地人的营地。

他们为这场求婚准备了那么久，因为他确信自己和安娜注定要永远在一起。"嘿……"莱德说，替这位新朋友感到难过，"我真的很抱歉——""不，我没事，"克斯托夫打断他，说着谎，"是啊。

没错。

好。

我还是去收拾行李吧，"莱德说，"你一起走吗？""我就，呃——行，我待会儿在那儿跟你们会合。"克斯托夫答应道。"好吧。

你知道往哪儿走吧？

对吧？"莱德问。"知道，"他确认道，"知道。

这林子我熟。"莱德点点头，朝营地走去。

克斯托夫浑身麻木。

他坐回刚才站着的那块石头上，双手抱住了头。

斯文用脑袋拱了拱他，给他打气，也想确认最好的朋友是否安好。

她怎么能丢下我？

我到底该不该去追她？

我们是不是在渐行渐远？

克斯托夫想着。

没有了她，他只觉得心里空落落的。

chapters.title: 第30章
chapters.en:
Elsa kept a steady pace ahead of Anna and Olaf. It was hard to tell how long they had been walking, but the night had slowly slid into day as they continued moving north. Bruni ran along on the rocks beside Elsa, stopping periodically to make sure everyone was still there.

Anna could tell that her sister was anxious by the way her eyes darted back and forth, looking at everything. Elsa sang the same haunting melody that had called to her so many times, wanting it to answer back…wanting it to tell her which way to go. Of course, Olaf, not to be left out, tried to copy her, singing in what he thought was the same voice. But it was far from it, and it made Bruni jump into the air and catch fire. The Fire Spirit looked at Olaf grumpily before dousing its flames and scrambling off into the bushes.

The snowman’s off-key singing made Anna grit her teeth, but she tried to be polite.

“Hey, Olaf—um, maybe just one of you should do it,” she suggested.

“I agree,” Olaf said, nodding. He raised a stick hand so he could whisper to Anna behind it. “She’s a little pitchy.”

A soft breeze whirled around him, announcing that the Wind Spirit had returned.

“Hey, Gale’s back,” Olaf said happily.

Gale fluttered around Elsa, getting her attention before drawing their eyes to a tattered flag that was barely visible over one of the hills.

“What…?” Anna said, breathless.

She and Elsa hurried through the trees with Olaf right behind them. They stopped suddenly on the crest of the hill and stared in silence before grabbing each other in shock. It was an Arendellian flag—old and in pieces, and attached to the mast of a ship. The vessel lay shipwrecked and broken in a dry riverbed, its hull ripped open.

Gale swept around the girls and blew toward the ship, pushing against the old, beaten flag, making it wave weakly.

“How can it be?” Anna asked.

Olaf studied the fragmented vessel curiously, not noticing that the girls were upset.

“What is it?” he asked.

“Mother and Father’s ship,” Anna replied softly, hardly believing it.

Olaf was confused. “But this isn’t the Southern Sea.”

“No. No, it isn’t,” Anna said. It didn’t make any sense, and yet there it was. She ran with Elsa down the embankment, desperate to get to the ship, throwing caution behind them. They were too fast for Olaf, but he tumbled after, trying his best to keep up with them.

The broken hull was jagged, but Elsa and Anna didn’t hesitate as they navigated the splintered beams and climbed into the old wooden ship. More than anything, they hoped to find something of their parents’, anything they may have left behind. But their brief moment of hope was soon gone. Everything inside had been destroyed over the years—tossed and mangled, or washed away. They moved silently through the wreckage in heartbroken shock.

“Why is their ship here?” Elsa asked, on the verge of tears. “How is it here?”

They searched deeper, under jagged wooden planks and ripped sails.

“It must have been washed in from the Dark Sea,” Anna guessed, sorting through the mess, her fingers moving faster and faster.

“What were they doing in the Dark Sea?” Elsa asked. She didn’t expect her sister to have an answer.

“I don’t know,” Anna replied. She stopped and stared at Elsa. Everything felt more mysterious than it had before. “So many secrets.”

Olaf’s head popped up over the side of the broken beams. Seeing the girls, he pushed himself the rest of the way in and tumbled into the hull. His head swiveled as he looked around, confused.

“How did the ship get through the mist?” he said. “I thought nobody could but us. Oh…unless nobody was on it.”

Anna needed to concentrate on her sister. “There’s got to be something here…,” she said, refusing to believe they had come this far to find out that all the answers were still hidden. Suddenly, an idea struck her. “Wait. Wait. Look around.” She dropped to her knees and felt around the floor with her hands. “Every Arendellian ship has a compartment. Waterproof.”

Anna’s words pushed Elsa into action. She ran her hands over the walls, looking for any sign of a compartment.

“That’s very clever,” Olaf said. “Although it does make me wonder why they don’t just make the whole ship waterproof.”

“Here,” Anna said. Her finger went into a small notch near the floor. It clicked and a hatch opened. Olaf and Elsa went to her in anticipation as Anna reached inside and pulled out a round glass tube. She uncorked it and removed a roll of parchments covered in mysterious text. “What language is this?”

“I don’t know,” Elsa said, glancing at some words in the margins. She pointed to them. “But look—this is Mother’s handwriting.”

Anna read the words out loud. “ ‘The end of the ice age…The river found but lost…Magic’s source. Elsa’s source?’ ”

Elsa took the parchment from her and read the mention of herself.

Anna opened another parchment. “It’s a map,” she said. Anna unrolled it carefully and gently spread it out on the floor. Elsa joined her and they looked at it together.

The map showed Arendelle, the Enchanted Forest, the Dark Sea, and what lay beyond. A crude line marked the mist, with question marks along its northern border. Dotted lines marked a route up the fjord.

“They traveled north to the Dark Sea, to—” Anna stopped short when the dotted lines crossed the sea to a small island, labeled again in their mother’s unique handwriting.

Elsa recognized the word. “Ahtohallan…”

“It’s real?” Anna asked.

“Ahto-who-what?” Olaf asked.

“Ahtohallan,” Elsa corrected him. “It’s a magical river said to hold all the answers about the past.”

Olaf felt proud that he had been right. “Reinforcing my water-has-memory theory—”

“Water has memory,” Elsa whispered. She closed her eyes and pressed her hands to the floor. She used her power to pull moisture from the old wooden beams, the air, and the floorboards.

“Elsa?” Anna said, “What are you doing?”

“I want to know what happened to them,” Elsa said.

A lacy, life-size ice sculpture formed in front of them, a perfect replica of their parents, dancing together and looking lovingly at each other. The sisters moved around it, taking in every detail.

Gale swept past them again and around the sculpture. As it swirled, echoes of distant voices filled the ship.

“Ahtohallan has to be the source of her magic,” said the distant, distorted voice of the girls’ mother in a memory from long before.

“If we know why Elsa has powers, we can help her,” their father said.

Elsa had an idea. She moved through the ship and placed her hands on a wall. Another sculpture formed, a replica of her parents sitting at a table, looking over a map.

“Do you really think the past can save Elsa’s future?” her father asked.

“No,” her mother replied, “but I think understanding what she’s a part of can.”

Elsa backed away from the sculpture, realizing that all of this was about her. Gale swept through the ship. Elsa followed it to the helm, understanding what she was supposed to do. She put her hands on either side of the doorframe and closed her eyes.

A sculpture began to form in front of her from the ground up. It was a wave.

“They look so scared,” Elsa said as Gale spun around the sculpture.

“The waves are too high,” Queen Iduna said.

“We keep going for Elsa,” King Agnarr replied as a wave crashed onto the deck. “Id una!”

“Agnarr!” she shouted back.

“I love you!” he cried.

“I love you!” she answered.

Elsa’s parents held each other as another wave overtook them. Elsa couldn’t watch anymore and bolted from the ship.

“Elsa!” Anna called as she ran after her sister.
chapters.zh:
艾莎走在安娜和奥拉夫前面，步履稳健。

走了多久已难分辨，但他们一路向北，夜色已悄然滑入了白昼。

布伦尼在艾莎身旁的岩石上一路小跑，不时停下来确认大家是否还跟得上。

从姐姐目光来回游移、四下张望的模样，安娜看得出来她很不安。

艾莎唱起那支呼唤过她无数次的幽婉旋律，盼着它回应……盼着它告诉自己该往哪走。

当然，奥拉夫可不愿被冷落，也学着她的样子唱起来，自以为用的是同一种嗓音。

可他差得远了，那声音把布伦尼惊得跳起来，一下子着了火。

火灵没好气地瞪了奥拉夫一眼，才熄灭身上的火焰，慌慌张张钻进灌木丛。

雪人跑调的歌声让安娜咬紧牙关，却还是尽量礼貌。"嘿，奥拉夫——呃，也许你们俩只要一个人唱就行。"她委婉提议。"我同意。"奥拉夫点着头说。

他举起一根树枝做的手，好遮着嘴跟安娜耳语："她有点儿跑调。"一阵轻柔的微风绕着他打转，宣告风灵回来了。"嘿，盖尔回来了。"奥拉夫高兴地说。

盖尔绕着艾莎飞舞，引她注意，随后把大家的目光引向一面破破烂烂、在小山丘上几乎看不清的旗子。"那是什么……？"安娜屏住呼吸说。

她和艾莎急忙穿过树林，奥拉夫紧紧跟在后面。

他们在山顶上猛地停住，先是一言不发地盯着看，接着惊愕地互相抓住了对方。

那是阿伦黛尔的旗帜——又旧又破，挂在了一艘船的桅杆上。

那艘船残破地搁浅在干涸的河床里，船身裂开着大口。

盖尔绕过两个女孩，朝那艘船吹去，拂动那面破旧的老旗，让它有气无力地飘了飘。"怎么会这样？"安娜问。

她没指望妹妹答得上来。"我不知道。"安娜答道。

她停下动作，盯着艾莎。

一切都比先前更扑朔迷离了。"这么多秘密。"奥拉夫的脑袋从破木板的边缘探了出来。

哦……除非上面根本没人。"安娜得把心思放在姐姐身上。"这里一定还藏着什么东西……"她说，不愿相信她们走了这么远，答案却依旧被掩埋。

等等。

四处看看。"她跪倒在地，用手在船板上摸索。"每艘阿伦黛尔的船都有个暗格。

防水的。"安娜的话让艾莎行动起来。

sentences.en: As it swirled, echoes of distant voices filled the ship. “Ahtohallan has to be the source of her magic,” said the distant, distorted voice of the girls’ mother in a memory from long before. “If we know why Elsa has powers, we can help her ,” their father said.
sentences.zh: 随着它盘旋，遥远的声音在船中回荡。那是许久以前一段记忆里、母亲那缥缈而失真的嗓音："阿托哈兰一定是她魔法的源头。""如果我们弄清艾莎为什么拥有魔力，就能帮她。"父亲说道。

sentences.en: Elsa’s parents held each other as another wave overtook them.
sentences.zh: 艾莎的父母相拥着，被又一个浪头吞没。

sentences.en: Elsa couldn’t watch anymore and bolted from the ship. “Elsa!” Anna called as she ran after her sister.

chapters.title: 第31章
chapters.en:
Elsa doubled over on the dry riverbank, tears running down her face. She felt completely overwhelmed by what she had seen on the ship. She missed her parents more than ever. She had always known they had not survived, but now she had proof.

Anna came to Elsa’s side, putting a hand on her back as she spoke softly to her. “Hey, hey, hey. What are you doing?”

“This is my fault,” Elsa confessed, her voice choked with emotion. “They were looking for answers about me.”

Anna did what she could to comfort her. “You are not responsible for their choices, Elsa.”

“No, just their deaths,” she lamented.

“Stop,” Anna demanded. “No. Yelana asked why would the spirits reward Arendelle with a magical queen? Because our mother saved our father. She saved her enemy. Her good deed was rewarded with you. You are a gift.”

Elsa looked up at her sister. “For what?” she asked softly.

“If anyone can resolve the past, if anyone can save Arendelle and free this forest, it’s you,” Anna explained. “I believe in you, Elsa, more than anyone or anything.”

Elsa clasped Anna’s hands tightly, grateful for her sister’s words of encouragement. She took a moment to dry her tears as she made a decision. “Honeymaren said there was a fifth spirit, a bridge between the magic of nature and us.”

“A fifth spirit?” Anna asked, surprised that Elsa hadn’t told her about it before.

“That’s who’s been calling me…from Ahtohallan. The answers about the past are all there.”

“So we go to Ahtohallan,” Anna said.

Elsa did have a plan to go to Ahtohallan. But that plan did not involve her sister.

“Not we. Me,” she said.

Anna didn’t like Elsa’s answer at all. They were supposed to take this journey together. Grand Pabbie had entrusted her to protect Elsa, and even if he hadn’t, Anna would have never let her sister go off alone. And now to hear her say that was exactly what she wanted to do, Anna wanted answers. “What?”

“The Dark Sea is too dangerous for us both,” Elsa warned.

“No,” Anna insisted. “No. We do this together. Remember the song? Who will stop you from going too far?”

“You said you believed in me,” Elsa reminded her. “That this is what I was born to do.”

“And I don’t want to stop you from that,” Anna assured her. “I don’t want to stop you from being whatever you need to be!” She made one last attempt to make Elsa see things her way. “I just don’t want you dying…trying to be everything for everyone else, too. Don’t do this alone. Let me help you. Please. I can’t lose you, Elsa.”

Elsa looked at her with weary eyes. “I can’t lose you, either, Anna.” She hugged her sister and motioned for Olaf to join them. “Come on,” she encouraged him.

After Olaf had joined Anna, Elsa used her powers to quickly blast a small ice path that flowed along the dry riverbed.

我们要一起完成这件事。

还记得那首歌吗？

谁会拦住你、不让你走太远？""你说过相信我，"艾莎提醒她，"说这是我生来要做的事。""我并不想拦住你去做这个，"安娜向她保证，"我不想阻止你成为你想要成为的任何样子！"她做最后一次努力，想让艾莎明白她的心意。"我只是不想让你……也为了别人拼尽一切而送了命。

别一个人去。

让我帮你。

求你了。

我不能失去你，艾莎。"艾莎用疲惫的眼神望着她。"我也不能失去你，安娜。"她抱住妹妹，招呼奥拉夫也过来。"来吧。"她鼓励他。

奥拉夫靠到安娜身边后，艾莎用魔力迅速开辟出一条顺着干河床延伸的冰路。

chapters.title: 第32章
chapters.en:
“Wait, what?” Anna asked, confused.

But Elsa wasn’t done. Next, she created an iceboat right under Anna’s and Olaf’s feet. They fell back into it. Once they were seated, Elsa waved her hand to send them racing down the icy path she had created.

“What are you doing?” Anna cried. “Elsa!” She threw out her arms and did whatever she could to stop them from sliding along the ice path. “No! No! Olaf, help me stop. GIVE ME A HAND!”

He yanked one of his arms off and gave it to her. Anna stared at it, then she shook it. What was she supposed to do with it? How was it going to help them stop and get back to Elsa?

Anna spotted a tree with a low-hanging branch up ahead. “Hang on!” she said. She held up Olaf’s arm and let his hand grab the branch. The boat swiveled as it changed course and flew up onto dry land. Anna and Olaf were relieved that her plan had worked!

They both breathed a sigh of relief. But neither of them had counted on the speed of their iceboat, which continued to push them over a slope and down a hill. Then they splashed into a river.

“Wait,” Anna said frantically. “Wait. No. No. No!” The boat raced even faster down the river than it had down the ice path. It began to spin. “Oh, come on!” Anna shouted angrily.

“Anna,” Olaf said, “this might sound crazy, but I’m sensing some rising anger.”

Anna hit a tree when the boat rotated. “Argh! Well, I am angry, Olaf,” Anna admitted. “She promised me we’d do this together!”

That wasn’t what Olaf had meant. “Ya-huh. But what I mean is I’m sensing rising anger in me.”

Anna paused in trying to stop the boat and gave the little snowman her full attention.

“Wait, you’re angry?” she asked.

“Um…I think so?” Olaf said uncertainly. “Elsa pushed me away, too. And didn’t even say goodbye.”

Anna understood then that Olaf was just like her. “And you have every right to be very, very mad at her.”

“And,” he said with panic on his face. “You said some things never change, but since then everything’s done nothing but change.”

Seeing how this had affected her friend, Anna let go of her anger. “I know. But look, I’m still here holding your hand.”

Olaf felt a little better. “Yeah. That’s a good…that’s a good point, Anna. But there’s one more thing. Please, don’t leave me, too. Your parents left you both, and we left Kristoff and Sven, and then Elsa left us…and if you leave, then—”

She knew he was troubled and she needed to ease his fears. “Hey, hey, hey—I’m not going to leave you, Olaf…. Not ever.”

“Promise?” he asked.

“I promise.” Anna still had the arm he had given her to try to stop the iceboat. The pinky on the hand wiggled.

“Pinky swear,” he said.

“Pinky swear,” she confirmed, wrapping her pinky around his and shaking it.

An odd thought occurred to Olaf. “Did you ever notice that our smallest finger contains our most positive swear power, while our longest finger contains our most nega—”

Anna slammed a hand over his mouth. “Olaf. No. Shhh!” The banks of the river were covered in sleeping Earth Giants.

He didn’t see them at first. “Don’t shush me. That’s rude and—” Then he saw them and lowered his voice to a whisper. “Oh, the giants…. They’re huge.”

Anna and Olaf silently glided past them. Anna saw up ahead that the river split into two paths. One path was lined with Earth Giants. The other led to a waterfall.

“Hang on, Olaf,” Anna said, having made a split-second decision about which way was best. “Try not to scream.” She reached out and grabbed a branch that redirected them toward the waterfall and away from the giants.

Moments later, they careened down the rushing water toward a pit.

Olaf screamed.
chapters.zh:
"等等，什么？"安娜困惑地问。

可艾莎还没完。

接着，她在安娜和奥拉夫脚底下造出了一艘冰船。

两人一屁股坐了进去。

等他们坐稳，艾莎一挥手，让他们顺着她造的冰路飞驰而去。"你在干什么？"安娜大叫，"艾莎！"她张开双臂，拼命想阻止他们顺着冰路滑走。"不！

不！

奥拉夫，快帮我停下。

搭把手！"他一把扯下自己的胳膊，递给她。

安娜盯着那只胳膊，然后摇了摇它。

她拿这玩意儿能做什么？

它怎么帮他们停下来、回到艾莎身边？

安娜看到前头有棵树，低垂的树枝横在路中。"撑住！"她说。

她举起奥拉夫的胳膊，让他的手抓住那根树枝。

冰船一转方向，斜飞上了干涸的岸地。

安娜和奥拉夫松了口气——她的办法奏效了！

两人都长长地舒了口气。

可谁也没料到冰船的速度，它继续推着他们冲过斜坡、滑下山坡。

接着他们扑通溅进了一条河里。"等等，"安娜慌乱地说，"等等。

不。

不。

不！"冰船在河里比在冰路上冲得更快。

船开始打转。"噢，够了！"安娜气恼地喊。"安娜，"奥拉夫说，"这话听着可能荒唐，可我感觉到一阵升腾的怒气。"船打着旋，安娜撞上了一棵树。"啊！

好吧，我确实在生气，奥拉夫。"安娜承认，"她答应过要和我一起做这件事的！"奥拉夫指的不是这个。"呀——哈。

我是说，我感觉到我自己的怒气也在升腾。"安娜停下阻止船的动作，全神贯注地看着小雪人。"等等，你在生气？"她问。"嗯……我想是吧？"奥拉夫不确定地说，"艾莎也把我推开了。

连再见都没说。"安娜这才明白，奥拉夫和她一样。"那你完全有权利对她非常、非常生气。""而且，"他脸上带着慌张，"你说过有些事永不改变，可自那以后，所有事都在变。"看到这话对朋友的影响，安娜放下了自己的怒气。"我知道。

不过你看，我还在这儿握着你的手呢。"奥拉夫心里好受些了。"是啊。

这倒是个……不错的道理，安娜。

不过还有一件事。

求求你，也别丢下我。

你父母抛下了你们俩，我们抛下了克斯托夫和斯文，然后艾莎又抛下了我们……你要是也走了，那——"她知道他正不安，得安抚他的恐惧。"嘿，嘿，嘿——我不会离开你的，奥拉夫……

永远都不会。""你发誓？"他问。"我发誓。"安娜手里还拿着他扯下来想阻止冰船的那只胳膊。

那只手的小拇指动了动。"拉钩发誓。"他说。"拉钩发誓。"她应着，勾住他的小拇指晃了晃。

奥拉夫冒出一个古怪的念头。"你有没有发现，咱们最小的手指拥有的誓约力量最正，而最长的手指拥有的却是最负——"安娜一把捂住他的嘴。"奥拉夫。

不。

嘘！"河两岸趴满了沉睡的地灵巨人。

他起初没看见。"别叫我闭嘴。

chapters.title: 第33章
chapters.en:
Anna slammed two rocks together and created a spark to light a piece of driftwood. The Lost Caverns that the waterfall had deposited them in lit up. She spotted Olaf’s carrot and reached to grab it out of the water as it floated by. “Found it.”

She carried the torch back to Olaf. He was putting his body back together on the shore of a pool of water. The broken iceboat and Anna’s wet cloak were next to him. Anna pushed Olaf’s carrot back into his face.

He spit out a fish and a mouthful of river water. “Thank you. Where are we?” he asked.

Anna looked up at the waterfall. “In a pit with no way out?”

Olaf spotted a dark opening behind a rock and ran to it. “But with a spooky, pitch-black way in.” He smiled back at her as he pointed to it.

Anna approached him and looked into the opening. She couldn’t decide if it was worth the risk of whatever was inside. They could wait in the pit for help, but how would anyone ever find them down there?

Olaf grabbed her hand and gave a little tug. “Come on,” he said. “It’ll be fun, assuming we don’t get stuck here forever, no one ever finds us, and you starve and I give up.”

Anna hesitated and looked around for another way out. But after seeing nothing else, she sighed and gave Olaf a nod. She held tightly to his hand and stepped into the darkness.

“But, bright side: Elsa’s gotta be doing a whole lot better than we are,” Olaf said, sounding hopeful.

chapters.title: 第34章
chapters.en:
Elsa stood on the shore of a dark, rocky beach that night while the wind whipped her hair around her face. The ferocious waves rose high and crashed before her on the shore like thunder. She gazed out across the waters and saw an icy landmass in the far distance. She had done it. She had made it to the Dark Sea. Now she just had to make it across.

Determined, Elsa removed her coat and boots. She released her hair from its braid and tied it behind her neck before taking a deep breath. She sprinted toward the tumbling waves. Frozen snowflakes radiated from each footfall, supporting her weight.

Twenty feet from the shoreline, the waves overtook her, knocking her down and shattering the ice she’d made.

Elsa was not going to give up. Dripping wet, she started over. She ran full force at the sea. She got past the first set of waves by leaping onto a large rock that sat a short distance from the shore. Then she froze the seawater that crashed against the rock and used it to make a slide to gain speed for her attack on the second set of waves.

One of those waves was colossal, however. It soared high above her. Elsa tried to freeze it, but it was too powerful. The ice wall she had attempted to create crashed on top of her, plunging her beneath the surface.

In the darkness underwater, waves continued to roll overhead. Lightning flashed, brilliantly illuminating the depths of the sea around her as she headed for the surface. But when the second electrical strike lit up the sky, it also showed what appeared to be a huge, ferocious horse deep in the water below. The horse swam up and looked her in the eye. Lightning struck again and the horse, the Water Spirit, was gone.

Elsa clawed her way to the surface. Waves tossed her as she looked down to see the Water Nokk galloping up from the depths, heading straight for her. She created an ice sheet to float on top of the water’s surface, and pulled herself onto it just in time for the Water Spirit to ram her vessel and send her careening into the air.

Struggling to breathe, Elsa turned to see the horse attacking again.

Its hooves drove her underwater. She tried to break free as it pushed her deeper and deeper. She grabbed onto the Water Nokk’s hooves and froze the horse. It resisted, and then the Water Spirit shattered into billions of particles of ice.

Elsa swam straight up, hoping to get away before the Water Nokk re-formed itself. She reached the surface, but the horse was right there and threw her out of the water.

Lightning flashed.

Elsa created a giant ice wave that collapsed onto the Water Nokk.

Lightning flashed again.

Underwater, Elsa made an ice shield to block the horse. It burst through the shield as if nothing were there at all.

Lightning flashed once more.

Above the water, the Water Nokk grabbed Elsa’s arm and dragged her through the waves. She fought to breathe. Desperate, she used her magic to throw out an ice bridle. It hooked onto the Water Spirit’s mouth and head. She swung around and landed on the horse’s back.

The Water Nokk panicked and bucked. But Elsa yanked on the reins and tried to gain control. The horse surfaced and turned toward the icy landmass that Elsa had seen in the distance. It ran, fighting, trying to throw her off, refusing to give in to her commanding hold.

Elsa pulled the reins tighter and pressed her legs down harder until the horse responded. Finally, its stride evened out and she relaxed her grip. They moved together, Elsa and the Water Nokk.

The icy landmass came into view ahead. It appeared to be an island. As Elsa got closer, she realized it was more than an island. It was a giant glacier that sparkled with magic. She was overwhelmed with joy.

“Of course,” she whispered. “Glaciers are rivers of ice.” The voice she had longed to reach called out to her, closer than ever. “Ahtohallan is frozen.” All she had to do was reach the secret river.

The voice continued to call to her, filling her ears. It sounded almost joyful, as if it knew she was near.

“I hear you,” Elsa said, “and I’m coming.”

She snapped the reins and the Water Nokk quickened its pace.

Elsa couldn’t stop trembling with anticipation as she approached Ahtohallan with the Water Spirit. Knowing the voice that had been calling to her was there gave her comfort.

The Water Nokk turned when they reached the shore, allowing Elsa to leap onto the icy white beach. The ground shimmered when her feet landed. It was a magical response. She felt power emanating all around her. It felt like she was home.

The horse shook its mane and turned back to the Dark Sea, slowly dissipating into the water. Elsa’s eyes moved from it and gazed up at the giant ice cave that stretched endlessly in front of her. She moved toward an opening in the ice that loomed like a fortress.
chapters.zh:
那一夜，艾莎站在黑黢黢、布满岩石的海滩上，海风把她的头发吹得在脸前乱舞。

狂暴的浪头高高掀起，在她面前的岸上如雷般炸开。

她极目远望，看见远方有一片冰封的陆地。

她做到了。

她抵达了暗海。

现在她只需横渡过去。

下定决心，艾莎脱下了外套和靴子。

她解开辫子，把头发在颈后束好，然后深吸一口气。

她朝翻涌的浪涛飞奔而去。

每一步落下都绽开冰晶雪花，托住她的体重。

离岸二十尺时，浪头将她吞没，把她掀倒，也击碎了她造出的冰。

艾莎绝不会放弃。

浑身湿透的她，重新开始。

她全力以赴冲向大海。

她纵身跳上离岸不远的一块巨石，越过了第一波浪。

接着她冻住拍击岩石的海水，用它做成一道滑梯，为自己冲击第二波浪蓄足速度。

可其中一道浪大得惊人。

它高高地凌驾在她头顶。

艾莎想把它冻住，可它太过凶猛。

她试图筑起的冰墙塌下来压在她身上，把她卷入水下。

水下的黑暗里，浪头仍在头顶翻滚。

闪电划过，把她周遭的海底照得通明，她正朝水面游去。

可当第二道闪电照亮天空，也照出了下方深水里一匹巨大而凶猛的马。

那马游上来，与她对视。

闪电再次劈下，那匹马——水灵——就不见了。

艾莎奋力划水，浮上水面。

浪头把她抛起，她低头看见水马正从深处飞驰而上，直冲她而来。

她造出一块浮在水面的冰板，刚把自己拉上去，水灵就撞碎了她的"船"，把她甩上了半空。

艾莎挣扎着喘气，转头看见那马又攻了过来。

马蹄把她踩入水下。

它把她越推越深，她拼命想挣脱。

她抓住水马的蹄子，把马冻住。

它挣扎着，随后水灵碎成了亿万片冰晶。

艾莎径直向上游，想在水马重组之前逃开。

她浮上水面，可那马就在那儿，把她甩出了水面。

闪电划过。

艾莎造出一道巨大的冰浪，朝水马塌压下去。

闪电再次划过。

水下，艾莎筑起冰盾挡住那马。

它如入无人之境，直接撞穿了冰盾。

闪电又是一闪。

水面上，水马咬住艾莎的手臂，拖着她穿过浪涛。

她挣扎着呼吸。

情急之下，她用魔力甩出一副冰做的马勒。

它扣住了水灵的嘴和头。

她一荡身，落到了马背上。

水马惊慌地尥起蹶子。

可艾莎猛拉缰绳，试图制服它。

马浮出水面，转向艾莎先前望见的那片冰封陆地。

它一路狂奔、奋力挣扎，想把她甩下去，不肯向她的掌控屈服。

艾莎把缰绳勒得更紧，双腿压得更沉，直到那马有了反应。

终于，它的步子稳了下来，她也放松了手劲。

艾莎和水马，融为一体般前行。

前方那片冰封陆地已清晰可见。

它看上去像座岛。

艾莎越靠越近，才发觉它不只是一座岛。

那是一块闪耀着魔法的巨大冰川。

她喜不自胜。"原来如此，"她轻声说，"冰川就是冰的河流。"那她渴望触及的声音唤起了她，比以往更近。"阿托哈兰是冻结的。"她只需抵达那条秘密的河。

那声音继续呼唤她，灌满她的耳畔。

它听起来几乎带着喜悦，仿佛知道她已临近。"我听见你了，"艾莎说，"我来了。"她一抖缰绳，水马加快了步伐。

艾莎与那水灵一同逼近阿托哈兰，激动得止不住颤抖。

想到那呼唤她的声音就在那里，她感到安心。

他们抵达岸边时，水马一转身，让艾莎跳上了那片冰白的沙滩。

她的双足落地，地面泛起微光。

那是魔法的回应。

她感到力量从四面八方涌来。

那感觉，就像回到了家。

那马甩了甩鬃毛，转身回到暗海，缓缓化入水中。

艾莎的目光从它身上移开，仰望起眼前延展开去、望不到尽头的巨大冰洞。

她朝那个如堡垒般巍然耸立的冰之入口走去。

sentences.en: Elsa stood on the shore of a dark, rocky beach that night while the wind whipped her hair around her face.
sentences.zh: 那一夜，艾莎站在黑黢黢、布满岩石的海滩上，海风把她的头发吹得在脸前乱舞。

sentences.en: The ferocious waves rose high and crashed before her on the shore like thunder.
sentences.zh: 狂暴的浪头高高掀起，在她面前的岸上如雷般炸开。

sentences.en: She gazed out across the waters and saw an icy landmass in the far distance.
sentences.zh: 她极目远望，看见远方有一片冰封的陆地。

sentences.en: She had done it.
sentences.zh: 她做到了。

sentences.en: She had made it to the Dark Sea.
sentences.zh: 她抵达了暗海。

sentences.en: Now she just had to make it across.
sentences.zh: 现在她只需横渡过去。

sentences.en: Determined, Elsa removed her coat and boots.
sentences.zh: 下定决心，艾莎脱下了外套和靴子。

sentences.en: She released her hair from its braid and tied it behind her neck before taking a deep breath.
sentences.zh: 她解开辫子，把头发在颈后束好，然后深吸一口气。

sentences.en: She sprinted toward the tumbling waves.
sentences.zh: 她朝翻涌的浪涛飞奔而去。

sentences.en: Frozen snowflakes radiated from each footfall, supporting her weight.
sentences.zh: 每一步落下都绽开冰晶雪花，托住她的体重。

sentences.en: Twenty feet from the shoreline, the waves overtook her, knocking her down and shattering the ice she’d made.
sentences.zh: 离岸二十尺时，浪头将她吞没，把她掀倒，也击碎了她造出的冰。

sentences.en: Elsa was not going to give up.
sentences.zh: 艾莎绝不会放弃。

sentences.en: Dripping wet, she started over.
sentences.zh: 浑身湿透的她，重新开始。

sentences.en: She ran full force at the sea.
sentences.zh: 她全力以赴冲向大海。

sentences.en: She got past the first set of waves by leaping onto a large rock that sat a short distance from the shore.
sentences.zh: 她纵身跳上离岸不远的一块巨石，越过了第一波浪。

sentences.en: Then she froze the seawater that crashed against the rock and used it to make a slide to gain speed for her attack on the second set of waves.
sentences.zh: 接着她冻住拍击岩石的海水，用它做成一道滑梯，为自己冲击第二波浪蓄足速度。

sentences.en: One of those waves was colossal, however.
sentences.zh: 可其中一道浪大得惊人。

sentences.en: It soared high above her.
sentences.zh: 它高高地凌驾在她头顶。

sentences.en: Elsa tried to freeze it, but it was too powerful.
sentences.zh: 艾莎想把它冻住，可它太过凶猛。

sentences.en: The ice wall she had attempted to create crashed on top of her, plunging her beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 她试图筑起的冰墙塌下来压在她身上，把她卷入水下。

sentences.en: In the darkness underwater, waves continued to roll overhead.
sentences.zh: 水下的黑暗里，浪头仍在头顶翻滚。

sentences.en: Lightning flashed, brilliantly illuminating the depths of the sea around her as she headed for the surface.
sentences.zh: 闪电划过，把她周遭的海底照得通明，她正朝水面游去。

sentences.en: But when the second electrical strike lit up the sky, it also showed what appeared to be a huge, ferocious horse deep in the water below.
sentences.zh: 可当第二道闪电照亮天空，也照出了下方深水里一匹巨大而凶猛的马。

sentences.en: The horse swam up and looked her in the eye.
sentences.zh: 那马游上来，与她对视。

sentences.en: Lightning struck again and the horse, the Water Spirit, was gone.
sentences.zh: 闪电再次劈下，那匹马——水灵——就不见了。

sentences.en: Elsa clawed her way to the surface.
sentences.zh: 艾莎奋力划水，浮上水面。

sentences.en: Waves tossed her as she looked down to see the Water Nokk galloping up from the depths, heading straight for her.
sentences.zh: 浪头把她抛起，她低头看见水马正从深处飞驰而上，直冲她而来。

sentences.en: She created an ice sheet to float on top of the water’s surface, and pulled herself onto it just in time for the Water Spirit to ram her vessel and send her careening into the air.
sentences.zh: 她造出一块浮在水面的冰板，刚把自己拉上去，水灵就撞碎了她的"船"，把她甩上了半空。

sentences.en: Struggling to breathe, Elsa turned to see the horse attacking again.
sentences.zh: 艾莎挣扎着喘气，转头看见那马又攻了过来。

sentences.en: Its hooves drove her underwater.
sentences.zh: 马蹄把她踩入水下。

sentences.en: She tried to break free as it pushed her deeper and deeper.
sentences.zh: 它把她越推越深，她拼命想挣脱。

sentences.en: She grabbed onto the Water Nokk’s hooves and froze the horse.
sentences.zh: 她抓住水马的蹄子，把马冻住。

sentences.en: It resisted, and then the Water Spirit shattered into billions of particles of ice.
sentences.zh: 它挣扎着，随后水灵碎成了亿万片冰晶。

sentences.en: Elsa swam straight up, hoping to get away before the Water Nokk re-formed itself.
sentences.zh: 艾莎径直向上游，想在水马重组之前逃开。

sentences.en: She reached the surface, but the horse was right there and threw her out of the water.
sentences.zh: 她浮上水面，可那马就在那儿，把她甩出了水面。

sentences.en: Lightning flashed.
sentences.zh: 闪电划过。

sentences.en: Elsa created a giant ice wave that collapsed onto the Water Nokk.
sentences.zh: 艾莎造出一道巨大的冰浪，朝水马塌压下去。

sentences.en: Lightning flashed again.
sentences.zh: 闪电再次划过。

sentences.en: Underwater, Elsa made an ice shield to block the horse.
sentences.zh: 水下，艾莎筑起冰盾挡住那马。

sentences.en: It burst through the shield as if nothing were there at all.
sentences.zh: 它如入无人之境，直接撞穿了冰盾。

sentences.en: Lightning flashed once more.
sentences.zh: 闪电又是一闪。

sentences.en: Above the water, the Water Nokk grabbed Elsa’s arm and dragged her through the waves.
sentences.zh: 水面上，水马咬住艾莎的手臂，拖着她穿过浪涛。

sentences.en: She fought to breathe.
sentences.zh: 她挣扎着呼吸。

sentences.en: Desperate, she used her magic to throw out an ice bridle.
sentences.zh: 情急之下，她用魔力甩出一副冰做的马勒。

sentences.en: It hooked onto the Water Spirit’s mouth and head.
sentences.zh: 它扣住了水灵的嘴和头。

sentences.en: She swung around and landed on the horse’s back.
sentences.zh: 她一荡身，落到了马背上。

sentences.en: The Water Nokk panicked and bucked.
sentences.zh: 水马惊慌地尥起蹶子。

sentences.en: But Elsa yanked on the reins and tried to gain control.
sentences.zh: 可艾莎猛拉缰绳，试图制服它。

sentences.en: The horse surfaced and turned toward the icy landmass that Elsa had seen in the distance.
sentences.zh: 马浮出水面，转向艾莎先前望见的那片冰封陆地。

sentences.en: It ran, fighting, trying to throw her off, refusing to give in to her commanding hold.
sentences.zh: 它一路狂奔、奋力挣扎，想把她甩下去，不肯向她的掌控屈服。

sentences.en: Elsa pulled the reins tighter and pressed her legs down harder until the horse responded.
sentences.zh: 艾莎把缰绳勒得更紧，双腿压得更沉，直到那马有了反应。

sentences.en: Finally, its stride evened out and she relaxed her grip.
sentences.zh: 终于，它的步子稳了下来，她也放松了手劲。

sentences.en: They moved together, Elsa and the Water Nokk.
sentences.zh: 艾莎和水马，融为一体般前行。

sentences.en: The icy landmass came into view ahead.
sentences.zh: 前方那片冰封陆地已清晰可见。

sentences.en: It appeared to be an island.
sentences.zh: 它看上去像座岛。

sentences.en: As Elsa got closer, she realized it was more than an island.
sentences.zh: 艾莎越靠越近，才发觉它不只是一座岛。

sentences.en: It was a giant glacier that sparkled with magic.
sentences.zh: 那是一块闪耀着魔法的巨大冰川。

sentences.en: She was overwhelmed with joy. “Of course,” she whispered. “Glaciers are rivers of ice.” The voice she had longed to reach called out to her, closer than ever. “Ahtohallan is frozen.” All she had to do was reach the secret river.
sentences.zh: 她喜不自胜。"原来如此，"她轻声说，"冰川就是冰的河流。"那她渴望触及的声音唤起了她，比以往更近。"阿托哈兰是冻结的。"她只需抵达那条秘密的河。

sentences.en: The voice continued to call to her, filling her ears.
sentences.zh: 那声音继续呼唤她，灌满她的耳畔。

sentences.en: It sounded almost joyful, as if it knew she was near. “I hear you,” Elsa said, “and I’m coming.” She snapped the reins and the Water Nokk quickened its pace.
sentences.zh: 它听起来几乎带着喜悦，仿佛知道她已临近。"我听见你了，"艾莎说，"我来了。"她一抖缰绳，水马加快了步伐。

sentences.en: Elsa couldn’t stop trembling with anticipation as she approached Ahtohallan with the Water Spirit.
sentences.zh: 艾莎与那水灵一同逼近阿托哈兰，激动得止不住颤抖。

sentences.en: Knowing the voice that had been calling to her was there gave her comfort.
sentences.zh: 想到那呼唤她的声音就在那里，她感到安心。

sentences.en: The Water Nokk turned when they reached the shore, allowing Elsa to leap onto the icy white beach.
sentences.zh: 他们抵达岸边时，水马一转身，让艾莎跳上了那片冰白的沙滩。

sentences.en: The ground shimmered when her feet landed.
sentences.zh: 她的双足落地，地面泛起微光。

sentences.en: It was a magical response.
sentences.zh: 那是魔法的回应。

sentences.en: She felt power emanating all around her.
sentences.zh: 她感到力量从四面八方涌来。

sentences.en: It felt like she was home.
sentences.zh: 那感觉，就像回到了家。

sentences.en: The horse shook its mane and turned back to the Dark Sea, slowly dissipating into the water.
sentences.zh: 那马甩了甩鬃毛，转身回到暗海，缓缓化入水中。

sentences.en: Elsa’s eyes moved from it and gazed up at the giant ice cave that stretched endlessly in front of her.
sentences.zh: 艾莎的目光从它身上移开，仰望起眼前延展开去、望不到尽头的巨大冰洞。

sentences.en: She moved toward an opening in the ice that loomed like a fortress.
sentences.zh: 她朝那个如堡垒般巍然耸立的冰之入口走去。

chapters.title: 第35章
chapters.en:
Elsa shivered as she looked at the glacier ahead of her. Ahtohallan, the secret river from Mother’s lullaby. It’s real, she thought. There was something about it that seemed so…familiar. She wondered if the familiarity came from the calling of the voice, or from the connection of magic. Because of how the colored lights twinkled and danced around the entrance to Ahtohallan, she knew it was full of magic.

Elsa boldly stepped into the opening of the ice cave, instantly feeling like she was finally where she was meant to be. She looked around with wonder at the smooth white walls, wondering what kinds of secrets were inside Ahtohallan. Elsa was nervous, but eager to find out.

The voice continued to call to Elsa in its haunting melody, and she answered back with confidence. She had always known that the voice wanted to help her, but she’d never imagined it would lead her to Ahtohallan. She moved around the cave’s entrance, following the call, willing to go where it led, ready for the voice to reveal itself. She was ready to learn.

The voice guided Elsa to a door in the ice. All she had to do was open it. The voice called to her again, stronger, and Elsa responded. Reaching out without hesitation, she pulled the door open and rushed forward, overcome with emotion and excitement for whatever lay ahead. She would do whatever it took to reach the voice. Every inch of her tingled to be with it as she dodged sharp, beautiful crystals that adorned the walls.

Elsa had never been more certain of anything in her life. She was there for a reason—and maybe it was the same reason she had been born. She was different from everyone else, and it was time to find out why. She didn’t tremble anymore. She just needed the voice to show her where she belonged.

The path through the cavern was not an easy one. The voice led Elsa over pillars of ice that tumbled as she leaped from one to the next. It called her to the bottom of a deep ravine, which she reached by creating a long staircase of ice that she ran down. Elsa met every challenge and triumphed.

Finally, she found herself in a giant room with a domed roof, where memories danced along the walls and ceiling. The memories were fuzzy, unclear. Though Elsa tried as hard as she could, she couldn’t make out what they were.

But the young queen could see the symbols for the spirits of nature, dancing and swirling around her. She reached for them, forming them into giant diamonds of ice. With her magic, she guided the diamonds to the floor, assembling them in the same snowflake pattern that was knitted into her mother’s scarf. But one was missing: the fifth element, the bridge between nature and people. Elsa stepped into the empty space and fulfilled her destiny.

The dome above her instantly illuminated with memories, but this time they were sharp and crystal clear. Perhaps it was a reward. The voice called to her again, and Elsa knew it too was one of the memories. When she called back, the memory clarified and came forward, facing her and singing the haunting melody. It all made sense. She stepped toward it and sang alongside the memory of her mother, who, as a young girl, had called out the day the forest fell.

Elsa understood why her mother had been there. Elsa had risked her life by moving through air, fire, water, and earth to be there. She was born for this and had proven her worth when she’d met up with the spirits of nature.

As Elsa sang along in harmony with the memory of Iduna, she began to transform into who she was always meant to be. Her dress spun around her body, and her hair fell loose and wildly untamed. A crown of vines and leaves adorned her head as the other elements swirled around her—air, fire, water, and earth. Elsa had transformed into the element Honeymaren had spoken of. Elsa was the fifth spirit, the bridge between nature and people. She was the Snow Queen.
chapters.zh:
艾莎望着前方的冰川，打了个寒颤。

阿托哈兰，妈妈摇篮曲里那条秘密的河。

它是真的，她想。

它身上有某种东西，让人觉得如此……熟悉。

她思忖，这份熟悉是来自那声音的呼唤，还是魔法的羁绊。

阿托哈兰入口处彩光闪烁舞动，由此可知那里满是魔法。

艾莎大胆地迈入冰洞的入口，立刻觉得自己终于来到了命中注定的所在。

她惊奇地环顾光滑的白色洞壁，猜想阿托哈兰里藏着怎样的秘密。

艾莎有些紧张，却迫不及待想一探究竟。

那声音仍以幽婉的旋律呼唤艾莎，而她自信地回应着。

她一直知道那声音想帮她，却从没想过它会把自己引到阿托哈兰。

她沿着洞口的边缘走动，循着呼唤而去，愿意去它指引的任何地方，准备迎接那声音现形。

她已准备好去了解真相。

那声音引艾莎来到一扇冰门之前。

她只需把它打开。

那声音再次呼唤她，更加有力，艾莎回应着。

她毫不迟疑地伸出手，拉开门冲了进去，对前方的一切满怀激动与期待。

为了抵达那声音，她愿付出一切。

她每一寸肌肤都因渴望与它会合而发颤，一边闪避着洞壁上那些锋利而美丽的冰晶。

艾莎一生中从未对什么事如此笃定。

她来此是有缘由的——而这缘由，或许正是她降生的缘由。

她与众人不同，是时候弄清原因了。

她不再颤抖。

她只需那声音告诉她，何处是她的归属。

穿过洞窟的路并不好走。

那声音引艾莎越过一根根冰柱，她从一个跳向另一个，冰柱纷纷崩落。

它把她唤到一道深谷的谷底，她造出一道长长的冰梯跑了下去。

艾莎迎战每一个挑战，并一一取胜。

终于，她来到一间穹顶的巨大厅堂，记忆在四壁与天花板上舞动。

那些记忆模糊不清。

艾莎用尽全力，也辨不清它们是什么。

可年轻的女王能看见自然之灵的符文，在她四周舞动盘旋。

她伸手将它们聚拢，凝成巨大的冰之菱形。

她用魔力把菱形引到地面，按妈妈围巾上织着的同一种雪花图案拼合起来。

可少了一块：第五元素，自然与人之间的桥梁。

艾莎踏入那片空位，完成了她的使命。

她头顶的穹顶瞬间被记忆点亮，而这一次，它们清晰锐利，如水晶般分明。

这或许是一种奖赏。

那声音再次呼唤她，艾莎明白，它也是一段记忆。

当她回应，那段记忆变得清晰，向前浮现，面对着她，唱起那支幽婉的旋律。

一切都豁然明朗。

她朝它走去，和母亲年轻时的记忆一同唱起——那天森林陷落，正是少女时的母亲发出了呼唤。

艾莎明白了母亲为何会在那里。

艾莎穿越风、火、水、土，冒死来到了这里。

她为这一切而生，并在与自然的精灵相遇时证明了自己的价值。

当艾莎与伊杜娜的记忆和声而唱，她开始蜕变成自己命中注定的模样。

她的裙裾绕身旋转，头发披散开来，肆意而不羁。

藤蔓与枝叶编成的冠冕戴在她头上，其余的元素——风、火、水、土——在她身周盘旋。

艾莎已化作霍妮玛伦所说的那个元素。

艾莎就是第五个精灵，是自然与人之间的桥梁。

她就是冰雪女王。

sentences.zh: 它是真的，她想。

sentences.en: There was something about it that seemed so…familiar.
sentences.zh: 它身上有某种东西，让人觉得如此……熟悉。

sentences.en: She wondered if the familiarity came from the calling of the voice, or from the connection of magic.
sentences.zh: 她思忖，这份熟悉是来自那声音的呼唤，还是魔法的羁绊。

sentences.en: Because of how the colored lights twinkled and danced around the entrance to Ahtohallan, she knew it was full of magic.
sentences.zh: 阿托哈兰入口处彩光闪烁舞动，由此可知那里满是魔法。

sentences.en: Elsa boldly stepped into the opening of the ice cave, instantly feeling like she was finally where she was meant to be.
sentences.zh: 艾莎大胆地迈入冰洞的入口，立刻觉得自己终于来到了命中注定的所在。

sentences.en: She looked around with wonder at the smooth white walls, wondering what kinds of secrets were inside Ahtohallan.
sentences.zh: 她惊奇地环顾光滑的白色洞壁，猜想阿托哈兰里藏着怎样的秘密。

sentences.en: Elsa was nervous, but eager to find out.
sentences.zh: 艾莎有些紧张，却迫不及待想一探究竟。

sentences.en: The voice continued to call to Elsa in its haunting melody, and she answered back with confidence.
sentences.zh: 那声音仍以幽婉的旋律呼唤艾莎，而她自信地回应着。

sentences.en: She had always known that the voice wanted to help her, but she’d never imagined it would lead her to Ahtohallan.
sentences.zh: 她一直知道那声音想帮她，却从没想过它会把自己引到阿托哈兰。

sentences.en: She moved around the cave’s entrance, following the call, willing to go where it led, ready for the voice to reveal itself.
sentences.zh: 她沿着洞口的边缘走动，循着呼唤而去，愿意去它指引的任何地方，准备迎接那声音现形。

sentences.en: She was ready to learn.
sentences.zh: 她已准备好去了解真相。

sentences.en: The voice guided Elsa to a door in the ice.
sentences.zh: 那声音引艾莎来到一扇冰门之前。

sentences.en: All she had to do was open it.
sentences.zh: 她只需把它打开。

sentences.en: The voice called to her again, stronger, and Elsa responded.
sentences.zh: 那声音再次呼唤她，更加有力，艾莎回应着。

sentences.en: Reaching out without hesitation, she pulled the door open and rushed forward, overcome with emotion and excitement for whatever lay ahead.
sentences.zh: 她毫不迟疑地伸出手，拉开门冲了进去，对前方的一切满怀激动与期待。

sentences.en: She would do whatever it took to reach the voice.
sentences.zh: 为了抵达那声音，她愿付出一切。

sentences.en: Every inch of her tingled to be with it as she dodged sharp, beautiful crystals that adorned the walls.
sentences.zh: 她每一寸肌肤都因渴望与它会合而发颤，一边闪避着洞壁上那些锋利而美丽的冰晶。

sentences.en: Elsa had never been more certain of anything in her life.
sentences.zh: 艾莎一生中从未对什么事如此笃定。

sentences.en: She was there for a reason—and maybe it was the same reason she had been born.
sentences.zh: 她来此是有缘由的——而这缘由，或许正是她降生的缘由。

sentences.en: She was different from everyone else, and it was time to find out why.
sentences.zh: 她与众人不同，是时候弄清原因了。

sentences.en: She didn’t tremble anymore.
sentences.zh: 她不再颤抖。

sentences.en: She just needed the voice to show her where she belonged.
sentences.zh: 她只需那声音告诉她，何处是她的归属。

sentences.en: The path through the cavern was not an easy one.
sentences.zh: 穿过洞窟的路并不好走。

sentences.en: The voice led Elsa over pillars of ice that tumbled as she leaped from one to the next.
sentences.zh: 那声音引艾莎越过一根根冰柱，她从一个跳向另一个，冰柱纷纷崩落。

sentences.en: It called her to the bottom of a deep ravine, which she reached by creating a long staircase of ice that she ran down.
sentences.zh: 它把她唤到一道深谷的谷底，她造出一道长长的冰梯跑了下去。

sentences.en: Elsa met every challenge and triumphed.
sentences.zh: 艾莎迎战每一个挑战，并一一取胜。

sentences.en: Finally, she found herself in a giant room with a domed roof, where memories danced along the walls and ceiling.
sentences.zh: 终于，她来到一间穹顶的巨大厅堂，记忆在四壁与天花板上舞动。

sentences.en: The memories were fuzzy, unclear.
sentences.zh: 那些记忆模糊不清。

sentences.en: Though Elsa tried as hard as she could, she couldn’t make out what they were.
sentences.zh: 艾莎用尽全力，也辨不清它们是什么。

sentences.en: But the young queen could see the symbols for the spirits of nature, dancing and swirling around her.
sentences.zh: 可年轻的女王能看见自然之灵的符文，在她四周舞动盘旋。

sentences.en: She reached for them, forming them into giant diamonds of ice.
sentences.zh: 她伸手将它们聚拢，凝成巨大的冰之菱形。

sentences.en: With her magic, she guided the diamonds to the floor, assembling them in the same snowflake pattern that was knitted into her mother’s scarf.
sentences.zh: 她用魔力把菱形引到地面，按妈妈围巾上织着的同一种雪花图案拼合起来。

sentences.en: But one was missing: the fifth element, the bridge between nature and people.
sentences.zh: 可少了一块：第五元素，自然与人之间的桥梁。

sentences.en: Elsa stepped into the empty space and fulfilled her destiny.
sentences.zh: 艾莎踏入那片空位，完成了她的使命。

sentences.en: The dome above her instantly illuminated with memories, but this time they were sharp and crystal clear.
sentences.zh: 她头顶的穹顶瞬间被记忆点亮，而这一次，它们清晰锐利，如水晶般分明。

sentences.en: Perhaps it was a reward.
sentences.zh: 这或许是一种奖赏。

sentences.en: The voice called to her again, and Elsa knew it too was one of the memories.
sentences.zh: 那声音再次呼唤她，艾莎明白，它也是一段记忆。

sentences.en: When she called back, the memory clarified and came forward, facing her and singing the haunting melody.
sentences.zh: 当她回应，那段记忆变得清晰，向前浮现，面对着她，唱起那支幽婉的旋律。

sentences.en: It all made sense.
sentences.zh: 一切都豁然明朗。

sentences.en: She stepped toward it and sang alongside the memory of her mother, who, as a young girl, had called out the day the forest fell.
sentences.zh: 她朝它走去，和母亲年轻时的记忆一同唱起——那天森林陷落，正是少女时的母亲发出了呼唤。

sentences.en: Elsa understood why her mother had been there.
sentences.zh: 艾莎明白了母亲为何会在那里。

sentences.en: Elsa had risked her life by moving through air, fire, water, and earth to be there.
sentences.zh: 艾莎穿越风、火、水、土，冒死来到了这里。

sentences.en: She was born for this and had proven her worth when she’d met up with the spirits of nature.
sentences.zh: 她为这一切而生，并在与自然的精灵相遇时证明了自己的价值。

sentences.en: As Elsa sang along in harmony with the memory of Iduna, she began to transform into who she was always meant to be.
sentences.zh: 当艾莎与伊杜娜的记忆和声而唱，她开始蜕变成自己命中注定的模样。

sentences.en: Her dress spun around her body, and her hair fell loose and wildly untamed.
sentences.zh: 她的裙裾绕身旋转，头发披散开来，肆意而不羁。

sentences.en: A crown of vines and leaves adorned her head as the other elements swirled around her—air, fire, water, and earth.
sentences.zh: 藤蔓与枝叶编成的冠冕戴在她头上，其余的元素——风、火、水、土——在她身周盘旋。

sentences.en: Elsa had transformed into the element Honeymaren had spoken of.
sentences.zh: 艾莎已化作霍妮玛伦所说的那个元素。

sentences.en: Elsa was the fifth spirit, the bridge between nature and people.
sentences.zh: 艾莎就是第五个精灵，是自然与人之间的桥梁。

sentences.en: She was the Snow Queen.
sentences.zh: 她就是冰雪女王。

chapters.title: 第36章
chapters.en:
With her hands, Elsa manipulated the giant symbols suspended in the air and used them to build a new snowflake, with the elements as the branches and herself as the center. This was the version of herself that Elsa had been waiting for her entire life, and it was what the other elements had been waiting for as well.

As Elsa looked around, the memories played out in front of her. It was as if her transformation was the key that had unlocked them.

Elsa raised her arms and used her magic to draw the memories closer. They landed all around her, the icy reflections of the past. Unlike the sculptures she had made in the forest, these moved and interacted with her. The voices were as clear as if the people in the memories were there in person. At first it seemed she didn’t know them, but as she looked closer, she gasped in surprise.

The first memory was of a young girl twirling high in the wind and a boy looking after her. She recognized them as her parents, on the day the Northuldra and Arendellians had fought in the forest. Her mother was riding on the currents of Gale.

Taking another step, Elsa recognized the memory that had solidified into a statue in the forest—it was her mother holding her father as she saved him. Elsa gasped when she realized why the image was suspended in the air; the Wind Spirit had lifted them out of the Enchanted Forest while others were locked in. It was Gale. Gale had always been there to protect Elsa’s family, even before she was born.

Elsa walked faster as new memories appeared with every step she took. She saw her mother in an orphanage in the woods outside Arendelle. “No one knew who you were,” she heard. “You didn’t have any family with you.”

She passed the next memories in a hurry—there were so many to see. Anna riding by as a child, standing on the seat of her bike. The bishop announcing the day Elsa took the throne: “Presenting Queen Elsa of Arendelle.” Elsa’s mother studying old documents in the library of the castle: “What have you found?” asked her father. “I think we’ve been looking on the wrong side of the sea,” her mother replied.

Elsa moved through crowds while continuing to watch her family. She spotted Hans talking to Anna. “I’m great, actually,” she said to him. He bowed and introduced himself. “Prince Hans of the Southern Isles.” Elsa threw a blast of power, shattering that memory, before walking on.

She watched a younger version of herself and her sister, fascinated. “Conceal, don’t feel; conceal, don’t feel….” Elsa kept moving.

Anna’s voice rang out: “I love you, Olaf!”

Elsa smiled when she saw her parents’ wedding. “To have and to hold, from this day forward—” her father promised. Then there were her parents when they were younger. She laughed as she watched her mother drop from a tree and sit next to her father. “Iduna,” said Agnarr. “What are you reading, Your Majesty?” a teenage version of her mother asked. “Some new Danish author,” he said.

Elsa blasted the memory with her magic and continued walking. This time she found her parents as adults, and they were embracing. “I need to tell you about my past, and where I am from,” Iduna said sadly. “I’m here,” said Agnarr, pulling her into his arms.

Elsa felt a breeze above her and looked up. The wind carried her father and mother, young teenagers in this memory, and placed them on an Arendellian cart. She watched her mother place a blanket over her father, then drape an Arendellian cloak around herself as soldiers arrived. “Get the prince out of here,” a soldier said to the wagon driver.

Elsa sensed someone behind her.

“Lieutenant Mattias,” a voice said. She turned to see a royal Arendellian walk by with another soldier at his side. A much younger Mattias turned at the sound of his king’s voice.

“Grandfather—” Elsa whispered, seeing King Runeard for the first time.

“We bring Arendelle’s full guard,” the king ordered.

“But they have given us no reason not to trust them,” argued Mattias.

Elsa’s grandfather shook his head. “The Northuldra follow magic, which means we can never trust them.”

His words hurt and deeply troubled Elsa. ­“Grandfather?” she said softly.

“Magic makes people feel too powerful, too entitled. It makes them think they can defy the will of a king,” said King Runeard firmly.

Elsa shook her head. “That is not what magic does,” she said. “That’s just your fear. Fear is what can’t be trusted.”

Her grandfather and the soldier walked right through the glacier wall in front of them. Mattias stayed where he stood and just watched them. Anna desperately wanted to follow to see what happened next. She threw out her hands and used her power to cut a large hole in the ice wall.

In the distance, the faint sounds of her mother’s lullaby filled the air, reminding her that if she went too far into Ahtohallan, she would never be able to return. But Elsa needed to know what had happened in the forest that day. She needed the truth.

She stepped through the hole in the wall that she had created and into a dark, narrow passageway that slowly sloped downward. She walked along it with unsure steps. As her hands rubbed against the wall, memories came alive on it.

“The dam will weaken their lands,” her grandfather said to the soldier with him. “So they’ll have to turn to me.”

On the wall ahead, she saw the mighty dam. Many Northuldra, gathered from far and wide, disappeared down a steep drop at the end of the narrow path. As Elsa approached, echoes from the chamber of memories became more and more distant.

“They will come in celebration, and then we will know their size and strength,” her grandfather said.

Elsa stopped at the edge of the drop and looked down, wondering if she should go farther. She saw her grandfather addressing the large group of Northuldra in front of him.

“As you have welcomed us, we welcome you. Our neighbors. Our friends,” King Runeard said.

The Northuldra leader stopped him. “King Runeard, the dam isn’t strengthening our waters. It’s hurting the forest. It’s cutting off the north!”

King Runeard nodded as if he were listening. As if he were concerned. “Let’s not discuss this here. Let’s meet on the fjord. Have tea. Find a solution.”

“Who will stop you from going too far?” the memory of Anna’s voice reminded Elsa.

Elsa looked back up the path to the magical light of the chamber of memories, debating whether she should return or move forward. She heard voices coming from it.

“No one really knows what happened that day,” someone said. It was when she’d first met the Northuldra. Then her father: “For Arendelle’s sake.” More voices. “You’re trapped here, too!” Yelana shouted. “We’ve never even seen the real sky,” Ryder complained. “A wrong demands resolution,” said Pabbie. “Without it…I see no future.”

Elsa decided that moving forward was the only choice there ever was. She let her body fall through the darkness until she landed in a forest made of ice. It felt empty and uninviting. It was so cold that Elsa shivered for the first time in her life. The cold had never bothered her before.

She spotted her grandfather walking determinedly through the forest. She started to follow him and noticed Northuldra festivities in a nearby clearing. She moved quickly, searching for her purpose there, the ground freezing around her feet with each step.

Up ahead, she saw the Northuldra leader sitting on the edge of a rock. Elsa was caught by surprise when a snowy image of her grandfather passed through her, heading for the Northuldra leader with a drawn sword in hand. Elsa was horrified by what he was about to do. She reached out to stop him.

“No!” she shouted. She was devastated to see what had really happened in the past, and she wanted to change it more than anything. But she couldn’t.

Ice crept up her body, slowly covering it. She panicked and focused on breathing. She tried to use her powers to force the ice off her, but it didn’t work.

The ice crept up her neck and toward her face. At that point, she knew she had gone too far, just like her mother’s lullaby had warned, and there was no way to return. She gathered all her magic to release in a last-minute signal to Anna. Only one stream of magic escaped, slicing through the air.

“Anna…,” she called out desperately. A second later, she was completely encased in ice.
chapters.zh:
艾莎用双手拨弄悬浮在空中的巨大符文，以元素为枝、以自己为中心，拼出一朵新的雪花。

这就是艾莎等待了一生的自己，也是其他元素所等待的。

艾莎环顾四周，记忆在她面前一幕幕上演。

仿佛她的蜕变，就是开启它们的钥匙。

艾莎抬起双臂，用魔力把记忆拉近。

它们落在她四周，是往昔的冰之倒影。

与她在森林里造的冰雕不同，这些会动，还会与她互动。

那些声音清晰得仿佛记忆中的人就亲临现场。

起初她似乎不认得他们，可定睛一看，她惊讶地倒吸一口凉气。

第一段记忆里，一个小女孩在风中高高旋转，一个男孩在一旁照看她。

她认出那是她的父母，在那天北地人和阿伦黛尔人在森林里交战的日子。

她的母亲正乘着盖尔的气流飞翔。

再迈一步，艾莎认出了那段在森林里凝成雕像的记忆——是母亲救起父亲时抱住他的情景。

艾莎恍然大悟这影像为何悬在空中，倒吸一口凉气：当时风灵把他们托出了魔法森林，而其他人却被困其中。

是盖尔。

盖尔一直守护着艾莎的家人，早在她出生之前便是如此。

艾莎走得更快了，每走一步都有新的记忆浮现。

她看见母亲在阿伦黛尔城外林中的一所孤儿院里。"没人知道你是谁，"她听见，"你身边一个亲人也没有。"她匆匆走过接下来的几段记忆——要看的实在太多。

童年时的安娜骑车经过，站在车座上。

主教在艾莎登基那天宣告："阿伦黛尔的艾莎女王陛下驾到。"艾莎的母亲在城堡图书馆里研读旧文献：父亲问"你发现了什么？"母亲答"我想我们一直在海的错误一侧寻找"。

艾莎穿过人群，目光仍追随着她的家人。

她瞥见汉斯正和安娜说话。"其实我好极了。"安娜对他说。

他鞠躬自报家门："南境群岛的汉斯王子。"艾莎甩出一道魔力，击碎了那段记忆，继续前行。

她入迷地看着年幼的自己和妹妹。"掩饰，别去感受；掩饰，别去感受……"艾莎继续走着。

安娜的声音响起："我爱你，奥拉夫！"艾莎看到父母的婚礼，微笑了。父亲许诺："无论疾病健康，从今往后——"

接着是更年轻的父母。

她看着母亲从树上跳下、坐在父亲身旁，笑了起来。"伊杜娜，"安格瑞说。"你在读什么，陛下？"少年时的母亲问。"某位丹麦新作家写的。"他说。

艾莎用魔力击碎这段记忆，继续前行。

这一次，她看见成年的父母相拥。"我得告诉你我的过去，还有我来自哪里。"伊杜娜忧伤地说。"我在这儿。"安格瑞说着，把她拥入怀中。

艾莎感到头顶一阵微风，抬眼望去。

风托起记忆中还是少男少女的父母，把他们放到一辆阿伦黛尔的马车上。

她看着母亲给父亲盖上毯子，又在自己肩头披上阿伦黛尔的斗篷，这时士兵来了。"把王子带离这里。"一名士兵对车夫说。

艾莎察觉身后有人。"马蒂亚斯中尉。"一个声音说。

她转身，看见一名阿伦黛尔王室成员走过，身旁跟着另一名士兵。

年轻得多的马蒂亚斯听到国王的声音转过头。"祖父——"艾莎低声道，第一次见到鲁内尔德国王。"我们带来了阿伦黛尔的全体卫队。"国王下令。"可他们并未给我们不信任他们的理由。"马蒂亚斯争辩道。

艾莎的祖父摇了摇头。"北地人信奉魔法，这意味着我们永远不能信任他们。"这话刺痛了艾莎，也让她深感不安。"祖父？"她轻声说，"魔法让人觉得太过强大，太过特权。

它让他们以为能违抗国王的意志。"鲁内尔德国王斩钉截铁地说。

艾莎摇了摇头。"魔法不是这样的，"她说，"那只是你的恐惧。

恐惧，才是不可信任的东西。"祖父和那名士兵径直穿过了眼前的冰壁。

马蒂亚斯站在原地，只是望着他们。

安娜急切地想跟上去，看看接下来发生了什么。

她伸出双手，用魔力在冰壁上切开一个大洞。

远处，母亲摇篮曲的微弱声响充盈在空气中，提醒她：若深入阿托哈兰太远，就再也回不去了。

可艾莎必须弄清那天森林里发生了什么。

她需要真相。

她穿过自己凿出的墙洞，进入一条幽暗狭窄、缓缓向下倾斜的通道。

她脚步迟疑地沿着它走。

她的手摩挲着墙壁，墙上的记忆活了过来。"水坝会削弱他们的土地，"祖父对身边的士兵说，"那样他们就只好依附于我。"前方的墙上，她看见了那座宏大的水坝。

许多从四面八方聚集而来的北地人，在窄道尽头消失在一处陡降的断崖下。

艾莎走近时，记忆之厅的回音越来越远。"他们会带着庆典而来，那时我们便知他们人数与实力。"祖父说。

艾莎在断崖边缘停下，朝下望去，思量是否该再往前。

她看见祖父对面前一大群北地人讲话。"正如你们欢迎了我们，我们也欢迎你们。

我们的邻居。

我们的朋友。"鲁内尔德国王说。

北地人的首领打断了他。"鲁内尔德国王，水坝并没有增强我们的水域。

它在伤害森林。

它在切断北方！"鲁内尔德国王点点头，仿佛在倾听。

仿佛很关切。"我们别在这儿谈这个。

我们去峡湾上碰头。

喝杯茶。

找个解决办法。""谁会拦住你、不让你走太远？"安娜声音的记忆提醒着艾莎。

艾莎回头望向通道上方、记忆之厅的魔法之光，权衡着该返回还是继续前行。

她听见里面有说话声。"没人真正知道那天发生了什么。"有人说。

那是她初次遇见北地人的时候。

接着是父亲："为了阿伦黛尔。"更多声音。"你也被困在这里了！"叶拉娜喊。"我们连真正的天空都没见过。"莱德抱怨。"冤屈须得昭雪。"皮比说，"否则……我看不见未来。"艾莎认定，向前走是唯一的选择。

她任由身体坠入黑暗，落在一片冰做的森林里。

那里空荡荡的，毫无生气。

冷得艾莎生平第一次打了寒颤。

从前，寒冷从未困扰过她。

她望见祖父坚决地穿过森林。

她开始跟上去，注意到附近空地上有北地人的庆典。

她快步移动，寻找自己此行的目的，每走一步，脚下的地面便冻结起来。

前方，她看见北地人首领坐在岩石边缘。

一个祖父的雪影从艾莎身上穿过、手持出鞘的剑朝北地人首领走去，让她惊愕不已。

他即将做的事，令艾莎毛骨悚然。

她伸手去拦他。"不！"她喊。

目睹过去真正发生的事，她心如刀绞，比什么都更想改变它。

可她无能为力。

冰爬上她的身体，缓缓将她覆盖。

她慌了，努力专注呼吸。

她试图用魔力逼退身上的冰，却无济于事。

冰爬上她的脖颈，逼近脸庞。

那一刻她明白，自己走得太远了，正如母亲摇篮曲所警示，已无路可返。

她汇聚全部魔力，要在最后一刻向安娜发出信号。

只逃出一道魔流，破空而去。"安娜……"她绝望地呼唤。

一秒之后，她被彻底封进了冰里。

sentences.en: With her hands, Elsa manipulated the giant symbols suspended in the air and used them to build a new snowflake, with the elements as the branches and herself as the center.
sentences.zh: 艾莎用双手拨弄悬浮在空中的巨大符文，以元素为枝、以自己为中心，拼出一朵新的雪花。

sentences.en: This was the version of herself that Elsa had been waiting for her entire life, and it was what the other elements had been waiting for as well.
sentences.zh: 这就是艾莎等待了一生的自己，也是其他元素所等待的。

sentences.en: As Elsa looked around, the memories played out in front of her.
sentences.zh: 艾莎环顾四周，记忆在她面前一幕幕上演。

sentences.en: It was as if her transformation was the key that had unlocked them.
sentences.zh: 仿佛她的蜕变，就是开启它们的钥匙。

sentences.en: Elsa raised her arms and used her magic to draw the memories closer.
sentences.zh: 艾莎抬起双臂，用魔力把记忆拉近。

sentences.en: They landed all around her, the icy reflections of the past.
sentences.zh: 它们落在她四周，是往昔的冰之倒影。

sentences.en: Unlike the sculptures she had made in the forest, these moved and interacted with her.
sentences.zh: 与她在森林里造的冰雕不同，这些会动，还会与她互动。

sentences.en: The voices were as clear as if the people in the memories were there in person.
sentences.zh: 那些声音清晰得仿佛记忆中的人就亲临现场。

sentences.en: At first it seemed she didn’t know them, but as she looked closer, she gasped in surprise.
sentences.zh: 起初她似乎不认得他们，可定睛一看，她惊讶地倒吸一口凉气。

sentences.en: The first memory was of a young girl twirling high in the wind and a boy looking after her.
sentences.zh: 第一段记忆里，一个小女孩在风中高高旋转，一个男孩在一旁照看她。

sentences.en: She recognized them as her parents, on the day the Northuldra and Arendellians had fought in the forest.
sentences.zh: 她认出那是她的父母，在那天北地人和阿伦黛尔人在森林里交战的日子。

sentences.en: Her mother was riding on the currents of Gale.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲正乘着盖尔的气流飞翔。

sentences.en: Taking another step, Elsa recognized the memory that had solidified into a statue in the forest—it was her mother holding her father as she saved him.
sentences.zh: 再迈一步，艾莎认出了那段在森林里凝成雕像的记忆——是母亲救起父亲时抱住他的情景。

sentences.en: Elsa gasped when she realized why the image was suspended in the air; the Wind Spirit had lifted them out of the Enchanted Forest while others were locked in.
sentences.zh: 艾莎恍然大悟这影像为何悬在空中，倒吸一口凉气：当时风灵把他们托出了魔法森林，而其他人却被困其中。

sentences.en: It was Gale.
sentences.zh: 是盖尔。

sentences.en: Gale had always been there to protect Elsa’s family, even before she was born.
sentences.zh: 盖尔一直守护着艾莎的家人，早在她出生之前便是如此。

sentences.en: Elsa walked faster as new memories appeared with every step she took.
sentences.zh: 艾莎走得更快了，每走一步都有新的记忆浮现。

sentences.en: She saw her mother in an orphanage in the woods outside Arendelle. “No one knew who you were,” she heard. “You didn’t have any family with you.” She passed the next memories in a hurry—there were so many to see.
sentences.zh: 她看见母亲在阿伦黛尔城外林中的一所孤儿院里。"没人知道你是谁，"她听见，"你身边一个亲人也没有。"她匆匆走过接下来的几段记忆——要看的实在太多。

sentences.en: Anna riding by as a child, standing on the seat of her bike.
sentences.zh: 童年时的安娜骑车经过，站在车座上。

sentences.en: The bishop announcing the day Elsa took the throne: “Presenting Queen Elsa of Arendelle.” Elsa’s mother studying old documents in the library of the castle: “What have you found?” asked her father. “I think we’ve been looking on the wrong side of the sea,” her mother replied.
sentences.zh: 主教在艾莎登基那天宣告："阿伦黛尔的艾莎女王陛下驾到。"艾莎的母亲在城堡图书馆里研读旧文献：父亲问"你发现了什么？"母亲答"我想我们一直在海的错误一侧寻找"。

sentences.en: Elsa moved through crowds while continuing to watch her family.
sentences.zh: 艾莎穿过人群，目光仍追随着她的家人。

sentences.en: She spotted Hans talking to Anna. “I’m great, actually,” she said to him.
sentences.zh: 她瞥见汉斯正和安娜说话。"其实我好极了。"安娜对他说。

sentences.en: He bowed and introduced himself. “Prince Hans of the Southern Isles.” Elsa threw a blast of power, shattering that memory, before walking on.
sentences.zh: 他鞠躬自报家门："南境群岛的汉斯。"艾莎甩出一道魔力，击碎了那段记忆，继续前行。

sentences.en: She watched a younger version of herself and her sister, fascinated. “Conceal, don’t feel; conceal, don’t feel….” Elsa kept moving.
sentences.zh: 她入迷地看着年幼的自己和妹妹。"掩饰，别去感受；掩饰，别去感受……"艾莎继续走着。

sentences.en: Anna’s voice rang out: “I love you, Olaf!” Elsa smiled when she saw her parents’ wedding. “To have and to hold, from this day forward—” her father promised.
sentences.zh: 安娜的声音响起："我爱你，奥拉夫！"艾莎看到父母的婚礼，微笑了。父亲许诺："无论疾病健康，从今往后——"

sentences.en: Then there were her parents when they were younger.
sentences.zh: 接着是更年轻的父母。

sentences.en: She laughed as she watched her mother drop from a tree and sit next to her father. “Iduna,” said Agnarr. “What are you reading, Your Majesty?” a teenage version of her mother asked. “Some new Danish author,” he said.
sentences.zh: 她看着母亲从树上跳下、坐在父亲身旁，笑了起来。"伊杜娜，"安格瑞说。"你在读什么，陛下？"少年时的母亲问。"某位丹麦新作家写的。"他说。

sentences.en: Elsa blasted the memory with her magic and continued walking.
sentences.zh: 艾莎用魔力击碎这段记忆，继续前行。

sentences.en: This time she found her parents as adults, and they were embracing. “I need to tell you about my past, and where I am from,” Iduna said sadly. “I’m here,” said Agnarr, pulling her into his arms.
sentences.zh: 这一次，她看见成年的父母相拥。"我得告诉你我的过去，还有我来自哪里。"伊杜娜忧伤地说。"我在这儿。"安格瑞说着，把她拥入怀中。

sentences.en: Elsa felt a breeze above her and looked up.
sentences.zh: 艾莎感到头顶一阵微风，抬眼望去。

sentences.en: The wind carried her father and mother, young teenagers in this memory, and placed them on an Arendellian cart.
sentences.zh: 风托起记忆中还是少男少女的父母，把他们放到一辆阿伦黛尔的马车上。

sentences.en: She watched her mother place a blanket over her father, then drape an Arendellian cloak around herself as soldiers arrived. “Get the prince out of here,” a soldier said to the wagon driver.
sentences.zh: 她看着母亲给父亲盖上毯子，又在自己肩头披上阿伦黛尔的斗篷，这时士兵来了。"把王子带离这里。"一名士兵对车夫说。

sentences.en: Elsa sensed someone behind her. “Lieutenant Mattias,” a voice said.
sentences.zh: 艾莎察觉身后有人。"马蒂亚斯中尉。"一个声音说。

sentences.en: She turned to see a royal Arendellian walk by with another soldier at his side.
sentences.zh: 她转身，看见一名阿伦黛尔王室成员走过，身旁跟着另一名士兵。

sentences.en: A much younger Mattias turned at the sound of his king’s voice. “Grandfather—” Elsa whispered, seeing King Runeard for the first time. “We bring Arendelle’s full guard,” the king ordered. “But they have given us no reason not to trust them,” argued Mattias.
sentences.zh: 年轻得多的马蒂亚斯听到国王的声音转过头。"祖父——"艾莎低声道，第一次见到鲁内尔德国王。"我们带来了阿伦黛尔的全体卫队。"国王下令。"可他们并未给我们不信任他们的理由。"马蒂亚斯争辩道。

sentences.en: Elsa’s grandfather shook his head. “The Northuldra follow magic, which means we can never trust them.” His words hurt and deeply troubled Elsa. ­“Grandfather?” she said softly. “Magic makes people feel too powerful, too entitled.
sentences.zh: 艾莎的祖父摇了摇头。"北地人信奉魔法，这意味着我们永远不能信任他们。"这话刺痛了艾莎，也让她深感不安。"祖父？"她轻声说，"魔法让人觉得太过强大，太过特权。

sentences.en: It makes them think they can defy the will of a king,” said King Runeard firmly.
sentences.zh: 它让他们以为能违抗国王的意志。"鲁内尔德国王斩钉截铁地说。

sentences.en: Elsa shook her head. “That is not what magic does,” she said. “That’s just your fear.
sentences.zh: 艾莎摇了摇头。"魔法不是这样的，"她说，"那只是你的恐惧。

sentences.en: Fear is what can’t be trusted.” Her grandfather and the soldier walked right through the glacier wall in front of them.
sentences.zh: 恐惧，才是不可信任的东西。"祖父和那名士兵径直穿过了眼前的冰壁。

sentences.en: Mattias stayed where he stood and just watched them.
sentences.zh: 马蒂亚斯站在原地，只是望着他们。

sentences.en: Anna desperately wanted to follow to see what happened next.
sentences.zh: 安娜急切地想跟上去，看看接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: She threw out her hands and used her power to cut a large hole in the ice wall.
sentences.zh: 她伸出双手，用魔力在冰壁上切开一个大洞。

sentences.en: In the distance, the faint sounds of her mother’s lullaby filled the air, reminding her that if she went too far into Ahtohallan, she would never be able to return.
sentences.zh: 远处，母亲摇篮曲的微弱声响充盈在空气中，提醒她：若深入阿托哈兰太远，就再也回不去了。

sentences.en: But Elsa needed to know what had happened in the forest that day.
sentences.zh: 可艾莎必须弄清那天森林里发生了什么。

sentences.en: She needed the truth.
sentences.zh: 她需要真相。

sentences.en: She stepped through the hole in the wall that she had created and into a dark, narrow passageway that slowly sloped downward.
sentences.zh: 她穿过自己凿出的墙洞，进入一条幽暗狭窄、缓缓向下倾斜的通道。

sentences.en: She walked along it with unsure steps.
sentences.zh: 她脚步迟疑地沿着它走。

sentences.en: As her hands rubbed against the wall, memories came alive on it. “The dam will weaken their lands,” her grandfather said to the soldier with him. “So they’ll have to turn to me.” On the wall ahead, she saw the mighty dam.
sentences.zh: 她的手摩挲着墙壁，墙上的记忆活了过来。"水坝会削弱他们的土地，"祖父对身边的士兵说，"那样他们就只好依附于我。"前方的墙上，她看见了那座宏大的水坝。

sentences.en: Many Northuldra, gathered from far and wide, disappeared down a steep drop at the end of the narrow path.
sentences.zh: 许多从四面八方聚集而来的北地人，在窄道尽头消失在一处陡降的断崖下。

sentences.en: As Elsa approached, echoes from the chamber of memories became more and more distant. “They will come in celebration, and then we will know their size and strength,” her grandfather said.
sentences.zh: 艾莎走近时，记忆之厅的回音越来越远。"他们会带着庆典而来，那时我们便知他们人数与实力。"祖父说。

sentences.en: Elsa stopped at the edge of the drop and looked down, wondering if she should go farther.
sentences.zh: 艾莎在断崖边缘停下，朝下望去，思量是否该再往前。

sentences.en: She saw her grandfather addressing the large group of Northuldra in front of him. “As you have welcomed us, we welcome you.
sentences.zh: 她看见祖父对面前一大群北地人讲话。"正如你们欢迎了我们，我们也欢迎你们。

sentences.en: Our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我们的邻居。

sentences.en: Our friends,” King Runeard said.
sentences.zh: 我们的朋友。"鲁内尔德国王说。

sentences.en: The Northuldra leader stopped him. “King Runeard, the dam isn’t strengthening our waters.
sentences.zh: 北地人的首领打断了他。"鲁内尔德国王，水坝并没有增强我们的水域。

sentences.en: It’s hurting the forest.
sentences.zh: 它在伤害森林。

sentences.en: It’s cutting off the north!” King Runeard nodded as if he were listening.
sentences.zh: 它在切断北方！"鲁内尔德国王点点头，仿佛在倾听。

sentences.en: As if he were concerned. “ Let’s not discuss this here.
sentences.zh: 仿佛很关切。"我们别在这儿谈这个。

sentences.en: Let’s meet on the fjord.
sentences.zh: 我们去峡湾上碰头。

sentences.en: Have tea.
sentences.zh: 喝杯茶。

sentences.en: Find a solution.” “Who will stop you from going too far?” the memory of Anna’s voice reminded Elsa.
sentences.zh: 找个解决办法。""谁会拦住你、不让你走太远？"安娜声音的记忆提醒着艾莎。

sentences.en: Elsa looked back up the path to the magical light of the chamber of memories, debating whether she should return or move forward.
sentences.zh: 艾莎回头望向通道上方、记忆之厅的魔法之光，权衡着该返回还是继续前行。

sentences.en: She heard voices coming from it. “No one really knows what happened that day,” someone said.
sentences.zh: 她听见里面有说话声。"没人真正知道那天发生了什么。"有人说。

sentences.en: It was when she’d first met the Northuldra.
sentences.zh: 那是她初次遇见北地人的时候。

sentences.en: Then her father: “For Arendelle’s sake.” More voices. “You’re trapped here, too!” Yelana shouted. “We’ve never even seen the real sky,” Ryder complained. “A wrong demands resolution,” said Pabbie. “Without it…I see no future.” Elsa decided that moving forward was the only choice there ever was.
sentences.zh: 接着是父亲："为了阿伦黛尔。"更多声音。"你也被困在这里了！"叶拉娜喊。"我们连真正的天空都没见过。"莱德抱怨。"冤屈须得昭雪。"皮比说，"否则……我看不见未来。"艾莎认定，向前走是唯一的选择。

sentences.en: She let her body fall through the darkness until she landed in a forest made of ice.
sentences.zh: 她任由身体坠入黑暗，落在一片冰做的森林里。

sentences.en: It felt empty and uninviting.
sentences.zh: 那里空荡荡的，毫无生气。

sentences.en: It was so cold that Elsa shivered for the first time in her life.
sentences.zh: 冷得艾莎生平第一次打了寒颤。

sentences.en: The cold had never bothered her before.
sentences.zh: 从前，寒冷从未困扰过她。

sentences.en: She spotted her grandfather walking determinedly through the forest.
sentences.zh: 她望见祖父坚决地穿过森林。

sentences.en: She started to follow him and noticed Northuldra festivities in a nearby clearing.
sentences.zh: 她开始跟上去，注意到附近空地上有北地人的庆典。

sentences.en: She moved quickly, searching for her purpose there, the ground freezing around her feet with each step.
sentences.zh: 她快步移动，寻找自己此行的目的，每走一步，脚下的地面便冻结起来。

sentences.en: Up ahead, she saw the Northuldra leader sitting on the edge of a rock.
sentences.zh: 前方，她看见北地人首领坐在岩石边缘。

sentences.en: Elsa was caught by surprise when a snowy image of her grandfather passed through her, heading for the Northuldra leader with a drawn sword in hand.
sentences.zh: 一个祖父的雪影从艾莎身上穿过、手持出鞘的剑朝北地人首领走去，让她惊愕不已。

sentences.en: Elsa was horrified by what he was about to do.
sentences.zh: 他即将做的事，令艾莎毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: She reached out to stop him. “No!” she shouted.
sentences.zh: 她伸手去拦他。"不！"她喊。

sentences.en: She was devastated to see what had really happened in the past, and she wanted to change it more than anything.
sentences.zh: 目睹过去真正发生的事，她心如刀绞，比什么都更想改变它。

sentences.en: But she couldn’t.
sentences.zh: 可她无能为力。

sentences.en: Ice crept up her body, slowly covering it.
sentences.zh: 冰爬上她的身体，缓缓将她覆盖。

sentences.en: She panicked and focused on breathing.
sentences.zh: 她慌了，努力专注呼吸。

sentences.en: She tried to use her powers to force the ice off her, but it didn’t work.
sentences.zh: 她试图用魔力逼退身上的冰，却无济于事。

sentences.en: The ice crept up her neck and toward her face.
sentences.zh: 冰爬上她的脖颈，逼近脸庞。

sentences.en: At that point, she knew she had gone too far, just like her mother’s lullaby had warned, and there was no way to return.
sentences.zh: 那一刻她明白，自己走得太远了，正如母亲摇篮曲所警示，已无路可返。

sentences.en: She gathered all her magic to release in a last-minute signal to Anna.
sentences.zh: 她汇聚全部魔力，要在最后一刻向安娜发出信号。

sentences.en: Only one stream of magic escaped, slicing through the air. “Anna…,” she called out desperately.
sentences.zh: 只逃出一道魔流，破空而去。"安娜……"她绝望地呼唤。

sentences.en: A second later, she was completely encased in ice.
sentences.zh: 一秒之后，她被彻底封进了冰里。

chapters.title: 第37章
chapters.en:
“Which lucky tunnel do we choose?” Olaf asked as he and Anna reached a fork in their path back in the Lost Caverns.

A gust of wind swept across Anna’s face, forcing her to close her eyes. It was even strong enough to make Olaf stumble backward.

“Whoa…,” Olaf said.

They turned their faces into the wind and witnessed a stream of magic and snow floating on it. Then an ice sculpture formed in front of them.

Olaf stared at it in concern, confused by what it meant. Anna slowly walked around it, examining every detail.

“Elsa’s found it,” she said.

“What is it?” Olaf asked.

“The truth about the past,” Anna answered. It was a sculpture of a man standing with his sword raised over another man, who was sitting. His back was turned to the standing man. The sitting man seemed unaware of the danger as he raised a cup to his lips.

Anna realized who the men were. “That’s my grandfather, attacking the Northuldra leader, who wields no weapon.” She knew it had to be true—all the ice sculptures they’d encountered had revealed what had really happened in the past. “The dam wasn’t a gift of peace. It was a trick.”

“That goes against everything Arendelle stands for,” Olaf said in shock.

“It does, doesn’t it?” Anna agreed. She hung her head as the gravity of the situation took hold. “I know how to free the forest. I know what we have to do to set things right.”

“Why do you say that so sadly?” Olaf asked. He thought it was the most exciting he’d heard all year.

Anna slumped on a rock and put her head in her hands. She always did what was best for her people. She’d never thought things would come to this.

“We have to break the dam,” she said.

Olaf thought that was the worst idea he’d heard all year. He thought maybe Anna had been in the caves too long.

“But Arendelle will be flooded!” he said.

Anna had already thought about that, and hated that there was no other way. “That’s why everyone was forced out. To protect them from what must be done.” They hadn’t been forced out of Arendelle because the spirits hated them. They had been forced out so that they could live.

“Oh…. Are you okay?” Olaf asked.

Anna wasn’t sure that “okay” was the right word. She felt sick to her stomach. “I could really use a bright side, Olaf.”

“Um?” He found something that was sure to cheer her up. “Turtles can breathe through their butts. And…I see a way out.”

Anna smiled. “I knew I could count on you.”

Olaf smiled, too. But as Anna turned away from him, he stumbled backward and put a hand to his forehead.

“Come on, Olaf,” she said, not noticing he was in distress. “Elsa’s probably on her way back right now. We can meet her, and—” Then she saw snow beginning to flurry off her friend and float into the air. Something was very wrong. “Olaf…?”

He looked at the snow flying off his body. “What’s this…?” Olaf asked.

“Are you okay?” Anna asked, having no idea what to do to help him. She had a very bad feeling.

Olaf didn’t understand why his body was literally floating away piece by piece. “I’m flurrying?” he said. Then larger clumps of snow blew off his body and sailed into the sky. “Wait. That’s— That’s not it. The magic in me is fading away. I don’t think Elsa’s okay….” He watched more of his body break apart. “Anna, I think she may have gone too far.”

Anna’s eyes widened in alarm. “What? No…no.”

Olaf looked down at his little body, changing with every bit of it that drifted away. He wasn’t sure what it meant, but knew one thing: “Anna…I’m scared.”

Anna was struck by the fear on his face as she began to understand what was going on. If something had happened to Elsa, if Elsa didn’t exist anymore, then Olaf couldn’t exist. Anna fell to her knees before him, suddenly terrified but trying not to show it.

“No, no, no,” she said. “It’s okay. It’s okay.” She pulled Olaf into her arms, holding back tears. “You don’t have to be scared. I’m right here.”

“Oh, that’s good,” Olaf said as she held him close. “Remember when you promised not to leave me?” He looked up at her face sadly. “I’m so sorry I forgot to promise not to leave you. You’re gonna have to do this next part on your own.”

Anna swallowed hard as a single tear slid down her cheek. “You’re not leaving me, Olaf…. Not ever…”

“Hey, Anna,” he said weakly, limp in her arms. “I just thought of one thing that’s permanent.”

“What’s that?” she asked.

“Love.”

Anna touched her heart. “Warm hugs.” She pulled him close and held on tight.

“I like warm hugs,” Olaf said, returning her embrace.

Anna choked on a sob, not wanting to accept what was happening to her friend as snow flurries filled the air. “I love you.”

Kristoff and Sven approached the ice sculpture of young Iduna saving young Agnarr in the ice garden that Elsa had created after their interaction with the Wind Spirit. As Kristoff watched, all of Elsa’s icy imagery flaked away. He held on to Sven, worried about what it meant for Elsa and Anna.

Outside the forest, Elsa’s ice palace began to melt. Warm water dripped from the dome ceiling and down the walls into the main room downstairs. The stairs and pillars crumbled into chunks of crushed ice. The magnificent ice chandelier that lit up the whole ground floor fell with a resounding crash. Then the second floor collapsed onto the first floor in a watery splash.

Grand Pabbie stood on the cliff overlooking Arendelle Castle and the village. The townspeople had set up camp behind him, waiting for Elsa and Anna to return with answers. He watched as the icy castle broke apart and floated into the sky. He took a deep breath and hung his head, understanding and fearing what it meant for Elsa. He looked over his shoulder, knowing he needed to tell the villagers the truth about their queen, but he wasn’t sure where to begin.
